And before anything else we say that it cannot be denied that the creations of the account of Creation were in six days, as in "and there was evening and there was morning, one day," "a second day," etc.; which shows that, although there were ten utterances, they were all nevertheless included in the six days. Now let us consider: if it is true that "In the beginning" is an utterance, whether in Chokhmah or in Keter, how can what is said there be right — "and the earth was formlessness and void [tohu va-vohu], and darkness," etc.? Would it be good in the eyes of YHVH for us to say that, when Malkhut was in Chokhmah or in Keter, the husks [kelipot] surrounded her there, namely formlessness, void and darkness? This is certainly very forced; for who put a husk up above? So the matter must certainly be this: that the Torah made known to us, before anything else, the existence of the Emanation, in the order of its emanation, in general. And this is the meaning of the verse "In the beginning": the concealed Keter, with the "beginning" [reshit], which is Chokhmah, "created" — that is, emanated — "Elohim," which is Binah; "et the heavens": these are Chesed and Tiferet. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained: that the word et comes to include Chesed, and "the heavens" is Tiferet; "and et the earth" is Gevurah, by the inclusion of et, and "the earth" is Malkhut. And Netzach, Hod and Yesod are included in Gedulah, Gevurah and Tiferet. And then it said "and the earth was formlessness and void," etc., which is to tell us of the existence of Malkhut and her chariots, good and evil. And after that it told us of the actions of these Sefirot in Malkhut. And because the first three are concealed and have no revealed action, their action and their utterance were drawn forth through the three Patriarchs, who are the three craftsmen: Chesed, Gevurah and Tiferet. Therefore "Let there be light" is the first utterance, and it is drawn from Keter, through Gedulah, to the palanquin. [And the second utterance, "Let there be a firmament," is drawn from Chokhmah, through Gevurah, to the palanquin; and therefore, etc. See Asis Rimonim and the Pelach.] And that is why the matter of the firmament that divides between waters and waters is found at times alluded to in Chokhmah, in the secret of the upper waters and the lower waters with the firmament in the middle, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Values of the Allusions, with God's help. And the third utterance, "Let the waters be gathered," is from Binah, through Tiferet. And this is the general sense of the passage of the Tikkunim. And now we say that the fourth utterance, which is on the third day, namely the utterance "Let the earth sprout," is drawn from Chesed through Tiferet, the third day. And the utterance "Let there be luminaries" is drawn from Gevurah — as is known, "luminaries" is written defectively [me'orot without the letter vav], which is from the side of Gevurah — and it was done through Netzach, the fourth day. And the utterance "Let the waters swarm" is drawn from Tiferet through Netzach, in Hod. And this is alluded to in the passage from Terumah that we copied above, which said, "the fourth arrangement: the light of the sun flowed," which is the mode of existence of Tiferet. And the reason is this: because Tiferet is composed of right and left, it received three utterances — from Chesed, from Gevurah, and one of its own. And because it inclines toward Chesed, it effected one utterance, that of Chesed: this is the utterance "Let the earth sprout," which is the second of the third day and the fourth of the utterances, and belongs to Chesed. And it handed over to Netzach the two [other] utterances, namely the fifth, which is Gevurah's, and the sixth, its own. Netzach effected the fifth, Gevurah's, and handed over to Hod the sixth, Tiferet's. And because judgment is complete only together with mercy, the light of the sun did not shine through Netzach, and the action of Netzach was not complete, until the fifth day came, which is Hod, on which the sixth utterance was done, which is the utterance of Tiferet. And this is what it said in the passage from Terumah, "the fifth arrangement … and it performed its service, to bring forth the light of the arrangement of the fourth day," etc. And Yesod, which is the sixth day, because it includes Netzach and Hod, brought forth three utterances, corresponding to Netzach, Hod and Yesod: the utterance "Let the earth bring forth" corresponding to Netzach, the utterance "Let us make man" corresponding to Hod, and the utterance "Behold, I have given" corresponding to Yesod. For the saying "Be fruitful and multiply" is not an utterance but only a blessing. For if you do not say so, there would be a full ten utterances, and how could he say "those are nine"? Rather, on this view, certainly nothing is called an utterance except an utterance of creation, and this one is an utterance of blessing. And because fruitfulness and increase belong to Yesod, this blessing was given on the sixth [day], which is Yesod. And with this the Sabbath day, which is Malkhut, was sanctified, and she was completed and "the city was built on its mound." And once she was complete she spoke her own utterance, which is "It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him," etc.; for through the coupling the blessing would flow, as is evident in many places in the Zohar. So it now turns out that, for the utterances themselves — which are what acts — to allude to the ten Sefirot, the utterances are only nine. For the utterance "It is not good" is not actually [the utterance of] Malkhut, but the actions of Malkhut; and the utterance of Malkhut is the one that was decreed from the mouth of Yesod, for Yesod emanated Malkhut. And because, in the passage of the Talmud in Rosh Hashanah with which we were dealing, the intent was that the ten Kingships are actually the ten utterances, he raised the difficulty and said "those are nine." For the utterance "Let there be light" is Chokhmah, as is explained in many places in the Zohar, and it comes out by the power of Keter. And what is meant is not Chokhmah proper; rather, of the utterances drawn to Malkhut, that which was drawn from Keter was the mode of existence of Chokhmah, and that which was drawn from Chokhmah was the mode of existence of Binah. That is why he objected "those are nine": for the utterance drawn from Malkhut, which is "It is not good that the man should be alone," is not Malkhut but what is drawn from Malkhut; and so the allusion of the utterances to the Sefirot themselves is only nine. And to this he answered, "'In the beginning' is also an utterance": for although it is the existence of the Emanation, the matter was together with Keter, and it is impossible that Keter not be included there, as we explained. And now what is found in the Zohar, Parashat Bereshit, and in the Tikkunim will be seen to be right: that this utterance alludes at times to Keter, at times to Chokhmah, at times to Binah, at times to Malkhut (which is also called "beginning" [reshit]), and at times to Da'at; for it is an utterance that includes the existence of the whole Emanation in general, as we explained. And with this we have discharged our obligation in this matter for the present, so that the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, should not conflict with one another, and should not conflict, God forbid, with what is explained in the Gemara in these passages, so as not to give an opening to those who speak falsehood. And each one shall come to his place in peace, and rest upon his couch.

And now, having cleared the stumbling-stones from the vineyard of this passage in the preceding chapters, we shall examine it closely a little, and afterward explain its meaning briefly, with the help of God. What should be examined is this. First, the order of the sages: it put Rav Yosef before Rabbi Yochanan, although Rabbi Yochanan preceded him by a long time. Second: since the Commandments, the utterances and the praises all allude to the ten Sefirot, what are they disagreeing about? Third: its saying "the ten praises that David spoke in the book of Psalms" is needless length, for certainly David spoke praises nowhere but in the book of Psalms; so much so that this very length almost made room for the error by which he was challenged, "But there are many praises!" — for the questioner understood, from the words "in the book of Psalms," that the whole book was meant. Fourth: its saying "the Ten Commandments that were spoken to Moses at Sinai": why did it go on at such length? Are there any others? And what further needs examining in its wording will become clear as we proceed, with the help of God. Now this passage is to be understood with what we already have from the Tikkunim, where Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that the Kingships are in Malkhut, the Remembrances in Tiferet and the Shofarot in Binah. And even if the later commentators have other explanations of this, they all agree that the Kingships are in Malkhut. And the one who asked already took it as given that the ten Kingships are certainly in the ten Sefirot. But he was in doubt whether they are the ten Sefirot included in Malkhut itself, in the way that each one is composed of ten, as we shall explain in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter two, with the help of God; or whether they are the ten Sefirot proper, but in their mode of existence as they pour their effluence into Malkhut; or whether we should say that they are the Sefirot actually in their own place. And should you say that they are called "Kingships" and so must be in Malkhut, since their name testifies to them: we would answer that they would be ten Kingships in the sense of the Malkhut within each and every Sefirah, in its own place. And along these lines we shall explain the Remembrances and the Shofarot, as explained. And this is what it means by "These ten Kingships — to what do they correspond?": since they are ten, I know that their number testifies that they correspond to the ten Sefirot; but the question is, in which aspect of them, of the three aspects we have mentioned? And on this the three sages were divided, one saying this and another that. Rabbi answered that they correspond to the ten praises that David spoke in the book of Psalms. And by the length of his wording, "that David spoke," he had in mind what our Sages, of blessed memory, have already explained: that all that David said in the book of Psalms he said only in correspondence to Malkhut, which was his attribute.

Thus he had in mind the first aspect, which is the ten Sefirot included in Malkhut, as we explained. But the questioner did not grasp the fine point of the phrasing in his saying "in the book of Psalms," and took it as meant to indicate a place; and so he objected, "But there are many!" And he was answered that only those in which the shofar is mentioned were meant; and these are at the end of the book. "Praise El in His sanctuary" is Keter. "Praise Him in the firmament of His strength" is Chokhmah. "Praise Him for His mighty acts" is Binah. "Praise Him according to the abundance of His greatness" is Gedulah. "Praise Him with the blast of the shofar" is Gevurah. "Praise Him with harp and lyre" is Tiferet. "Praise Him with timbrel and dance" is Netzach. "Praise Him with strings and pipe" is Hod. "Praise Him with sounding cymbals" is Yesod. "Praise Him with clashing cymbals" is Malkhut. And all of these are in Malkhut, as is evident from their being in the book of Psalms, which corresponds to Malkhut. And Rav Yosef had in mind the second aspect, namely that what is meant by the ten Kingships is that all the Sefirot pour their effluence into Malkhut; and this is what he meant in saying "to the Ten Commandments," etc. For it has been explained that at the giving of the Torah each and every attribute poured one of the Commandments into the Sefirah of Malkhut, and Malkhut revealed that Commandment and showed it to Israel. And this is the meaning of (Exodus 20:15) "And all the people saw the voices": they saw the voices coming to Malkhut, so that Malkhut might speak the Commandment by the power of each and every Sefirah. And this is what Rashbi, peace be upon him, meant in the book of the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 10), and these are his words: "And on the seventh day the Torah was given: this is the Righteous One, the foundation of the world; and at his grade Malkhut spoke with them. And they have established it: [as] with ten kings, lest they be unable to speak with one mouth, He touched the house [bayit] and included in her all ten." Thus far [his] words.

The meaning is clear without our examining his wording closely now, so as not to go on at length. And further, [it is clear] that He spoke from the side of Malkhut, for she was the one speaking, by the power of each and every Sefirah that pours its effluence upon her. And this is what Rav Yosef meant in saying "the Ten Commandments that were spoken to Moses at Sinai": he meant that they were spoken to him by means of "Sinai," which is Malkhut, as explained. Nor is it surprising that they are ten apart from Malkhut; for Malkhut has an aspect [in which she is counted] with the ten, and an aspect in which she receives from the ten, in that she receives from herself — in the secret of the modes of existence yod and heh within her, as will be explained in the Gate of the Modes of Existence. And with this the wording of Rashbi, peace be upon him, becomes exact, when he said "He touched the house [bayit]": for the mode of existence bet in Malkhut is the mode of existence heh, and these are lower grades in her relative to the aspect of the yod, as will be explained in the Gate mentioned. And that is why he said "and included in her all ten": for even Malkhut must be included with her.

So Rav Yosef had in mind the second aspect, which is the ten Sefirot pouring their effluence into Malkhut. And Rabbi Yochanan had in mind the third aspect, which is the aspect of the Sefirot proper, in their own place. And this is what he meant in saying "by ten utterances the world was created": these are the Sefirot themselves, in their own place. And what is intended with regard to Malkhut is that, when we are at the Kingships, we should direct our intention to the ten Sefirot in their own place, or to the Malkhut within each and every Sefirah, as we explained above.

The matter of "those are nine" has been explained above. And he answered, "'In the beginning' is also an utterance": for although it speaks of the existence of the Emanation, it nevertheless has the existence of an utterance. And the proof of this is "By the word of YHVH the heavens were made": meaning that the existence of the emanation of "the heavens," which are Tiferet — their emanation is from Keter, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, with the help of God.
And it said "by the word" [bi-devar], the language of utterance, to teach that the existence of the Emanation is referred to as utterance.

Thus from this passage it appears explicitly that the ten Commandments, the ten utterances and the ten praises, by their existence, are faithful witnesses in our holy Torah to the existence of ten Sefirot, without any hesitation whatsoever — apart from what we wrote in the preceding Gate, in chapter one, with God's help. And no question at all remains on this for our tradition, to say that perhaps they are twenty or five.

Having shown in the preceding chapter that there is no room to demand a proof for our tradition, since we have a decisive proof, as explained, we now say that there is likewise no room to ask the Emanator for a reason why He emanated ten, and not twenty or five or the like. (Nor, indeed, does the question arise, for there is a refutation of its very premise.) What we ought to investigate is this whole Emanation: why was it emanated? And with our answer to this, everything will be settled. And it is this. The intent of the Emanator, King of kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, was to bring within limit things that are not within limit. That is: the Emanator is not finite, and the Emanator's intent in creating this lowly world was that the world should be finite, perishing and passing away. And for this reason the Emanation was necessary: so that, through the emanated being emanated and the grades chaining down, grade after grade — emanated from Emanator, created from emanated, formed from created, made from formed — the grades would at length reach the passing-away and destruction in which they stand. For there is a created thing that "came to be in a night and perished in a night," and there is one that, "if it stand a day or two," will not endure. And now, how shall the clay say to its Maker, "Why thus and not thus?" He saw in His wisdom that finitude — the coming-to-be and passing-away of created beings — could not be reached unless the number of the emanated were ten. For if they were fewer than ten, created beings would not descend to that grade of descent, because of their nearness to the source. But now that all that was possible in the Emanation has been emanated, it follows of necessity that the grades that chain down from them descend to finitude, because they are as far removed from the root as is needed to arrive at finitude. And we do not mean to say that the Emanation is limited or finite, God forbid. We mean that the actions that proceed from them effect a finite work, like the work of this world, which comes to be and passes away and has limit and measure, being wrought by the agents through the beings created from the emanated. And the need for finitude and limit in the lower beings was explained by our Sages, of blessed memory, in the Mishnah, when they said, "By ten utterances the world was created. And what does this teach? Could it not have been created by one utterance?" That is: it was not impossible, God forbid, for this world to be created by a single utterance that would include all the things and grades and creations and beings that have now come to be. For although some actions are through Chesed and some through Gevurah, and so with all of them, the power to create by a single utterance alone would not be lacking on that account; for the power of all of them is in each one of them, as is known — each being composed of ten, as we shall explain in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter two, with God's help. And the reason ten utterances were needed is "to exact payment": meaning that through ten utterances created beings descended to finitude. For had they not been finite, a person would live forever and would not receive punishment for his iniquities, and the side of impurity and the husk would spread through the world, and the damage would not be rectified. So too the righteous would be sunk in this world and would not see the good. Therefore the world had to be finite and limited, in order to exact payment from the wicked and to give a good reward to the righteous. And the meaning of "who destroy the world that was created," etc., is that they destroy the world, and have the power to bring it to an end, because it is finite and was created by ten utterances. And so too the righteous sustain it; for were it not finite, the righteous would not sustain it nor the wicked destroy it. For this reason it had to be created by ten utterances — that is, the emanation of ten grades — so that it should be finite: the wicked man perishes and passes away and returns to his dust and is rectified, and the righteous man departs in honor to greet the face of his Father in heaven and to eat the fruit of his deeds. Yet there is a difficulty with this reason. If the cause of the Emanation was to bring the lower beings to passing-away and destruction, so as to reward those who do righteousness at all times and to punish the wicked, as explained, then after the resurrection — which is not a time of reward and punishment, nor a time of deeds, as is known — what reason is there for the Emanation? For wickedness will already have ceased from the earth, and it is the time of permanence. Shall we say that the purpose of the Emanation lasts only until the time of the resurrection? God forbid: certainly not. For the principal state of the world and its perfection are then, as is known; and then, certainly, will be the perfection of the Emanation and its shining. And the same difficulty arises with the holy palaces, in which a person is judged according to his deeds, to be rewarded or punished, as will be explained in the Gate of the Holy Palaces, with God's help. If so, in the time of the resurrection, when there is no rewarding or punishing or judging or bringing of charges against human beings, what will become of the palaces? Shall we say that they will be for nothing, and that each and every one will cease from the work that they were doing? Yet this is no question; for it is possible that they will be united, each with the next, one within another, "each one cleaving to his brother"; and in the time of their oneness and union there is no judgment in them, and the sparks are swallowed up in their sources, and they take their pleasure in abundant peace, as is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Pekudei, on the palaces. And for this reason too it cannot be said that the purpose of the Emanation is to reward and to punish, to judge and to bring charges against the guilty and the innocent. For then we would ask: after the resurrection, when human beings are no longer judged according to their deeds but enjoy what they toiled for on the eve of the Sabbath [that is, in this world], it would turn out, God forbid, that they [the emanated] exist for nothing. Therefore we say that this was not the principal purpose of their emanation, even though reward and punishment do proceed from them under the supernal providence, as we shall explain in the Gate of Essence and Governance and in the Gate of Self and Vessels. Rather, the principal intent was to make His divinity known to what is other than Himself, as we shall explain in the second reason in this chapter, and we shall add further explanation in chapter seven, with the help of God. And so it turns out, on the contrary, that as long as the world is in ruin from the filth of the serpent and the husk, the emanated are not united as they should be, and His divinity is not revealed, and knowledge among the people of the children of Israel has come to an end and is finished — until He has mercy from heaven and the world emerges from the filth of the serpent and is rectified as it should be. Then the world will return to its rectification, and His divinity will be revealed among those below, rightly and properly, and human beings will grow stronger in knowledge of Him. And then it is said (Jeremiah 31), "And they shall no longer teach, each man his neighbor," etc., "for they shall all know Me, from the least of them to the greatest of them." And then the light of the Torah, its hidden things and its secrets, will be revealed, rightly and properly, and the emanated will be united in complete union; for the verse will be fulfilled that is written (Zechariah 14), "And YHVH shall be King over all the earth; on that day YHVH shall be one and His Name one." And from the Mishnah of the ten utterances nothing can be inferred [against this], for it may be explained thus: "By ten utterances the world was created" means that all ten Sefirot acted in the creation of the world, although it could have been created by the power of one, namely Keter, which is called "one utterance," as explained in the Zohar; "but rather in order to," etc. — that is, so that they could effect actions in different aspects, whether of judgment or of mercy; for Keter has no judgment in it, only simple mercy, as is known. And this Mishnah does not mean that the emanation of the emanated was for the sake of the world, God forbid; it is a reason for their action below, in the lower world, although the first Sefirah has the power to effect everything. There is also another reason, close to the preceding one. The Emanator, King of kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He — it is His attribute to pour effluence upon what is other than Himself, and that His good effluence should do good to created beings and pour upon them from His attributes: lovingkindness, for example, through the attribute of Chesed, and so with all the Sefirot. And He saw fit to emanate this Emanation and to reveal His greatness to the eyes of created beings, so that He might be recognized by His creatures and apprehended a little, through His holy and pure Emanation. And it belongs to the attributes of His goodness that His will is to reveal His exaltedness to the lowly. And because, when His exaltedness is revealed to created beings in Keter, created beings still have no power to apprehend Him, so exalted is that emanated one, He had to emanate Chokhmah, and so from Chokhmah to Binah, down to Malkhut, for there the exaltedness of the King is apprehended. And the parable for this is a ray of the sun entering a house through an aperture, to light the inner side of the house. Because it is so bright, no one in the house can bear it, and their eyes grow dim from looking at the sun, for it is great and dazzles exceedingly; so that they have had to make there a very large lantern, for the light to shine through to its far side, so that those standing in the house receive the benefit of the light and not its harm. And because the light of the sun is so bright in its strength and might, even though the light has been sweetened a little and hidden and concealed a little, those standing in the house, their sight being weak, still need a second screen, and after the second a third, up to ten. And now, when a man comes into the house to enjoy the light that shines through the lantern, and asks why the number of these lanterns is thus and so and not otherwise, we shall blunt his teeth and tell him that it is out of great foolishness that he asks about this. For since the purpose of the screens is to set the light right, so that it is sweetened to the eyes of those who see, then if the screens were fewer, the eyes of those who see would be darkened by the abundance of its light, and it would do harm; and if they were more, the light would be darkened further, and the sweetness of its light would not reach those who see, and "those who look through the apertures would be darkened." And that is not what is intended. What is intended is to set the light right, so that they may enjoy it as bright as it can be, but not in a mode of existence in which it harms by excess of brightness: rather a bright light, a sweet light, a fragrant light. And a compelling proof for this reason is found in a passage of the Zohar that we shall copy in the Gate of Self and Vessels, with the help of God: it is the passage "To whom then will you liken Me, that I should be equal?" etc. And there we showed, from the explicit words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, that the principal purpose of the Emanation is "so that they might know Him," etc.: for through the Sefirot His greatness is revealed to us. And it is not as we have seen with the investigators, men of darkness and confusion: for because they remove the predicates, the providence of the divinity is hidden from their eyes, and they thought that they had apprehended Him while their heart was far from Him. For they err about the truth of the Ein Sof, blessed be He [holding that because of His great greatness and exaltedness He does not watch over those below], and so they deny His providence and most of His dealings and actions in this world. "Not like these is the portion of Jacob, for He is the former of all." And the matter of His predicates — His sitting and His rising and His walking and His speaking and everything of the kind — is understood by those who know this wisdom, and will be explained at length in the coming Gates, with the help of God.

Now that God has granted us, in the preceding chapters, to set out a seemly and acceptable account of the reason for the Emanation and to ground it in the words of our Sages, of blessed memory, we wish in this chapter to treat the matter at greater length and breadth, with the help of God, in such a way that the eyes of the inquirer are enlightened on this matter. And before we come to explain it we shall ask one question, over which some of the investigators of this wisdom have been perplexed: namely, whether the Ein Sof, King of kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, has the ability to emanate ten Sefirot other than these, or not, God forbid.

Now it is fitting that we investigate: if He is able — since it is the attribute of His goodness to pour effluence upon what is other than Himself — why did He not emanate even a thousand thousand thousands, since this lies within the possibility of His ability, and emanate ten Sefirot many times over, and many worlds, in the way that He brought this world into existence? At first sight this question would startle the eyes of the discerning and leave him astounded. But the truth is that this question is a question of great foolishness, and it is out of great folly that the questioner asked it. And the reason is this: we say to the one who asks this question that his question cannot escape three alternatives. Either he is asking that the second Sefirot be equal to the true, emanated Sefirot: that is, a Keter equal to Keter, a Chokhmah equal to Chokhmah, a Binah equal to Binah, and so with all of them. Or that they be greater than these, that is, finer than these. Or that they be lesser than these and [more] revealed. Now none of these three aspects is possible. For the Sefirot are fine with the utmost fineness — that is, spiritual with the utmost spirituality — free of body and of the corporeal and its accidents, as we have explained and as we shall explain in the Gate of Gates. And since it is true that they are not bodies, they cannot be distinct from the Emanator, and come under the count of ten, except by way of cause and effect: that is, the Emanator is cause to the emanated, and there you have a difference between Him and those He emanated — besides other differences which we have no business explaining now.

Now Keter is distinct from Chokhmah in that Chokhmah is the effect of Keter and Keter is the cause of Chokhmah; and this is how they are distinct from one another down to the lowest grade. For apart from this they have no distinction by which to come under the number ten, since what is not a body is not divided into parts, as we shall explain at length in the Gate of the Order of Their Standing, with God's help. So when the questioner says that there should be ten other Sefirot equal to these, we answer him that it is impossible. For if a Keter is equal to Keter, there cannot be two Keters: by what would they be distinct, so as to be two? Hence from the one, unique Emanator only one emanated being can be emanated. Two is impossible, because there is nothing to distinguish them: both are effects of the First Cause. Otherwise they are not spiritual; and if they are spiritual, they cannot be two. It is therefore necessary that only one emanated being be emanated from the Emanator. And in the same way we answer about a Chokhmah beside Chokhmah, and so for all the Sefirot, until we prove conclusively that there can be no ten Sefirot but these. And let it not be asked: "If so, God forbid, the Emanator has no power to emanate two equal Keters as His effects, which would be distinct from one another although equal." This is foolishness. For this is not due to any lack or weakness of ability, God forbid, either in the Emanator or in the emanated. On the contrary, it is to their praise. For in order to be distinct they would have to descend to the lowliness of body, which is divided into parts, and that is not fitting. For the greatness of the master is known from the greatness of the servant, and it belongs to his perfection to make what is other than himself perfect. Nor should it be asked: "On the contrary, we would [then] know and recognize His superiority — that He, who is without body, should make it corporeal, and that from being simple and incorporeal, as is known, He should bring body and corporeality into existence. So let Him emanate two Keters, and let them be corporeal." To this we answer you that He has indeed created many of this kind, namely the angels, which in truth are corporeal, although their corporeality is fine, like the corporeality of fire and finer still, as is explained in the Gate of the Palaces. Nor should it be asked that He stamp into the spiritual the nature that, although it is fine and spiritual, it should be divided into parts. For that would be a lessening of the spiritual, whose principal perfection lies in its oneness and its being undivided. And the parable for this: a questioner would not ask, "Does a king have the power to be a servant? And since he does not have the servant's ability, the servant turns out to be more praiseworthy than he." On the contrary: he certainly does; but if he did so, it would be a debasement and a lessening of the crown of kingship, and the honor of a king is to keep himself far from every kind of servants' service. So it is with the Emanator and the emanated: it is to the Emanator's praise to stamp into the emanated the power of His seal, that they be simple, not composite, and far from corporeality and from all its accidents.

Thus we have proved that it is impossible for them to be equal. And now we say that to ask that they be greater than these is likewise no right question, and there is no truth in his words. For there is no difference between the Emanator and the emanated except the difference between cause and effect; and as near to the Emanator as it is possible for an emanated being to be, so near has Keter been brought — to the point that there is no room left to say that there could be an emanated being between Keter and the Emanator: there is only the fact that the one is cause and the other effect. And this is what necessitates its descent from the rank of the Emanator — a descent that is nonetheless great without end, for it is dark before its Emanator, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim. And there is no room to ask why the Ein Sof did not emanate Keter exactly equal to Himself, since power is not lacking. For the truth is that the emanated cannot be equal to the Emanator; and this is not because of any lack in the Emanator, but because of the nature of the emanated. For once it is emanated, it is the effect of its cause, and its cause is above it, with a certain priority in several respects, since no effect can attain to its cause. It therefore follows of necessity, from its being emanated and an effect, that it descends from before its Master by the difference that lies between cause and effect. And what causes it this lack is that it is emanated and an effect, and the First Cause is prior to it. With this the question whether that [other] Keter could be greater than this Keter is also removed, since this Keter is the greatest that is possible under the law of the emanated. And to say that it should be less than this is likewise impossible; for there already is something less than it, which is Chokhmah, and whatever would rise above Chokhmah is Keter. That is: since Chokhmah is the effect of Keter, and descends from Keter only by what lies between cause and effect, one cannot ask for another emanated being between Chokhmah and Keter. For this emanated being cannot be equal to Keter, nor equal to Chokhmah, for the reason we have explained; and between Keter and Chokhmah it is impossible, because Keter and Chokhmah are cause and effect, and there is no gap between them that could admit an effect prior to Chokhmah and posterior to Keter — unless Chokhmah were to descend to the place of Binah, that is, the third effect; and then these would simply be Chokhmah and Binah. And with this all the questions are removed altogether.

And now, by what we have raised here, we shall explain the matter of the three aspects in each Sefirah, on which we shall speak at length in the coming Gates, with the help of God. They are these: each and every Sefirah has three aspects — first, its aspect relative to what is emanated from it; second, relative to itself; third, relative to its emanator. And the point is that in Keter itself, since it is emanated from the Emanator, who emanates and is not emanated — of whom it is certainly forbidden to speak at length, and may God forgive us for having spoken of Him at such length until now — [we say no more]. And so, in Chokhmah, which is emanated from Keter, there must be an aspect that is level [mishtaveh, with its emanator] — that is, a nearness that is united with its emanator, which is Keter, such that there is no distinction between them at all. After that it descends within itself and becomes distinct, from itself to itself, until it comes to be the cause of Binah, which is its effect.

And within it itself there must be the aspect of cause to effect, so that it rises from aspect to aspect, ever higher. And to illustrate this: the aspect that is level with Keter is the cause of the aspect of its own self, and the aspect of its own self is the cause of the one that is level with Binah [and likewise in each and every aspect there will be these same three aspects — from Asis Rimonim]. And between every two aspects three further aspects are necessary: namely, the aspect that makes the first aspect level with Keter, the aspect itself, and the aspect that makes it level with its own self. And let us draw a bodily figure from which the intellect may rise to the spiritual: as though we were to draw a rosh tor [a wedge], that is, this elongated triangle.

Now this triangle slopes downward, and it widens toward its top. It is a parable for the emanated: the nearer they come to their source, the more exalted and the wider they are — not a width of limit and body, but a width of fineness and spirituality.

And when the inquirer looks well, he will find that the top of Keter is wide, and that it slopes and goes on narrowing until its width comes to be level with the width of Chokhmah. And even at the place where Keter and Chokhmah are level there is a great difference; for this is necessitated by that which pours forth [mashpi'a], sloping [meshuppa] downward, whose descent has no resting-place. For the farther it moves from the upper face, the more the emanated is revealed and is caused by its cause, which is above it. And this is "cause and effect," for one who has the eyes of intellect and whom YHVH has graced with knowledge. And this is the secret of "each one is composed of ten," and the secret of the descent of the grades within the very self of the Sefirah. For the Keter-within-Keter is the side that draws near to the Emanator, and the Malkhut-within-Keter is the side that draws near to Chokhmah, and the Keter-within-Chokhmah is the effect of the Malkhut-within-Keter. And all this can be seen from the figure we have drawn. For the narrow part of Keter is the cause of the wide part of Chokhmah; and so the Keter-within-Chokhmah is the side that draws near to Keter, and the Malkhut-within-Chokhmah is the side that draws near to Binah, and the Keter-within-Binah is the effect of the Malkhut-within-Chokhmah. And on this model it must likewise be said that each and every part is itself composed of ten Sefirot, because the light has no resting-place but keeps moving away and descending; and each and every point, each and every part, is the cause of the point below it and the effect of the point above it. And He saw in His wisdom that unless Keter itself descended ten degrees, Chokhmah could not be emanated from it at all. Likewise, had Chokhmah not descended ten degrees, it would not have been possible for Binah to be emanated from it. And so with all the Sefirot, and so with all the parts and the points. And the same rule and the same reason hold for ABYA [Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah]: for in Atzilut there is ABYA, and in Beriah there is ABYA, and in Yetzirah ABYA, and in Asiyah ABYA. For ABYA is the sum of all that is distinct from the First Necessary One, the Ein Sof, King of kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, from Keter down to the central point at the navel of the earth; and they are the kinds of their descent, in four grades. And each one of them, in turn, when we come to divide them, we divide into four grades, and each and every grade into four grades; except that the four of Atzilut are so fine that the Asiyah-within-Atzilut is the cause and origin of the Atzilut-within-Beriah, and likewise the Asiyah-within-Beriah is the cause and origin of the Atzilut-within-Yetzirah, and so in this order with all the grades and all the parts — so that existence turns out to be like a jointed lampstand, [its parts] united and embracing one another, as explained. And having raised this, I wish by means of it to address the question of the number ten that we asked in the preceding chapters. It is known that every effect is encompassed by its cause, and the cause encompasses the effect, as we shall explain at length in the Gate of the Order of Their Standing, with God's help. And now let us draw a bodily figure, namely a circle within a circle, like this:

— so that no gap comes between these spheres. And now, if the questioner should ask why this draftsman did not draw yet more circles inside these circles, surely we shall blunt his teeth and tell him that he "has gathered the wind in his fists." For there can be no further addition to the number of circles, since they descend one from another by [no more than] a point, and there cannot possibly exist another circle within the great circle that encompasses them all within it.

Now from the bodily figure let us raise our intellect to the spiritual matter that we are explaining. It is known that the Sefirot descend one from another by the difference that lies between cause and effect; and therefore they are one within another, the effect encompassed by the cause, like these circles, where the larger encompasses the one smaller than it, which is the effect. Thus Keter encompasses Chokhmah and is its cause, and Chokhmah descends from Keter by the measure of what lies between cause and effect; and Chokhmah is the cause of Binah, so that Binah descends one grade from Chokhmah and two grades from Keter, being the effect of that [Chokhmah] which is the effect of it [Keter]. And in this way the grades descend down to Malkhut.

And Malkhut is the end of Atzilut and the beginning of Beriah, and it is to Beriah as the Ein Sof is to Atzilut; and the last grade in Beriah is to Yetzirah as Malkhut is to Beriah. And this is their order, until they come to the spheres by way of degrees that are hidden and concealed from us, and revealed to those versed in the account of Creation and the account of the Chariot.

And there is no difference between Malkhut and Beriah except the difference between cause and effect. And with the descent from the last grade of Atzilut there had necessarily to be the beginning of Beriah, which is the grade that is united with Atzilut as the effect is united with its cause; and so from Beriah to Yetzirah, and so from Yetzirah to Asiyah, down to the spheres.

As for the order of the spheres, the astronomers, dim of sight, imagined that each sphere is adjacent to the next, so that no gap comes between them. But this is not the view of the masters of the Torah, who see by the everlasting light; rather, between one firmament and the next is a journey of five hundred years. And although there is this air between them, the matter nevertheless shows the evenness of the creation and its necessity, and that there could not be less than this between sphere and sphere — until the matter comes down to the element of fire; and the element of fire is united with the element of air, and the element of air is united with the element of water, and the element of water is united with the element of earth, one above the other, with no gap between them. And now, who gives a man a mouth to ask, "Let there be so many grades more, or so many fewer," or "Why did He not create the world larger than this, or smaller?" For all this is great foolishness to those who know the order of the grades. And the constitution of the world is in the most excellent mode of existence possible, in the order of the grades from the highest that can exist to the lowest that can exist, whether in limit, in finitude or in corporeality. And indeed, were the order of the Sefirot not between Him and the world, the world, on account of its lowliness, could not be governed by the Ein Sof — unless the world were to rise to the spiritual grades, which are the Sefirot; and for that He has already emanated the Sefirot. And the intent is nothing other than to reveal the Emanation and the divinity, and not to conceal it. And it is revealed through the descent of the grades to the lowest aspect, where they now are. For even this thick, coarse earth, down to its navel, has grade after grade, to seven earths, as we shall explain something of this in [the Gate of] the Order of Their Standing, with the help of God. This is the reverse of the view of the foolish astronomers, who imagined they could give the measure of the earth and said that a line of twenty-two thousand mil would encircle it round about, and that, were the earth bored through, [the bore] would pass through to its underside through a thickness of seven thousand three hundred and thirty-three and a third mil. And they walk on in darkness.

On this matter we have a received teaching and a weighty precedent, as we shall write in the name of the Zohar in the Gate mentioned. And to return to our subject: had the world been created without intermediaries — apart from the fact that this is impossible, for the reason we have explained —

— this would be a concealment of the divinity. For when we came to know His greatness from His governance, would we not believe that, in truth, He is exalted above His world [only] by what lies between a cause and its cause [that is, by one step of cause and effect]? Therefore, so as not to conceal His divinity, He emanated the grades in the way I have explained. For now, when we look upon Keter, may it be blessed and exalted, and then raise above it its cause, the Ein Sof, King of kings of kings — how greatly is His Name magnified in the eyes of all His creatures!

And so this glorious chapter is complete, and this Gate is concluded. And since YHVH has blessed us thus far, and helped us in all the way that we have gone, we are journeying to the place that we know: namely, to investigate whether the Ein Sof is the Keter, with the help of Heaven.
The Third Gate: To Know Whether the Ein Sof is the Keter:

What is intended in this Gate is to discuss the matter of the perplexity that has fallen among the Kabbalists, [in coming] to know whether the Ein Sof is the Keter itself or other than it. And this is its name, by which they call it: "Whether the Ein Sof is the Keter."
Chapter One:

Many of the Kabbalists among the people of our nation have been perplexed with a great perplexity, and have fallen into the pit of error, and thought that the supernal Keter is the Ein Sof, and that it is in the number of the ten. And [there are] some of them who said that, since we have ten grades, what need is there for a further emanation? — but rather that the matter of the Emanator with the emanated [beings] is [the] ten. And they [thought to] support themselves from the Mishnah of Sefer Yetzirah, which said "ten and not nine, ten and not eleven"; and they said that [its] saying "and not eleven" [means] to say that we should not add further upon ten — but [rather] that the ten are precisely [the count], [including] the Emanator, who is the Ein Sof, the supernal Keter. This is their way — and may their Master forgive them, for this is a matter of cutting [the shoots] and separation; and one who looks at what I explained concerning that Mishnah, in the First Gate, ch.6, will see that, on the contrary, from there [comes] a proof to the opposite.

Now this view is rejected for several reasons. If you wish, [argue] from Scripture; if you wish, [argue] from reason. The [argument from] reason is: that since the Emanator is distinguished from His emanated [beings] in several matters — first, that the emanated [beings] fall under time, and He does not fall under time. And I do not wish to say "time" according to what appears from the plain sense of our words, but the intent is that there was already a time when they were not emanated, as [for instance] before the Emanation. And this is one of the things impossible in the Ein Sof — that there was [ever] an existence in which He did not exist; rather, He is necessary of existence, and He brought time into existence, and not that He is possessed of time, God forbid. And in this matter is understood [the saying] "first, yet there is no beginning to its beginning" — for although we say "first," and every expression "first" indicates that it has a beginning (for it is true that He is first to all that come after Him) — yet the expression "first" indicates the beginning of time. And therefore it said that He is first, and even so there is no beginning to His beginning; and the expression "first" is only to negate that no other preceded Him. And this is what is said in the Tikkunim, "I am first and I am last." And Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that ANI (I) is AYIN (Nothing), which is the supernal Keter. And "I" (ani) is Malkhut, which is the end of the Emanation — "its end embedded in its beginning and its beginning in its end" — for AYIN is alef = supernal Keter, yod = Chokhmah, [final] nun = Binah, with the extension of the vav, which is [the] nun, [i.e.] yod upon vav; and the existence of the [final] nun itself is Malkhut, in truth. It is found [that] AYIN comprehends the whole Emanation. And this [is] "I am first" — the secret of the extension and spreading of the Emanation from above to below; and "I am last" is the existence of the returning light, reversing from below to above. And by this is understood the matter of "first and last": for Keter is truly called "first," because it is first to all that come "in the beginning," which is [the emanated and below]; but above it, in the Ein Sof, the expression "first" does not apply. And this is "and before One, what can you count?" — the meaning [being]: Keter is called "one," which is the beginning of the count, which is the number of the ten, in which the whole count is comprehended, and the count's foundation is above, as we explained in the preceding Gate. And it said that "before One" — which is that [which is] prior to it, namely the Ein Sof — "what can you count?", for there applies there neither number, nor speech, nor any necessity at all. And of Him it is said (Job 37:20), "shall it be counted to Him when I speak?" — for number does not apply there. And with this premise is understood the verse (Isaiah 43) in which all the literalists were perplexed: "You are My witnesses, says YHVH, and My servant whom I have chosen, that you may know and believe Me and understand that I am He: before Me no God was formed, and after Me there shall be none." And the explanation: "that I am He" — namely Keter, for it is Keter that is truly called "He" (Hu); and to indicate its concealment, the word "Hu" [is] a pronoun for the hidden [third person]. And therefore it said that it is also called "I" (Ani), to indicate that it is the beginning of the Emanation and the end of the Emanation, in the secret of "I am first and I am last," as explained. And it said "before Me no God was formed" — and the word "formed" (notzar) [is] according to its plain sense, whose meaning is "was not emanated"; for the expression "formation" (yetzirah) too serves [to denote] the Emanation, just as the expression "creation" (beri'ah) serves, namely "In the beginning [God] created." And it said: "before Me none was emanated" — for it [Keter] is the head [first] of those that come within the category of the emanated; and it is the end of the whole Emanation, and this is what is said "and after Me there shall be none." And this indicates the strength of the greatness of the Ein Sof, King of kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, which indicates His endurance — that He does not fall under time, but, on the contrary, He brought time into existence, and the existence of His non-being cannot be depicted in any manner in the world. And this is one of His many superiorities over His emanated [beings]: that all of them fall under [contingent] existence, [in] that there was already a time when the Ein Sof was without them, as before the Emanation. And many have thought to say that Keter was prior to all — that is, that, although there was no Emanation, it was in existence, and it is a garment to the Emanator forever. And the holders of this view are masters of the shields [formidable scholars]; and the principal necessity that compelled them to this matter is their saying, of blessed memory, in Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer, "before the world was created, He and His name alone existed" — the meaning [being] that "He and His name" are the Ein Sof and Keter; and they necessitated from this that Keter is prior, and that it is unified with the Emanator and a garment to Him. But this matter is not fitting to be believed. Rather, that the whole Emanation was emanated at one time, and Keter too is among the emanated [beings], as is necessitated from several passages, some of which we shall copy in the Gates, with God's help — and in particular in the Gate of Self and Vessels, and in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, and the Gate of the Tzachtzachot, with God's help. It is found that the Emanator is exalted above His emanated [beings] — for His emanated [beings], their non-being preceded them; which is not so [with] the Emanator, King of kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He. And behold, [this is] a first distinction. Further, the Emanator is distinguished from the emanated [beings] in that their life depends on another — namely, on the Emanator who gives them life; and He is the source and the light and the effluence to all His emanated [beings] — they are found, all of them, to need Him; whereas the Ein Sof, blessed be He, needs nothing other than Himself, but is the source of life, and life is found from Him, until He is the life of [all] life. And therefore, in some places, Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Tikkunim, called Him by the expression "a light that does not subsist in [another] light," etc. — since He does not depend on life and effluence from the side of another, but is the source of light to all the other luminaries. And this matter Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, folio 132b) and in the Zohar [on] Bereshit (22): "Rabbi Shimon opened further and said: 'See now that I, I am He, and there is no god with Me.' He said: Companions, hear ancient words that I wish to reveal... What is [the meaning of] what it said, 'See now that I, I am He, and there is no god with Me'? Rather, this is the Cause above all the upper ones, that [One] called the Cause of Causes, the Cause [from] among these causes, [such] that none of these causes does any deed until it takes permission from the one above it, as we established above regarding 'let us make man' — 'let us make,' surely, was said of two, [in] that this one said to the one above it... And the one above it does nothing until it takes counsel from its fellow. But the one called the Cause over all the causes, above which there is none and below which there is none equal to it — this is what is written, 'And to whom will you liken Me, that I should be equal? says the Holy One.' He said: 'See now that I, I am He, and there is no god with Me,' that takes counsel from Him, in the manner of the one that said, 'And God said, let us make man.'" Thus far [the Zohar's] words.

Now [Rashbi], peace be upon him, intended, in this holy passage, to exalt this superiority — that the Ein Sof is exalted above His emanated [beings], [in] that they need to take counsel, the lower from the upper, for it [the lower] needs effluence from its cause that emanates upon it; and therefore it says "let us make man" — as if to say, "you emanate, and I will act, and man is found made by the two of us"; and the upper one still needs to be emanated [upon] from its cause, for it too does not have the ability [on its own]. But the Ein Sof, blessed be He, does not need to say to another "let us make," but [says] "I, I am He, and there is no god with Me" — that is, "in assistance with Me" — neither a lower one, for it has none below it equal to it, nor an upper one, for there is no upper one other than it, for it is above all the existents. And it said "the Cause over all the upper ones, the Cause [from] among these causes" — [Rashbi] intended to explain to us that the reason it is called the Cause of Causes is for two reasons. The first: from the expression "ascent" (aliyah), and the intent is that it is above all the upper ones — and the intent is not an ascent of place, God forbid, for nothing enters into [the category of] place in the Emanation, all the more so in the Emanator, but the meaning [is] the existence of an ascent of degree, and spirituality, and ability. And the second meaning is from the expression "cause" (illah) and "reason" (sibbah) — that it is a cause and a reason to all the causes that are in existence.

Now a second distinction has been explained, by which the Ein Sof, the Emanator, blessed be He, is distinguished from the emanated [beings]. Further, a third distinction, and it is: that all the emanated [beings] have a name among the holy Names, which delimits them, by which that Sefirah and that emanated [being] is called — like Ehyeh in Keter, and Yah in Chokhmah, and so for all the rest of the Sefirot, as we explained in the First Gate explicitly. And likewise the four-letter Name comprehends the whole Emanation, as is explained in the Zohar, and we shall explain in the Gate of the Four-Letter Name. This is not so [with] the Ein Sof, the Emanator, blessed be He, who has no name and [vowel-]point by which we can designate Him, nor attribute that would delimit Him; and we have not found for Him a name to designate Him except "necessary of existence." And the explanation: that He is necessary in His existence, because the world is impossible, ever, without a conductor who gives effluence and life to all the existents; and for this reason His existence is necessary. And because there is no name that would delimit Him, therefore we designate Him "necessary of existence," and this name the philosophers attributed to Him. Further, they attributed to Him the name Ein Sof (Without End), and the reason [is] because He has no end and terminus. For the thing delimited by a name has an end; and the divinity, because it has no end, has no name that would delimit it, and therefore we designate it by [the name] Ein Sof.

And further [there is] another explanation: because the inquiry into Him has no end — for it is not in the manner of the other inquiries, which have an end and a settling upon a single conclusion; but the inquiry into the divinity is without end, and therefore there is none who knows in Him any essence at all, except by means of the Sefirot, which reveal somewhat of His greatness — [and] only from His Sefirot and upward; [but] from there [upward] there is no apprehension, on account of the depth of what is apprehended; and therefore they designated Him Ein Sof. Further, they attributed to Him "Cause of Causes," and the intent is that the causes — from which other [things] are caused — are [themselves] caused [by] Him; and therefore He is called "the Cause of [the] causes," since He is a first cause to all the causes in the world: for although they are causes to other caused [things], even so they are all caused [by] Him. And there are [those] who said that the supernal Keter too is called "the Cause of Causes," since it is a cause to all the other causes, which are caused [by] it; which is not so from it [Keter] and below — [in] that Chokhmah is not a cause to all the caused causes, for Keter is the [one] that causes and is not caused [by] Chokhmah, but on the contrary Chokhmah is caused [by] it. And likewise, for this reason, they said that Keter is called "the Cause of Causes," [in] that it is the cause of the causes that are effects of it. However, the Ein Sof is called "the Cause of all causes" and "the Cause over the causes," with the addition of "all," to indicate, concerning the Ein Sof, that it is the cause of all causes — even Keter; which is not so [with] Keter, of which the expression "all causes" does not [rightly] apply (and likewise it lacks the "all"), since there is already a cause and reason of which it is the caused [one] — [in] that Keter is caused [by] the Ein Sof, and the Ein Sof is its cause; and likewise [the expression with "all"] would not be attributed thus to Keter. And these three names — namely, Ein Sof, and "the Cause of all causes," and "the Cause over all causes" — Rashbi attributed to the Emanator, blessed be He, in his books many times; and he likewise attributed to Him other names, such as "the Concealed of the Concealed," and likewise "the Ancient of Ancients," and many like these similar to them; and when the inquirer examines them closely, he will find that they all indicate the concealment, as we explained — that He has no name, nor being, nor designation that would delimit Him. And behold, [this is] a third distinction, by which the Emanator is distinguished from the emanated [beings] — apart from several other distinctions, such as the removal of measure, and limit, and the predicates, and the changes, for all is in His Sefirot; and we shall not prolong [discussion] of them. And let us say that, since the Emanator is exalted and distinguished from His emanated [beings] [to] the utmost of distinction, and is distanced [to] the utmost of distance, then reason gives that it is not fitting for the Emanator to enter into the number of the emanated [beings], God forbid, as those thought who said that He is the Keter. And now let us come to prove [it] from the proofs.

After we have, in the preceding chapter, established from reason that Keter is not the Ein Sof, now we shall come, in this chapter, to nullify this view from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, who enlightens the eyes of Israel in this wisdom; and we have from his words several proofs. First, he said in the book of the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, folio 6), and these are his words: "But the Name YHVH is a chariot to its Master, to the supernal Keter. And therefore, 'there is none holy like YHVH' — the Cause over all, hidden and concealed in Keter; and from it His light spread upon YHVH, which is yod = Chokhmah, heh = Binah, vav comprising six Sefirot, heh = Malkhut" — thus far [his words], for our matter. And this is its explanation: YHVH, which is an allusion to nine Sefirot, as he expounds and goes on, is a chariot to its Master, [namely] Keter; and the reason he said "its Master" is because it [Keter] is a father to the whole Emanation, and the whole Emanation is a throne to it. And it said "there is none holy like [koh]" — [this] will be understood with what Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in another place, where he said that "there is none holy like koh" [refers] to Keter. And he said that this is the kaf of "koh," which is the kaf of Keter; and the reason for the kaf is that it is two yods, in the secret of "ten, ten the spoon" (asarah asarah ha-kaf); and this is what he said, "and therefore there is none holy [like koh]" — the meaning [being]: because YHVH is a chariot to Keter — [in] that the four-letter Name [has a] yod at the head [beginning], and Adonai [has a] yod at the end — they are two yods, in the secret of direct light and returning light, which is the kaf of Keter — as this matter will be explained at length in the Gate of the Reversal of the Light, with God's help. And because these two lights are a chariot to Keter, which is the cause of the lights [coming] from the side of the Cause of Causes, the Ein Sof, blessed be He, concealed within it — and from it the light spread by means of Keter, in order that there be direct light and returning light — therefore it is called the kaf of Keter, which is two yods. And let the inquirer not hope from us the explanation of this matter, for its principal place is in the aforementioned Gate. Thus far the explanation of the passage, in brief.

Now he said explicitly, "the Cause over all, hidden and concealed in Keter" — indicating that the Ein Sof is not the Keter. Further, he wrote in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 70, folio 124), and these are his words: "It is called YHVH from the side of the supernal Keter, which is closed up like a closed fist (kometz) that is closed — [such] that none knows what soul there is within. And the one that is within is closed up in thought; the Cause of Causes we call it." Thus far [his words].

And the explanation: that he said at the beginning of his words, above, that in Malkhut is the four-letter Name without [vowel-]point; and according to her nourishment, so is her vocalization. And now he said "from the side of Keter" — the meaning [being]: when she [Malkhut] is nourished from it [Keter], she is called by the name YHVH, which is [the four-letter Name] with the vocalization of kametz (kometz); and the reason [is] "like a kometz that is closed" — the meaning [being]: like [the One that] is closed up in thought, the meaning [being] that even thought is forbidden in [respect of] Him; and He is called by us "the Cause of Causes" — but not that this name delimits Him, for there is no name that would delimit Him, as we explained in the preceding chapter. And the main part of this passage, with all that follows it, is explained at length in the Gate of the Four-Letter Name.
Behold, he explained to us explicitly that the Cause of Causes is hidden and concealed in Keter, and that the Ein Sof is not the Keter itself.

And further, explicitly, in the Tikkunim in another place (Tikkun 70, folio 130), these are his words: "The supernal Keter, although it is primordial light, clear light, refined light, is dark before the Cause of Causes." And the main part of the passage will be explained in the Gate of the Tzachtzachot, blessed be God.

Behold, he indicated explicitly that Keter is not the Ein Sof, in his saying that Keter is dark — that is, that its light does not shine at all [by comparison], that it has no power before the Cause of Causes, which is its Emanator. Further, in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 18, folio 112), these are his words: "A unique Lord, ruling over them all, hidden and concealed in Keter." Thus far [his words].

And the explanation: that above this passage he spoke of the matter of the spiritual life-forces and chariot in the Sefirot, and afterward he said that the Ein Sof — who is called "a unique Lord," as is explained in Sefer Yetzirah — is hidden and concealed in Keter. And the intent is that His divinity is revealed only by means of the sheath of His light and His garment, which is Keter, and by means of it He rides in the rest of the Sefirot.

Behold, he indicated explicitly that Keter is not the Ein Sof. Further, in the Ra'aya Mehemna (Pinchas, folio 243), these are his words: "Because the Cause of Causes is hidden and concealed in this Keter and spread out in the Name YHVH. On Sabbaths and festivals there is no dominion to Samael and the Serpent, nor to all his appointed [forces]; and there is no dominion to Gehinnom — the evil female of Samael and the Serpent — nor to his hosts: all of them are hidden away before the hosts of the King, in the manner that the nations of the world will be hidden away when the Messiah is revealed; this is what is written, 'and they shall come into the caves of the rocks and into the clefts of the crags.'" And its explanation is clear; and from it, it appears with clarity that one cannot say that Keter is the Ein Sof — [the Ra'aya Mehemna] indicates this in saying "the Cause of Causes is hidden and concealed in this Keter." It appears from his words that Keter is a palace for the Cause of Causes.

Now we have several clear proofs and faithful witnesses that Keter is not the Ein Sof, apart from several other proofs besides — and we have not copied them, because we need to copy them in the coming Gates, such as the passage of Elijah, "You are One," etc., which we shall copy in the Gate of Self and Vessels, ch.5; and some of them we have not seen [fit] to copy at all, on account of the length. Even so, by these proofs the view of those who say that Keter is the Ein Sof is nullified.

After we have, in the preceding chapter, striven to establish, of necessity, that the Ein Sof is not the Keter, but [that] each of them is a matter in its own right — that is, this [one is] Emanator and this [one] emanated — we have seen [fit], in this chapter, to nullify another view, close to the view of the earlier Kabbalists, namely the view of Rabbi Shem Tov in Sefer ha-Emunot, Gate 4, ch.1, who first counted the Sefirot and said that Keter is the first Sefirah, [and] afterward said that Keter is not in the category of the Sefirot. And this is the form of his language, in utmost brevity: "All the Kabbalists agreed to count these ten Sefirot — the first, supernal Keter; the second, Chokhmah, etc.; however, the most wondrous and the deepest in the wisdom agreed that, in truth, the supernal Keter is not to be counted in the category of the ten, for it is like the Ein Sof; and just as the Cause of all causes is not to be counted at all, so it is not fitting to count the supernal Keter, for there is no beginning and no terminus and end in it, and it is the All. And Rashbi warned about this in several places, and to this he directed [his words] in Sefer Yetzirah, 'ten and not eleven.' And you already know that it is agreed among the sages of the Mishnah that Elijah the prophet is revealed to all the worthy; and there is a tradition, to some of the later [authorities] of blessed memory, that he was revealed to the great Rabbi Abraham, the pious Av Beit Din, of blessed memory, and from him the great Rabbi Ra'avad, his son-in-law, received [it], and the pious Rabbi Isaac, whose tradition is choice flour, [penetrating] very deep into the wisdom of Kabbalah. And he too explained 'ten and not eleven' — that Keter is not to be brought into the count; and the one that completes the count is the supernal Da'at, which the verse alluded to (Proverbs 3:20), 'by His knowledge the depths were cleaved.' And of it [Sefer] ha-Bahir said that it is the holy palace. And the principal [reference] of the unique Name written in the books of the Prophets, they directed [it] in the letters of the Name, by means of Tiferet, to this [Da'at], for it is a palace to the supernal root." Thus far [his words].

And he prolonged much further according to this view. And in another place he wrote that, for this reason, Sefer Yetzirah called Chokhmah "the depth of beginning," for it is the beginning, etc. This is the view of Rabbi Shem Tov, who wished to say that Keter is not in the count of the Sefirot — though he admitted, regarding the matter, that the Ein Sof is not the Keter, as is proved from his language in which he said, "and just as the Cause of all causes is not to be counted at all, so it is not fitting to count the supernal Keter" — [thereby] indicating that the Cause of all causes is not the Keter, but [rather] Keter is emanated from it. And before we enter into the demolition of this view, it is fitting that we know who brought them into this error; and we say that they were driven to this view on account of three things. First, the passage "By ten utterances the world was created" (Avot 5:1), which we copied in the preceding Gate, in ch.3; and there we strove with the matter and established that from that passage there is no proof for his words at all. And the second: that they saw [that] in Sefer Yetzirah [the author] began to count from the mishnah of the depths from Chokhmah, in his saying "the depth of beginning and the depth of end," which are Chokhmah and Binah — so that it appears that it [Chokhmah] is first to the Emanation, and Keter is not in the count of the Sefirot; and likewise in his saying "one: the spirit of the living God," etc., "two: spirit from spirit" — they said that "one: the spirit of the living God" is Chokhmah, and "spirit from spirit" is Binah, etc. — [so that] it appears that the count of the ten Sefirot begins from Chokhmah. And the third: that they found a great tree on which to hang, namely the divine Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Idra, [where] these are his words: "The place where the beginning is found is from the Holy Ancient One, which is illumined from the mazal," etc., as we shall copy, with God's help.

Now, since the beginning of the Emanation is from Chokhmah, which is illumined from Keter, it appears explicitly that Keter is not in the category of the count of the ten Sefirot; therefore they pressed themselves to seek the completion of the count of the ten, and sought Da'at. But in truth they did not seek what is right. For the matter of this view is rejected — if you wish, [argue] from Scripture; and if you wish, [argue] from reason. A proof from reason: because [Keter] cannot escape [being one] of two things — either it is emanated, or it is not emanated. If it is emanated, then, since it is an effect of the First Cause, why should it not enter into the count of the Sefirot? For who diminished the honor of the Emanation [so much] that Keter, because it is like the Ein Sof and is great and praiseworthy, should not enter into the count of the Sefirot? — for the Sefirot (namely Chokhmah and Binah) are also like the Ein Sof in their power and their excellence, and even so we did not restrain ourselves from counting them among the ten. And behold, since Keter is a cause to Chokhmah, and Chokhmah a cause to Binah, and the three of them are surely emanated — then as Chokhmah [stands] to Binah, so Keter [stands] to Chokhmah; and just as Chokhmah is counted in the count of the Sefirot together with Binah, so Keter should be counted together with Chokhmah. If so, what is the reason that we should elevate Keter above all the rest of the emanated [beings]? And further, that which he said — that it is like the Ein Sof — is no excellence at all, since it is impossible for it to be exactly equal to the Emanator, for, being an effect of Him, it necessarily descended from the degree of its cause; and after we have exalted the Cause of all causes as much as is possible in [what is] without end, it is not fitting to exalt Keter so much, for it is not at the degree of its Emanator, since it is emanated and an effect of a First Cause, as explained. And as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in saying "it is dark before the Cause of Causes" — he indicated that it is not at the degree of the Ein Sof, God forbid; and if so, why is it "like the Ein Sof"? For the definition of the Ein Sof is a predicate by which nothing is [truly] predicated at all, except [of] the Emanator. And since it [Keter] is in the category of the emanated [beings] and is not like the Ein Sof, then why should it not come into the count of the Sefirot? — for it is only of the count of the emanated [beings]; and why should we count some of them and leave out some? This is not fitting. And if you say that it is not emanated — this is impossible to believe, unless we say that it is the Cause of all causes and there is none besides it; for if not so, it is a duality, God forbid, [for us] to say that there is one thing besides the Cause of all causes that was not emanated from it. And if we say that it is emanated as well, but [that] it is not like the rest of the emanated [beings] because it preceded them by a long time — this is impossible, for there cannot be priority over Chokhmah except the priority of cause and effect; for it is impossible to separate and distinguish between every emanated [being] and emanated [being] except like the distinction of cause and effect; and so too the distinction between Chokhmah and Binah. And just as we bring into the count of the emanated [beings] Chokhmah together with Binah, so we also bring in Keter together with Chokhmah. And since, from reason, it is necessitated that Keter is in the count of the ten, it is likewise necessitated from the proof from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 70, folio 118), [where] these are his words: "And these limbs are all in the Sefirot: the head [is] Keter; the brain, Chokhmah; Binah [is] the heart, and in it 'the heart understands'; the two arms, Chesed and Gevurah; the body, the central pillar; the two thighs, Netzach and Hod; Yesod [is] the member (amah); the Shekhinah [is] its sign (ot)." Thus far [his words].
And although there is somewhat in it to rouse [discussion], even so it is not of [what is] relevant to us.

Now he counted ten Sefirot against the limbs, and counted the supernal Keter [as] the head, and did not count Da'at at all — thus the supernal Keter is in the category of the Sefirot. Further, in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, folio 3): "And I heard the sound of their wings, in ten kinds of praise. In a simple song, which is yod — Keter; a doubled song, which is YH — Chokhmah and Binah; a tripled [song] in YHV — which is ChaGaT [Chesed-Gevurah-Tiferet]; a quadrupled [song] in YHVH — which is NHYM [Netzach-Hod-Yesod-Malkhut]." Thus far [his words].

Behold, he counted ten Sefirot in ten letters, and did not count Da'at at all, but [rather] Keter. And there is no reason to say that this Keter that he counted is Da'at — for if so, he should have begun from Chokhmah, which is the beginning of the Emanation according to their view; and further, [because] all agree that this one's name is Keter and this one's name is Da'at, and they differ only [as to] which of them comes into the count of the ten.

And further, a proof from the Zohar, Parashat Bereshit (folio 31), [where] these are his words: "And therefore 'Bereshit' — bet [+] reshit — is Chokhmah, as Yonatan rendered 'Bereshit' [as] 'with wisdom' (be-chokhmeta), because it is second to the count. And it is called 'reshit' (beginning); [yet] this supernal Keter, [being] concealed, is first; and because it does not enter into the count, the second is [called] 'reshit' — therefore, bet [+] reshit." Thus far [his words].

And the explanation: that he found a difficulty in the word "Bereshit," for the bet is large, and it alludes to Chokhmah, as is known, and the word "reshit" too alludes to Chokhmah — it is found, then, that Chokhmah is alluded to in this word twice, improperly; and this he intended in saying "Bereshit — bet [+] reshit — is Chokhmah," the meaning [being] that both allude to Chokhmah: the bet, as is well known that it is bet, and "reshit" in his saying "reshit," which is Chokhmah.
