And [the passage] proceeds to this inquiry, to explain to us how, if a person sins and blemishes the Sefirot, "God judges him"—even though He is without attributes; and likewise, if he acts righteously, what it effects for Him. And the reason is: although the blemish is in the Sefirot, nonetheless, because the Emanator clothes Himself in them, [the offender] forfeits his head to the King. And the parable for this is to a person who tears, with malice, the garments of the King—and all the more so when they are upon the King; even though he did not touch the King Himself, nonetheless he has touched the honor of the King, and has forfeited his head to the kingship. So is the matter with the Sefirot: by reason that the Ein Sof, blessed be He, clothes Himself in them, it is fitting that the one who blemishes them, God forbid, should be liable as though he had touched the King Himself. And this is what he said, "and because You are within, whoever separates," etc. The matter of separation and parting is the matter of the "cutting," as explained in the preceding chapter in the parable of the stories. "And these ten Sefirot proceed in their order"—by this he intended to indicate to us that the order of their standing is according to the order of their emanation, this one above that, by way of cause and effect, even though [more] shall be said of this in the Gate of the Order of Their Standing, God willing. And we saw fit to divide this passage into two chapters, in order to give space between the contiguous [portions], so that the one who studies may be able to encompass the matter of the chapter, by reason of its being brief.

"One long, one short, and one intermediate"—the intent is to explain to us that the Chesed and the mercy and the judgment are all by means of the Sefirot, not in the Emanator. And this is what he said, that the Sefirot proceed in their order, and their order is "one long and one short," which indicates the attributes, as we shall explain, God willing; and all of it is on the side of the emanated ones, who are the bounded, not the Emanator. And the intent in saying "long and short" is not "long and short" in any truly bounded length and shortness, God forbid; but rather the intent is: "long"—from the side of the line of Chesed, where there is long-suffering even to the wicked; and "short"—I mean short of patience, that is, given to wrath, which is the line of judgment; and "intermediate"—which is the line of mercy that mediates between the two, namely Tiferet between Gedulah and Gevurah, and Yesod between Netzach and Hod. And all is comprised in "long, short, and intermediate"—that is, Chesed, judgment, and mercy, which is the inclusiveness of the whole Emanation, as we shall explain in the Gate of Essence and Governance, God willing. "And You are the One who governs them"—the intent is that, although he said that the change of judgment and mercy and the other changes are on the side of the Sefirot, not on that account do we attribute the action to them; for the action is only by means of the Governor, the Emanator, who is the soul that spreads forth within them—namely, the ten Sefirot that are Self, as explained in chapter 4. For by means of the power that hovers over them, governing them like a shepherd his flock, and inclining them to whatever He wishes, there is none who governs them but Him, and none who saves but Him—like the likeness of the soul, whose actions are by means of the soul, and whose changes are by means of the body, as explained there. And it is found, accordingly, that the Chesed and the judgment and the mercy are in relation to them, who are subject to change, while the power for the action is the Self. "Garments You arrayed for them"—meaning that they are like garments to that which is within them, as in the matter of the body, which is a garment to the soul. And he compelled this matter from the matter of the soul, and said that the souls are emanated from the Sefirot; and as the soul is to the body, so is the Ein Sof to the Sefirot. And this is what he said, "from which souls fly forth"—that is, the emanation of the souls is from the Sefirot. And although their emanation is from one place—namely, the Sefirot—and therefore it would be necessitated that human beings be in one uniformity, by reason of the uniformity of their soul; and even if they differ according to the grades of the Sefirot, nonetheless the changes would not multiply, by reason of the fewness of the sources—I mean, the source of the emanation of the souls, which are but ten aspects corresponding to the ten Sefirot—nonetheless the souls were differentiated by reason of their partnership with the body, until no person resembles his fellow.

And behold, these changes are in the aspects of the body, even though the soul has no changes. And so is the matter with the Sefirot, which are the sources of the souls, which are a garment to the Emanator; and although the Emanator has no changes, nonetheless the changes are in the aspect of the emanated ones, who are a garment to the Emanator. Or he means "Garments You arrayed for them"—that is, the Emanator further created ten other Sefirot, which are garments to the Sefirot. And the Sefirot, in relation to the garments—which are the other Sefirot—are as the Ein Sof is in relation to the Sefirot in which He clothes Himself; for just as the Ein Sof, blessed be He, is not at all subject to change, so the Sefirot, which are vessels to the soul, are not intrinsically subject to change, by reason of their nearness to their source, they being the first emanated ones; therefore the ten Sefirot of Creation were necessitated. And the Emanation, in relation to Creation, is as the soul that spreads forth into the vessels. And to the second ones, called Creation, there is yet a garment, called Formation, to which Creation is as the soul within the body—for in Formation the changes are more particular than in Creation. And likewise, the relation of Creation to Formation is as the relation of the Emanation to Creation.

And further, by reason of their nearness to their source, the third array—which is Formation—required a fourth array, which is Action; and by means of the chaining-down of these garments, the limit and the changes and the cessation and the finitude are effected. And the matter will be explained in the Gate of ABYA, God willing. And let us return to the explanation of the passage: for the Emanation, which is ten Sefirot, are vessels in relation to the soul that spreads forth within them; and yet the soul and the vessels are united in a complete union; and the Emanation is a soul to Creation, and Creation a body to the Emanation, and Formation as a kind of garment to the body—for just as the garment covers the body and clothes it, so Formation is a garment in which Creation clothes itself, as explained there. And this is what he said, "and several bodies You arrayed for them"—meaning, You arrayed for these Sefirot, further, garments in which the bodies clothe themselves to effect the changes; for even those bodies have yet a garment in which they clothe themselves—namely, Formation, which is the garment of Creation. And this is what he said, "which are called body relative to the garments that cover over them"—meaning, those bodies are called "body" in relation to another garment in which that body clothes itself, namely Creation, which is a body to the Emanation; and to this Creation there is a garment, which is Formation, as explained. And this explanation is the principal and correct one. And to indicate precisely that they are like the likeness of the soul in the body, he said that the Emanation is designated, in its totality, by the limbs of the body. And this is what he said, "and they are called, in this arrayment," etc.: Chesed, the right arm; and Gevurah, the left arm; and Tiferet is the body that is between the two arms; and from it extend the thighs, which are Netzach and Hod, this one to the right and this one to the left; and the covenant, "the Righteous One, Foundation of the world," Yesod, extends from the extension of Tiferet; and Malkhut is the mouth. And by reason that the order troubled him—for it would have been fitting that Malkhut be in the order of the lower Sefirot, not above them all, as the mouth—therefore he compelled the matter, that it is called the Oral Torah because it is dependent upon the mouth. And afterward he returned to explain the first three, and said that Chokhmah is the brain, and therefore it is called "thought," for thought is in the brain; and Binah is in the heart, and proof of this is from what the Sages, of blessed memory, said—"the heart understands"—they alluded that the heart is from Binah. And because the thought and the understanding that are in the heart are concealed actions of the body—for you have in the body no actions more concealed than the thought and the understanding that are in the heart—and because, in the supernal Form, the brain in which is thought and the heart in which is understanding are Chokhmah and Binah, therefore of them it is said (Deuteronomy 29:28), "The hidden things"—which are the thought and the understanding—"belong to YHVH our God"—which are Chokhmah and Binah, called "YHVH our God," which are the thought and the understanding of the heart, which are hidden. "The supernal Keter is the crown of Malkhut, and of it is said," etc.—meaning, now he comes to explain, concerning the matter of Keter, why Malkhut is called "mouth," which is above, in the head, embedded in the skull, which is Keter; and therefore the head is called "the crown of Malkhut," by reason that the two of them are united—"crown of Malkhut" in the secret of "declaring the end from the beginning" (Isaiah 46:10): "beginning" is Keter, and "end" is Malkhut, and its extension and its emanation are from the supernal Keter. And this is the reason that he placed the seven Sefirot of the structure before the first ones: because the explanation of the mouth, which is Malkhut, is settled only from within the explanation of Keter, as explained. And there are versions in which is written "the skull that lays no tefillin." And it appears to me that it is possibly a scribal error, and that the principal correct version is "skull" alone; and its meaning is the cranium in the head, which hovers over the brain, and it is Keter, which crowns Chokhmah, and it is above all. But if we do read it [as "the skull that lays no tefillin"], its explanation is thus: that below Keter there is the skull of Zeir Anpin, which lays tefillin—which are four passages, four lights: "Kadesh"—Chokhmah; "Ve-haya ki yevi'akha"—Binah; "Shema"—Chesed; "Ve-haya im shamoa"—Gevurah—and these are the tefillin on the head of Zeir Anpin. However, on the head of Arikh Anpin there are no tefillin, because there is no emanation above its emanation; and therefore it is called "the skull that lays no tefillin."

And this matter will be explained in the Idra, in the Sefer Or Yakar. "Within, it is Yod-Heh-Vav-Heh"—he has already explained above that within the Sefirot is the Self, and the Sefirot are a body to the soul that spreads forth within them. And therefore, after he explained the matter of the Emanation in the form of a body and a fitting parable, he came to explain the Self that spreads forth within them. And it is already well known that the four-letter Name, though its basis is four letters, amounts to ten letters in its plene spelling—which are ten Sefirot; and they are the Sefirot that spread forth within the vessels. "And it is the watering of the Tree," etc.—meaning, as we explained in chapter 4, that it is within the power of the Self to enlarge the Sefirot and to add to them, to enlarge them and to diminish them according to the will of their Emanator, as is explained in the passage of the Ra'aya Mehemna that we shall explain in chapter 8. And therefore he called the Self "the watering of the Tree"; for just as the water enlarges the tree and makes it grow, so the inner Emanation enlarges and gives life to the vessels that clothe the Self. And this is what he said, "and it is the watering of the Tree in its arms and its branches, like water that waters a tree, and it grows by that watering." And this is the effluence itself, as we shall explain, God willing. "Master of the worlds," etc.—he needed to dwell upon this to indicate that the four-letter Name in its plene spelling, which is the watering of the Tree, is the Self, the innerness of the Sefirot, which spreads forth from the Ein Sof into the midst of the Sefirot. And the Self is the soul to the Sefirot, the vessels; and they are alive by reason of the inner Sefirot, like a soul that gives life to the body. "And in You there is no likeness and no image," etc.—he comes to explain to us that the existence of the actions, and the judgment and the mercy effected by means of the Self that spreads forth, is not acquired by acquisition in the Self; rather the action is performed accidentally by means of the Self, and intrinsically by means of the vessels—like the likeness of the water that is in the vessels, and the likeness of the light that spreads forth in the lanterns, which we mentioned above. And therefore he said "and in You"—meaning, in the Ein Sof above, before its spreading forth in the Sefirot, there is nothing: not in action, not accidentally and not intrinsically. And the actions are after the spreading-forth of the Sefirot of the Self within the vessels. And this is what he said, "and in You there is no likeness and no image, of anything within or without"—meaning, neither of the actions that are in the Self nor of the actions that are in the vessels. And now this will in no way be apprehended from all that we apprehended of the view of Rabbi Menachem; for according to our view the principal providence and governance is by means of the Sefirot, which are the Self that spreads forth within the vessels. And that Self and the Ein Sof are all one unified thing—except that there is a distinction in our apprehension of Him, between before His spreading forth and after His spreading forth: I mean, the Ein Sof, blessed be He, in His aspect before the Emanation—in which aspect no action whatever is to be adjudged—or in relation to His aspect after the Emanation, when He was revealed and shone by way of these Sefirot, and then the Self spreads forth within the vessels. And the revelation that was revealed, and before its revelation, are all one and unified—like the likeness of the water unified in the spring even after its spreading forth, and like the likeness of the ray of the sun in its source. "And You created heaven and earth," etc.—meaning, now, in the manner we have explained, it is apt that the creation of heaven and earth and the rest of the created beings was by means of the Self of the Godhead, not by means of the vessels, as would arise in the mind from the side of inquiry, which is the view of the inquirers—as they say, that He has removed His providence from this world, as explained in chapter 3; rather the creation was in truth by means of the simple Self, and yet from this there followed for Him neither multiplicity nor change, as explained. And therefore he was abundant in mentioning the matters of creation, saying "heaven and earth," etc.; for although these are many things differing one from another, with all this no multiplicity is necessitated in Him, God forbid. "So that by them [the supernal ones] might be made known"—the intent is that by means of the creation, in which he was abundant in the matters of the actions, [it is] to make known by them the supernal things, for from the lower things we recognize the supernal—as he said (Job 19:26), "and from my flesh I behold God"; and by them a person recognizes the Godhead. And after a person discerns the supernal from the lower, he returns from above to below and recognizes the greatness of the lower, which are suspended from the supernal; for so is the order of the apprehension of the hidden things—from the later to the prior, and afterward from the prior to the later. And the matter is that He emanated His Emanation first, and within it spreads forth the Self; and after the Emanation, Creation; and after Creation, Formation; and after Formation, Action—all this to make known His greatness and His existence in the world; for from Action we discern Formation, and from Formation we ascend and discern Creation, and from Creation we ascend and discern the Emanation, and from the Emanation we recognize the Self that spreads forth; and afterward we recognize the binding of the things in the First Cause, for we know and recognize the binding and union of the Self with the Emanation, and the two of them are united in a firm bond in the Cause of all causes; and from there we recognize and know the binding and union of Creation with the Emanation, and from Creation we know and recognize the binding and union of Formation with Creation, and from Formation we know and recognize the binding and union of Action with Formation—all one, unified, like a strong and mighty chain and a jointed lampstand. And all this is in what is emanated and created and formed and made from Him; but in His Self there is no apprehension, except that we know and recognize that all is suspended upon Him, like an amulet on the arm. And this is what he intended in saying, "and there is none who knows You at all"; for there is none who can apprehend His exaltedness at all, but only that we recognize and know that He is Lord of all, and that from Him all is drawn, in a chain of will and love, and not by compulsion at all—only by benefaction, from cause to effect; and He is the cause over all. And this is what he said, "and You are known as Lord over all"; for the apprehension of the human intellect concerning Him is the chaining-down of the worlds from Him, from cause to effect, and He is the cause over all. "And each of the Sefirot has a known name"—I mean, as was explained in the first Gate, and as will be explained in the Gate of the Four-Letter Name, that the Names and the Sefirot, in existence, are all one thing; and the Name that bounds the Sefirah comprises the Sefirah in the existence of its spirituality. And he said "a known name," that each Sefirah has a name of its own, this one not like that, just as their actions are not the same. "And by them the angels are called"—for those Names which belong to the Sefirot, sometimes the angels appointed over the actions of the Sefirot are called by them, as will be explained in the Gate of the Palaces, chapter 15. And he was lengthy in this to say that, although the relation of the Sefirot to Creation is as the relation of the Ein Sof to the Sefirot, and likewise the relation of Creation to Formation, as explained above, nonetheless the matters are not equal. For the Ein Sof is not called by the name of the Sefirah, whereas the angel is called by the name of the Sefirah, and the Sefirah by the name of the action—as in the matter of Gevurah, Gabriel. But not so the Ein Sof, for He Himself is not called "mighty," since He has no descriptions. And from this we may draw an analogy to the Tetragrammaton-forms and the Names that may not be erased: for the Sefirah and the angel are called by one name, because they are bounded by that name or that Tetragrammaton-form; but in the Ein Sof there is no Tetragrammaton-form and no name that bounds Him. And this is what he said, "but You have no known name," because there is no relation of the actions in Him, and He is not subject to change, nor bounded by a limit, nor finite, such that He should be designated by a name of action, or by a Tetragrammaton-form and name. "For You are the One who fills all names"—as is known, that He is the Self that spreads forth within the Sefirot and fills and gives life to them, and is their root, like the likeness of the soul that is the root of the body. And this is what he said, "and You are the completeness of them all," for their completeness is in their power, and their power is the Self that spreads forth. And to indicate that He is the soul and that the action depends principally upon Him—and even though the actions are performed by means of the Sefirot, as I explained—therefore he said, "and when You depart from them," etc.: meaning, that upon the departure of His Self that spreads forth within the Sefirot, the vessels remain empty, without benefit, like a body without a soul, God forbid. "You are wise, but not with a known wisdom"—he was emphatic to say that, although the Sefirah is called "Chokhmah," the intent is not that He is wise by means of this Chokhmah; and likewise, though He is called "understanding," it is not that He understands by means of this Binah; rather, on the contrary, He is the source of Chokhmah and Binah, and Chokhmah and Binah are vessels to His wisdom and His understanding; and it is not that the Sefirah is literally His wisdom and His understanding, for then He would be found wise by a wisdom outside Himself. And He is the vitality of Chokhmah and Binah, and they are emanated from Him—as the Ra'aya Mehemna explained, in a passage that will be explained in chapter 8, where it said "wise of Himself," etc., "for Chokhmah is not called wisdom of itself," etc. "You have no known place, except to make known," etc.—meaning, it is not that, because we say He is wise with Chokhmah and understands with Binah, it would be necessitated from this that His source and His Presence are in Chokhmah and Binah, God forbid; for He is not subject to place, and Chokhmah and Binah and the rest of the Sefirot do not bound His greatness and His exaltedness, for He is not grasped in limit and place. And even though the Emanation is the place of His Presence, this is that He contracted Himself to show the peoples His glory, so that they might be able to apprehend some of His greatness. And the measure of the phrase "You have no known place" is: because place necessitates limit and corporeality, for that which is grasped in place is a body, possessing limit; and the matter is not so in the Emanation; for the Ein Sof is not grasped in place, and even if He clothes Himself in the Emanation and is revealed in it [in] some of His greatness, it is in order to show the peoples and the princes that they might know Him. And this is the reason for the Emanation, as explained in the second Gate, God willing. "And to show how the world is governed in judgment and mercy"—meaning, He revealed His Emanation to show His governance to the inhabitants of the world; and as he concludes, the matter of righteousness and justice is in the Sefirot in relation to human beings—not that any attributes whatever are grasped in Him; and the attributes are in Him accidentally, and intrinsically in the Sefirot. Thus far has our poor intellect reached in the explanation of the passage that comprises the bulk of the corners of the wisdom. And we entreat the face of the one who studies, that in this passage he labor at the doors of contemplation, once and twice and three times, and he will find for his soul repose in this matter, as explained.

We have yet a sound proof for this inquiry from within the words of Rashbi—may peace be upon him—(in Zohar Chadash, portion Va'etchanan, fol. 67), in the passage [of the Measuring Line]. And these are his words: A light that does not subsist in [another] light engraved and brought forth the spark of all sparks, and it struck within the delight-in-delightings, and was concealed within it and not known. At the time when this delight wished to expand, this spark, concealed within that will, issued forth in a manner that is seen and not seen, [yet] did not abide so as to subsist in that manner. When this will expanded, this spark struck—showing color and not color—and entered into this expansion and issued forth in its colors, and ascended and descended and stood, in [its] ascent, within the will and the expansion. The will struck its expansion in the concealment that is not known, and brought forth thin lights, comprised as one. When these thin lights wished to issue forth—the spark in which are lights—it struck against that expansion and was distanced (another reading: was pressed); and from within the distancing (another reading: the pressing) those thin lights issued forth and were heard as one. Then this spark showed its colors in them, and they were all colored as one—white and red, green and black; and it tarried within it twelve months. Afterward they were uprooted from there and transplanted in another place. And this spark ascends and descends; and this is called the Botzina de-Kardinuta (the Hardened Light). This [light] arrayed and struck within all the plantings of lights, and says to it, "Grow!" Then it brought forth the wellsprings of that first expansion; and it darkened and gave light to them all, and they were enlarged by this Botzina de-Kardinuta. He who gives light, gives light, and it ascends and descends and expands in all directions. And then it is called the Measuring Line; and the measure abides above and below. The Measuring Line is the Botzina de-Kardinuta, the concealed of all concealed; a shining measure that arrayed beauty for all—that beauty which issues from the first simplicity, it arrayed them. By it they abide, to measure above and below. Whoever merits this and knows it merits to know the wisdom of his Master. Happy is his portion in this world and in the world to come. End of his words.

We saw fit not to be lengthy in the precise [parsing] of the language of the passage, but rather to explain it with a strong hand, because there is no comprehension in it at all; and by our way the whole will be explained, God willing. "A light that does not subsist in [another] light"—meaning, the Ein Sof, the King of the kings of kings, who is a light shining to all the lights; and yet He does not subsist in the light of the Sefirot, but rather rules over them, and is not revealed within them, for in His existence He is the Necessarily Existent, abiding in Himself as before His spreading forth in the Sefirot. Or he means: that it would be fitting that the Ein Sof, by reason of the abundance of His concealment, be called "darkness"; and since Malkhut, too, is called "darkness," yet the two are not equal—for the darkness of the Ein Sof is by reason of the utmost brilliance, which is not apprehended nor revealed, and by reason of the abundance of His concealment He is called "darkness"; whereas Malkhut is called "darkness" by reason of the absence of light.

And behold, by reason that he called the Ein Sof "light," which is not fitting—for it is not apprehended that it should be called "light," but he was compelled to call it "light" to indicate that it is the source of all the lights, and the whole Emanation are sparks of light shining from it, and therefore he designated it by the name "light"—afterward he made amends for this: that even though he called it "light," it is not an apprehended light, but a concealed light that is not fit to be designated by the name "light," except "a light that does not subsist in [another] light," but rather is concealed in the utmost concealment. Or he means "a light," etc.—the Ein Sof, who is a radiance shining to all the luminaries and exalted above all the lights: for the other lights receive light from another and are suspended upon lights other than themselves; but the Ein Sof, blessed be He, is a light that does not receive and has no need of another. And the meaning of "engraved" is "incised." And this is because it is already well known that the Sefirot are more refined when they are in their source than after their spreading forth, as will be explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, God willing. And now, since he wished to say "and brought forth," which is the beginning of the Emanation and the revelation and the thickening, he had to say "engraved"—the intent being to say [it is] the beginning of the thickening of the light to be revealed; all this by way of parable, to our human intellect and our limited understanding. And he said "and issued forth" (nafik), which is an intransitive verb, and he did not say "and brought forth" (apik), because these sparks are the Self that spreads forth within the Sefirot, as will be explained; and since this is the existence of His Self, therefore he said "and issued forth," whose meaning is that it issued forth of itself, and did not bring forth another; for the spreading-forth of His Self and its revelation is by means of itself, not by means of another. "The spark of all sparks"—meaning, the light of the luminaries, a soul to the souls, which is the Self of the Godhead, namely the ten Sefirot, a soul to the Sefirot the vessels, as explained in the preceding chapters. "And struck within the delight-in-delightings"—the intent is the Keter, when it is concealed in the Ein Sof; then it is called "delight-in-delightings."

And behold, it struck within it to be revealed, and the spark was concealed within the Keter, as is fitting, because it is a soul to it. And this is what he said, "and was concealed within it and not known"—the intent is that neither the Keter nor the spark, which is a soul to it, was revealed, by reason of the abundance of concealment. "At the time when this delight wished to expand"—meaning, the Keter is called "delight"; and the reason he called it "delight" and did not call it "delight-in-delightings" as above is because it is already emanated and stands to emanate—for it has a revelation greater and greater than when it was concealed in the Ein Sof—and therefore it is called "delight" alone, indicating the revelation. "Wished to expand"—the intent is that the Keter wished to be revealed and to emanate an expansion, which is Chokhmah, together with the Sefirot that were concealed within the Keter. "This spark issued forth"—it is a simple matter that, before the emanation of the Sefirot, He had to emanate the soul; for the soul is the cause of the Sefirot, and it is the one that enlarges and gives life to them, as explained above and as will be explained, God willing. And so it was necessitated to order the matter, to emanate the soul, which is the spark—namely the light that shines and sparkles within the Sefirot; and afterward Chokhmah, which is the Sefirah itself, the vessel, would be revealed and emanated; and afterward the spark and the soul would enter into the midst of Chokhmah. And this is why he first said "this spark issued forth and was concealed within that will," which is the light of the soul concealed within the Keter, which is "the will." "In a manner that is seen and not seen," etc.—meaning, while it was in the Keter it was concealed and hidden; and above, in the Keter, by reason of the abundance of concealment, he said "and not known." But now, after the spreading-forth into the existence of Chokhmah, the light and the soul sparkle within it, because it has more revelation—as is known, that it is called "being"—he said "in a manner that is seen and not seen." And he was precise in saying "in a manner" (ke-gavna) and did not say "in the manner" (be-gavna, with a bet), because even "manner" is not aptly [said] except [as] "seen and not seen"—meaning, an apprehended existence, yet not a sufficient apprehension; rather, "and did not abide so as to subsist in that manner"—meaning, the colors are the actions, and the action of Chokhmah is not apprehended, as we shall explain in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 3, God willing. "When this will expanded"—meaning, above he said "when it wished," that is, when it wished to expand and be revealed and had not yet expanded, and then there was the existence of the soul of Chokhmah; and now he said "when it expanded," that is, that the existence of Chokhmah itself was literally emanated. "This spark struck," etc.—meaning, the soul of Chokhmah struck within it and emanated it and entered into it, for so is the way of the soul within the Sefirot. And he said "color and not color," and did not say "seen and not seen" as he said above; the reason is that above it was within the Keter and was more concealed, and therefore he said "seen," etc.; but now that it is literally within Chokhmah, he said "color and not color," which is more revealed—namely, an apprehended color; and that a person cannot judge which color it is, because the essence of Chokhmah is not apprehended at all. "And issued forth in its colors"—the intent is that there were emanated in Chokhmah all the rest of the Sefirot, which were concealed within the Keter; and likewise there were emanated there also the rest of the souls of the Sefirot, comprised in the spark, which is the soul of Chokhmah; and they are called "colors" because there is nothing in the lantern to show its colors except by means of the light that shines and makes its colors shine toward its surface; therefore the colors are attributed to the soul, namely the spark and the light.

And the matter of how the Sefirot were comprised in the Keter and were emanated to Chokhmah, etc., will be explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, God willing. "And ascended and descended and stood, in [its] ascent, within the will and the expansion"—meaning, the soul is concealed within the Ein Sof, that is, His Self; and it pierces and descends down to the order of the Sefirot. For one may not say that what is in Chokhmah is not what is in Keter, and what is in Keter is not what is in Chokhmah, God forbid; rather all is one thing, like the likeness of the ray of the sun shining through the lanterns: for although the light shining through one lantern is red, and that shining through another is green, with all this we shall not deny that the two lights are one unified light, and the change follows from the change of the lanterns. And so for the matter of the soul, that all is one unified light, and even if it is changed, it is by reason of the Sefirot. And accordingly the soul "ascends and descends and stands, in [its] ascent," for the two of them are crowned as one, and all is unified in the Ein Sof. And although we say that the light is one and unified, we shall not deny that the light shining through the Keter is the first grade, and the light is revealed there [at] the utmost height; and as the light descends from before the presence of the Ein Sof, so it descends wondrously according to the descent of the grades, from cause to effect. And with all this, the reason for the changing is by reason of the screens and the lanterns that thicken the light and darken it, and it is accidental to them, not intrinsic; and from this no blemish whatever follows to the light, just as no blemish is attributed to the ray of the sun even though its light is darkened by reason of the lanterns. And this is what he said, "and ascended and descended and stood, in [its] ascent," which is the Ein Sof; "within the will" is the Keter; "and the expansion" is Chokhmah; and the intent is that the light is united in a complete union, as explained. "The will struck its expansion"—for Chokhmah, by the power of Keter, emanated Binah together with the rest of the Sefirot; and this is "the will struck," which is the Keter; "its expansion" is Chokhmah. "In the concealment that is not known"—meaning, in the first aspect that belongs to Chokhmah together with Keter; and from there [comes] the union of Keter with Chokhmah, to give it power to emanate Binah; and that aspect is concealed, as is fitting to the Keter; and from within that aspect the Keter was united with Chokhmah, so that Chokhmah might emanate, from its power, Binah; and this matter will be explained at length in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, God willing. "And brought forth thin lights, comprised as one"—the intent is Binah, which comprises seven Sefirot; and then, while they are there, they are like the horns of locusts—until the Holy One blessed be He transplanted them, etc. And this is what he said, "thin"—that they are not in revelation and thickness as when they are emanated below, but rather are in great refinement. And he said "comprised as one"—the intent is Binah, which comprises them, as we said; and the whole principal [function] of Binah is the inclusiveness of the six extremities; and by them it is called heh, which is the five bars of the Tabernacle, which are from Chesed downward, comprised in the five lights that are in the account of creation, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Fifty Gates, chapter 7, God willing. "When they wished to issue forth"—meaning, although he said above that they were already emanated, we have already explained that they cannot be emanated unless their soul and their sparkling light are emanated to them first; but he wished to complete the matter of the emanation of the Sefirot, [and] afterward he returned and said that when they wished to be revealed, they were revealed by means of the soul, which is called "spark." "In which are lights"—it is the soul fitting to Binah, which comprises the souls of the rest of the Sefirot, just as it comprises the actual Sefirot as well, as we explained. "It struck against that expansion and was distanced," etc.—the intent is that by the power of the soul the Sefirot were emanated, thin lights, in the manner we explained above, for they were like the horns of locusts. "And were heard as one"—the intent is that until now the lights were not revealed in revelation at all; and even now that they are revealed, it is not an intrinsic revelation but a partial revelation: somewhat of hearing without sight; and this is what he said, "and were heard as one." And his saying "as one" means united as one in the existence of Binah, and in it the Sefirot appear at the beginning of their revelation, as we shall explain the law and its reason in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, God willing. "Then this spark showed its colors in them"—that is, the spark of the soul; and here he said "showed" and not above, and the reason is that in Binah is "the grade that stands to be asked of," as is known, and therefore "it showed its colors in them," which is not so above; and this is what he said above, "and were heard," to indicate that in Binah is the beginning of the revelation, as we explained. And the reason for "its colors" is not that the spark, namely the soul that spreads forth, possesses colors—for we already premised above that the soul is simple, etc.—but rather, by means of the revealed light the colors appear in the Sefirot, as in the parable of the lantern, which possesses known colors, and those colors are revealed only by means of the ray of the sun shining through it, and then, by means of the light, the colors are seen. And so is the matter with the Sefirah: it was not able to show the peoples and the princes its power except by means of the soul that gives it life and gives it power to act—like the likeness of the body, which has no action except by means of the soul, even though the soul is simple, as explained; and the intent is that the soul reveals the colors of Binah. And the measure of the phrase is thus: "it showed its colors in them"—I mean, it shows in them, in the Sefirot themselves, their colors. And the reason he said "its colors" in the singular and did not say "their colors" is because they are comprised in Binah in a unified oneness, as explained. "And they were all colored as one," etc.—meaning, there are no colors except in Binah when it is revealed in itself; and "they were colored" afterward, below, by means of revelations; and since from there downward are the colors, namely the actions, therefore, close to their revelation, he said "they were colored." "White"—Chesed, and Netzach, which branches from it, for it too is white, but not like it. "Red"—Gevurah and Hod, both of which are red, in the secret of judgment. "Green"—Tiferet and Yesod, which are between the two colors, white and red. "And black"—it is Malkhut; and it is named thus by way of the "darkness" we explained above. And all this will be explained in the Gate of the Colors, God willing. "And it tarried within it twelve months"—it is already well known that we reckon the molad of BaHaRaD for the conjunction before the creation of the world (see Tur, Orach Chayim, §427).

And behold, it had to be a full month, and there is no month without a year; therefore there had to be, before the emanation of the structure, some [span of] time—not "time," God forbid, but a priority in the manner of the other priorities, which are a priority of rank, like the priority of the cause over the effect. And therefore there had to be, before the emanation of the six days of the structure, [a state in which] they were crowned in Binah, in the secret of six and six: six for mercy, and six for judgment. And this is what is called "tarrying." And these are the twelve boundaries that are likewise in Binah, which are the twelve Tetragrammaton-forms that are in Tiferet after its emanation in its place, as will be explained in the Gate of the Chapters of the Names, chapters 6, 7, and 8, God willing.

And behold, with this there may be understood a great doubt that falls upon the account of creation, namely their saying that there was no creation on the seventh day—and why, since the creation of the Sabbath day itself was already [accomplished], for the day itself requires creation; for so it is said in the Zohar: "six days the Lord made"—it says "six," and not "in six," implying that the six themselves the Lord made, which is the creation of heaven and earth, which are the six that comprise the six extremities; and accordingly, the creation of the Sabbath itself was already [accomplished]; and if so, how did He "rest" and "cease" on the seventh day? Rather, surely the Sabbath preceded the world; and were it not for the Sabbath, which gives power to the six days, they would have no power to act, because all six days, which are the six extremities, receive power from the central point, which is the sustaining of the hollow of the extremities, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Fifty Gates, chapter 5, God willing.

And behold, the six days had to tarry in the Sabbath to receive their sustenance from it; and if so, the Emanation was only six days, for the Sabbath preceded the world. And likewise the matter of this world: after six days will be the Sabbath; and just as the days of the week draw sustenance from the Sabbath and enter into it, this is "and it tarried there twelve months," which are a year—namely Tiferet, which comprises six extremities, and it draws sustenance [of] judgment and mercy; and so it is found, six for judgment and six for mercy, which are the twelve months. And this is the choicest of the explanations that arise in this matter. "And were transplanted in another place"—the intent is their emanation to their places, as is known, that they were like the horns of locusts, and the Holy One blessed be He transplanted them.

And the matter of the reason for the transplanting and the planting will be explained at length in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, God willing. "And this spark ascends and descends"—the intent is the soul that is unified within them, and ascends up to the uttermost height, and descends down to the uttermost depth, as I explained. "And this is called the Botzina de-Kardinuta"—the meaning of "Botzina de-Kardinuta" in all the Zohar is "brimstone," and the intent is the Keter; for the supernal light, which is the Ein Sof, cleaves to the Keter and is held within it, like a lamp of brimstone in which the light is held most firmly. And some read kadrinuta, and its meaning is "blackness," by reason of the abundance of its concealment. And we have another way in this matter, and it is explained in the Sefer Or Yakar, God willing. And now, accordingly, the light that spreads forth from within the Ein Sof, which is concealed in the supernal Keter, spreads forth from there and descends and shines by way of the Sefirot, of which it is the soul. And because the source of the light and the Self is from the Keter, therefore the whole Self is called Botzina de-Kardinuta, because its root and the source of the light is related to the Keter. And so Rashbi—may peace be upon him—explained in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 6): "The Cause over all, hidden and concealed in the Keter; and from it His light spreads forth by way of YHVH"—that is, yod, Chokhmah; heh, Binah; vav, comprising six Sefirot; heh, Malkhut. End of his words. And we have already explained it with a strong hand in the third Gate, chapter 2, God willing.

And behold, our whole matter appears from within it: that the light of the Self that spreads forth within the Sefirot has its source [in] the Keter, by means of the Ein Sof concealed within it. If so, it is fitting that this light be called by the name Botzina de-Kardinuta, which is a name of the Keter; for by means of this light the Keter is so called, because it shines like a lamp, etc. "This [light] arrayed and struck within all the plantings of lights, and says to it, 'Grow!'"—meaning, by means of this light, which overflows and shines within the Sefirot, it enlarges them and gives them measure and weight according to the will of the Emanator, namely His Self that spreads forth. And to this the Sefer Yetzirah directed [its words] (cited above in the third Gate, chapter 4), saying, "their measure is ten, which have no end," etc.—that it is in His power to enlarge them without end, and to bound them with a limit, in the manner explained above in the preceding Gates. And concerning the matter of the soul he said, "and the Lord is one," etc.—who is unified in the source, for the soul and the source are all one. "Ruling over the Sefirot, all of them, and forever and ever"—the intent is that, if He wishes, He would expand them up to the Ein Sof, without end; and the intent is in the increase of the revelation of His light within them. And the measure of the language of the said passage [is thus]: "This [light] arrayed and struck," which is the Emanation; "within all the plantings," which are the Sefirot; "lights," which are the souls and the Self that spreads forth—meaning, He emanates within the Sefirot lights and Self. "Then it brought forth the wellsprings of that [supernal] expansion," etc.—meaning, then, after the emanation and the arraying of the order of the Sefirot, each one according to its rank, then Chokhmah—which is the expansion mentioned above—arrays the source of the lights, I mean the effluence from the Keter, and it is in its power to add or to diminish. The matter is that the absence of the light and its departure, or its providence and its descent by way of the Sefirot, is in Chokhmah—as in the matter of (Psalms 10:1) "Why, O Lord, do You stand afar off?"—in the manner of the light likened in the parable of the stories, which I explained, God willing. And therefore Chokhmah is the one that brings forth the sources and the light of the Sefirot, in order to give them life and to enlarge them by that effluence of light; and it is in its power to conceal the light, so that it does not shine as is fitting, and then judgment comes to be. And this is what he said, "then it brought forth the wellsprings," etc., "by this Botzina de-Kardinuta"—meaning, by means of the light of the Self that spreads forth from the supernal Keter, as explained. "He who gives light, gives light"—meaning, by means of it the Ein Sof, who is designated, in concealment, [as] "He who gives light, gives light," so as not to designate Him by a name, gives light. Or he means: by means of the Botzina de-Kardinuta there is light and effluence to every possessor of light, and it shines, because there is no light to a Sefirah except by means of the Botzina de-Kardinuta, which is the source of light to all the lights. "And it ascends and descends and expands in all directions"—meaning, by means of the light it enlarges the Sefirot and gives them measure in every direction, as he concludes; though this light is unified in its source, as explained; and therefore it is called the Measuring Line—meaning, a line in the manner of the attributes, which are in a line; and it is the Measuring Line that gives measure to all the Emanation. And it is literally the Botzina de-Kardinuta, as we explained; except that the aspect of the light itself is called Botzina de-Kardinuta, and in the aspect of the attributes, [in] measuring them according to His will, which is the Self of the Emanator, it is called the Measuring Line. And this is what he said, "by this Botzina de-Kardinuta," which is the light, as explained, "when it expanded in all directions," that is, that it gives measure to every side of the sides of the Emanation, then it is called the Measuring Line. "And the measure abides above and below"—meaning, in the aspect of its giving measure to all the attributes, it is called the Measuring Line, and in the aspect of its Self, it is called Botzina de-Kardinuta; for that is its aspect in relation to before its spreading forth in the Sefirot, to illumine and to measure. And this is what he said, "and the Measuring Line is the Botzina de-Kardinuta"—meaning, this Measuring Line is itself the Botzina de-Kardinuta, the concealed of all concealed—that is, its aspect before it spread forth to measure and to give measure to the Sefirot. "A shining measure that arrayed beauty for all—that beauty which issues from the first simplicity"—meaning, the Botzina de-Kardinuta and the Measuring Line are two aspects unified in the utmost union; for the matter of its aspect before its spreading forth, that is, the departure of the light into the source, and the aspect of its measure, are all together—namely, "a shining measure," which is the light that spreads forth and gives beauty to all the attributes, in the manner of the parable of the light to the lanterns, as explained. "Which issues from the first simplicity"—if so, its being a measure to the attributes, and its being a lamp (botzina)—that is, "which issues from the first simplicity"—are all one, unified. "It arrayed them by it," etc.—meaning, the Botzina de-Kardinuta is the one that arrays the attributes by the Self, namely the Measuring Line. "Whoever merits this," etc.—as is well known, that the one who discerns the courses of the Self within the Sefirot, that is the lovely rank, above which there is no rank; and of such a one, and the like of him, it is said, "He saw his world in his lifetime, [and] recognizes his Maker." And of him it is said (Psalms 91:14), "I will set him on high, because he has known My name"; and of this it is said (1 Chronicles 28:9), "Know the God of your father, and serve Him." And let not the one who studies think that the departure of this light of the Self that spreads forth, to its source, or its spreading forth, indicates change in the Emanator, God forbid; for change is not aptly [predicated] of such a matter, just as change is not aptly [predicated] of the removal of providence from the world, even according to the way of Rabbi David and the rest of those who speak on this matter; for the change in the attributes is by reason that they are not prepared to receive the Self—not by reason of change, God forbid.

And behold, the explanation of this passage is completed, according as it was poured forth upon us from Heaven. And it is not hidden from us that this passage requires a wider explanation, and an intellect that is not now within the human compass—how much more so that the absence of [such] existence could explain it; but with all this we have done what was incumbent upon us, and from within it we have learned the existence of the Sefirot and the Self that spreads forth within them, as has been explained, and it will yet be explained at length, God willing. And blessed is YHVH, the God of Israel, who has not let a redeemer cease for us, and has enlightened our eyes in this passage—which is in the apprehension of a thing agreed upon in the mouths of all the Kabbalists when they say "the effluence that overflows." And from within them the give-and-take has been clarified: that the effluence is the revelation of the soul of the Sefirot and of the Self of the Emanator within the Sefirot; and then His light descends and pierces down to the abyss, for the Sefirot will answer [with] the light to Creation, and Creation to Formation, and Formation to Action, and Action to the heavens, and the heavens will answer the earth, and the earth will answer Israel; and "abundant good to the house of Jacob" in their cleaving to their God, as it is written (Deuteronomy 4:4), "And you who cleave to YHVH your God are alive, all of you, this day." For the cause of life is by reason of the cleaving. And he means by saying "alive, all of you"—that you all draw sustenance from the Living, Eternal One; and therefore "alive, all of you."

After we have compelled, from the passage in the preceding chapter, the matter of the Self and the vessels, there is yet a clear proof to bring, in a third passage of Rashbi—may peace be upon him—in the book of the Ra'aya Mehemna (portion Bo, fol. 42b). And these are his words: "And to whom will you liken Me, that I should be equal?" (Isaiah 40:25)—for before the Holy One blessed be He created any image in the world and formed any form, He was alone, without form and without likeness. And whoever apprehends Him as He was before creation—when He is beyond any image—it is forbidden to make for Him a form or image in the world, neither by the letter yod nor by the letter heh, nor even by the holy Name, nor by any letter or vowel-point in the world. And this is [the meaning of] "for you saw no likeness"—of anything that has in it a likeness or image you saw nothing. But after He made this image of the Chariot of the supernal Adam, He descended there and was called by that image "YHVH," so that they might apprehend Him by each and every attribute among His attributes; and He was called "El, Elohim, Shaddai, Tzeva'ot, Ehyeh," so that they might apprehend Him by each and every attribute—how the world is governed by lovingkindness and by judgment, according to the deeds of human beings. For were His light not to spread forth over all creatures, how would they apprehend Him, and how would "the whole earth is full of His glory" be fulfilled? Woe to him who likens Him to any attribute—even to any of these attributes that are His own—how much more so to human beings, whose foundation is in the dust, who perish and pass away. Rather, His likeness is according to His dominion over that attribute, and indeed over all creatures, and above that attribute; and when He withdraws from it, He has no attribute, and no likeness, and no form—like the likeness of the waters of the sea, for the waters that issue from it have no graspable [shape] at all, and no form; but by the spreading-forth of the waters of the sea over a vessel, which is the earth, a likeness is made, and we can make there a reckoning. Thus: the source of the sea is one. A spring issues from it, according to its spreading-forth into that vessel, in a circle, which is the yod—behold, the source is one, and the spring that issues from it is two. Afterward He made a great vessel, like one who digs a great pit and it is filled with the water that issues from the spring—behold, that great vessel is called "sea," and it is the third vessel. And that great vessel is divided into seven vessels, like long vessels; thus the water spread from the sea into seven streams. Behold, the source, and the spring, and the sea, and the seven streams—these are ten. And if the Craftsman should break those vessels that He fashioned, behold, the water returns to the source, and the broken vessels remain dry, without water. Thus the Cause of causes made ten Sefirot, and called Keter "source," and in it there is no end to the welling of the light; and therefore He called Himself Ein Sof, and He has no likeness or form, and there is no vessel there to grasp Him, to know Him by any knowledge at all; and therefore it is written, "Into what is too wondrous for you do not inquire, and into what is concealed from you do not search." Afterward He made a small vessel, and this is the yod, and it was filled from Him, and He called it "a welling spring of wisdom," and He called Himself "wise" by it, and He called that vessel "Chokhmah." And afterward He made a great vessel and called it "sea," and called it "Binah," and He called Himself "understanding." By it [He is] "wise of Himself and understanding of Himself." For Chokhmah is not called wisdom of itself, but only on account of that Wise One who fills it from His welling; and it is not called Binah of itself, but only on account of that Understanding One who fills it from Himself. For were He to withdraw from it, it would remain dry; this is [the meaning of] "the waters have failed from the sea, and the river is parched and dry" (Isaiah 19:5). Afterward, "and He smote it into seven streams" (Isaiah 11:15), and made it into seven precious vessels, and called them Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod, Yesod, Malkhut. And He called Himself "Great" in Gedulah, and "Pious" in Chesed, and "Mighty" in Gevurah, and "Glorious" in Tiferet; and in Netzach, "the Master, victor of battles," and He is the Victory of victories; and in Hod He called His name "the Majesty of our Maker"; and in Yesod He called His name "Righteous," and Yesod—all the vessels and all the worlds rest upon it; and in Malkhut He called His name "King." And "His are the greatness, and the might, and the glory (Tiferet), and the victory (Netzach), and the majesty (Hod), for all that is in heaven [and earth]"—which is the Righteous One; "His is the kingship"—which is Malkhut. All is in His authority: to diminish in the vessels, and to add to them welling, and to diminish according to His will in it; and there is no other god above Him to add to it or to diminish from it. End of his words, as relevant to our intent. And now, may the repose of the holy Rashbi—may peace be upon him—be exalted, for he has enlightened our eyes with the pleasantness of his sayings and the sweetness of his tongue; he was lengthy in explaining to us all the details upon which we were lengthy in chapter 4. And although our intent is explained from within his words, with all this we shall set our eyes upon this passage, to explain some of the doublings of the language and to expound the depth of his words, God willing. "Before He created," etc.—meaning, before the Ein Sof, blessed be He, was revealed in this pure and holy Emanation of His, the existence of His simple Godhead was united in the Self of His Godhead alone, and He had neither name nor letter nor vowel-point, since the existence of the Names is in the Emanation; and if so, since there was no Emanation, there was neither name nor figure. And the meaning of "form and figure" is an attribute that should be designated to Him; for the Emanation is an attribute and a concealed form, apprehended by the prophets—peace be upon them—by means of the intermediaries; but then, before His Emanation, there was neither name nor figure nor attribute at all, but rather the Ein Sof united in the Self of His Godhead, as explained. "And whoever apprehends Him before creation"—meaning, the Ein Sof, blessed be He, has two aspects: whether we consider Him in relation to His Godhead before the Emanation, which is His aspect revealed to His own Self and not to another; or His apprehended aspect, which is His aspect toward the emanated ones. And now he said "and whoever apprehends Him"—the intent is that one who wishes to engage in His existence, in the knowledge of His Godhead above the emanated ones—which is the first aspect—must take care not to depict in Him any name or letter or vowel-point. And this is what he said, "and whoever apprehends Him before creation"—meaning, to engage with Him before the emanation of the created and the emanated ones, namely His first aspect, which is "beyond image"—meaning, that He is above the emanated ones, that is, His aspect concealed from them. He said that it is forbidden to make for Him a form and image, etc.—meaning, that it is not fitting to bound Him by a letter or a vowel-point, to say "His attribute is thus," [since] He has no attributes above. And therefore He is not designated by letters, for the letters and the attributes are all one. And the matter is that the letters are emanated forms that bound the corporeal letters to the spiritual; and how would it be apt to ascribe emanated forms to the aspect of the Ein Sof before the Emanation? And therefore neither name nor vowel-point is apt of the Ein Sof; and even in Keter, letters are not applicable in the aspect of its own self, but only in the aspect of its rectification—that is, what it comprises of nine Sefirot; and therefore it is called by the name Ehyeh and by the name YHVH: from the side of Chokhmah it is called by the name YHVH, and from the side of Binah by the name Ehyeh, for the name Ehyeh is female to the name YHVH. And this matter will be explained in the coming Gates, God willing, and in the Sefer Or Yakar, in the commentary on the Idra. "And not even by the holy Name," etc. And at first glance this is difficult, in view of what is expounded in Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer, which said that before the world was created the Holy One blessed be He and His Name alone existed—from which it appears that the four-letter Name preceded [the world] as [old as] His own pre-eternity. But this is no question, for the four-letter Name is the existence of the Sefirot, and it is a coming-to-be in the coming-to-be of the Sefirot; but in the Ein Sof neither name nor vowel-point is applicable.

And the matter of the passage will be explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, chapter 4, God willing. "Of anything that has in it a likeness," etc.—meaning, of all the Sefirot that receive likeness and image upon His spreading-forth within the vessels, as will be explained; and this is the second aspect that belongs to the Emanator, which is His aspect toward His Sefirot, namely His Self that spreads forth within them; and this aspect receives likeness by means of the Sefirot, like the likeness of the soul that receives form and likeness by means of the body. And he said that even that existence is not fitting to ascribe to His aspect concealed from all His emanated ones, for there is no apprehension of it, and no name, at all. And the measure of the language, "of anything that has in it a likeness," etc., means [the likeness] that is the bounding of the Sefirot, even though it is not [literally] a bound. "You saw" nothing in the Ein Sof; and even though no prophet or seer can reach Keter, how much more so the Ein Sof above. The intent is that they reached, in the grades of Chokhmah, to know the simplicity of the Ein Sof in itself, in the understanding of the intellect, and they discerned that above, in the First Cause, it is impossible to depict by any figure His spreading-forth within the Sefirot, because He is not apprehended by another, as I explained. "But after He made," etc.—the intent is, after He emanated the pure and holy Emanation, that is, the figure of Adam, by way of parable, as explained above in chapter 6 in the passage of Elijah. "He descended there"—meaning, that is His spreading-forth within the Sefirot. "And was called," etc.—meaning, just as the Sefirot are [named], so the light that spreads forth within them is called. "So that they might apprehend Him"—meaning, therefore He spreads forth within them; and the reason is that the whole Emanation itself is only to reveal His Godhead to the lowly, as explained in the Gate of the Reason for the Emanation. "By each and every attribute," etc.—meaning, He spread forth according to His attributes, so that the inhabitants of the world might recognize Him according to His existence in each and every attribute, and His action by means of it. "For were He not to spread forth," etc.—the intent is that, were the grades not to descend to this limit, with the soul, which is the Self, spreading forth within them, they would not recognize the Maker, as explained in the said Gate. "And how would the whole earth is full of His glory be fulfilled?"—this is a second reason that His spreading-forth within all His emanated ones was necessitated: for were He not spreading forth within them, how would "the whole earth is full of His glory" be fulfilled? And this matter will be explained at length in the Gate of the Order of Their Standing, God willing. "Like the likeness of the waters of the sea"—meaning, just as the waters that gather into the vessels, whether long or round or square, will be in the likeness of the vessels, and that likeness and form is not acquired in the water but only while it is there—not intrinsically but accidentally—so the Self that spreads forth into the midst of the Sefirot: the changes and the attributes are not acquired in it intrinsically but accidentally, like the likeness of the spreading-forth of the soul within the body; and the judgment and the mercy are intrinsic to the Sefirot, which are called vessels, and accidental to the Sefirot which are called Self. And the matter is by means of the Sefirot; and after His withdrawal from the Sefirot, no attribute is acquired in Him. "Into what is too wondrous for you do not inquire," etc.—it is already well known that the attribute of Keter is not apprehended even by the Sefirot at all, and therefore it is expounded concerning this Sefirah, "into what is too wondrous," etc. "He made a small vessel"—the intent is to the smallness of the apprehension in it, and therefore it is called "small"; but in the matter of its existence it is greater than the one below it, for it is a cause to all that is beneath it. "And He called it a welling spring of wisdom"—meaning, to His spreading-forth which is within the Sefirot He called "spring," etc. "And that vessel"—meaning, the Sefirah, which is the vessel, He called "Chokhmah," etc. "By it [He is] wise of Himself and understanding of Himself." The intent is to explain to us how He is wise with a wisdom that is His own, and not with a wisdom outside Himself—even though they are vessels—since they are wisdom and understanding only by means of the Self that spreads forth within them, and that Self is the principal Chokhmah and Binah; and accordingly it is found that He is wise with a wisdom that He Himself is the Chokhmah, and understanding with an understanding that He Himself is the Binah, and Chokhmah and Binah are vessels in which His wisdom and His understanding clothe themselves. "And He called Himself Great in Gedulah," etc.—His intent is to explain to us that, although in Him, may He be blessed, the descriptions are not ascribed, since He is utterly simple, without descriptions, with all this, from the side of His uniting with the Sefirot and spreading forth within them, the descriptions were necessitated for Him. And this is "and He called Himself," etc.—meaning, He called Himself "Great" by means of His spreading-forth within Gedulah, etc.; and so for the rest of the Sefirot. "To add to the vessels or to diminish in them"—in the manner explained in the preceding chapter, that the spreading-forth that is within them is what enlarges them, and brings them into a limit, and expands them forever and ever, for they are His vessels, and all is according to His will; which is not so in His Self, the King of the kings of kings, for there is none who overflows to Him, and He overflows to them all. Thus far has reached the force of the words of Moses our Teacher—peace be upon him—with Rashbi—may peace be upon him—and his companions, in a manner direct toward them and revealed to their eyes, as he explained in the Introduction of the Tikkunim, that He grants permission to the heads of the academies that are in the Garden of Eden to gather to them and to engage with them in this wisdom.

And behold, it has been explained from within these passages that the Sefirot are the Self of the Creator, and that He is the soul that spreads forth within the Sefirot, which are vessels; and behold, in this manner the Ein Sof is called "a soul to the souls," for He is a soul to the Sefirot, which are souls to the rest of the effects beneath them; and they are refined, the utmost of refinement, until the intellect cannot liken them to anything in the world, by reason of the abundance of their refinement and their eminence.

After we have agreed, in the matter of the Sefirot, that they are Self and vessels, and the matter has been well explained—that the descriptions in the Ein Sof are not literally in Him, but by means of His Sefirot, as we explained in the preceding chapters—we have gained a fine and pleasant resolution to the great perplexity in which all the philosophers, and most of the later sages of Israel who engage in the externals, were perplexed. And it is that which Rambam, of blessed memory, asked in the Sefer ha-Madda, in Hilkhot Teshuvah, chapter 5, and these are his words: "Perhaps you will say: but does not the Holy One blessed be He know all that will be before it comes to be? Did He know that this one would be righteous or wicked, or did He not know? If He knew that he would be righteous, it is impossible that he should not be righteous; and if you say that He knew he would be righteous and [yet] it is possible that he should be wicked, then He did not know the matter in its fullness." End of his words.

And behold, according to this question, it is impossible to say that the foreknowledge is above and the free will is in the hand of the human being, for the one contradicts the other. And now we have from this no difficulty at all, neither root [nor branch]. And the matter is that they posited foreknowledge in the Creator, and said that He knows, wills, and is able; for although in the rest of the descriptions they are not to be ascribed to Him, these we are compelled [to ascribe]. And so some of the Kabbalists wrote. But I say that, since we said above that the Creator is wise by means of the attribute of Chokhmah and not by a wisdom outside Himself—as we expanded the explanation in the preceding chapters—so we say that Keter is called "Will," and the Creator wills by means of it; and we shall yet be lengthy in this in the Gate of the Tzachtzachot, chapter 6, God willing. And likewise the Creator is able by means of Binah, for it is called "Power," as is known. And He knows by means of Da'at, for the attribute of Da'at is the Creator's knowledge—I mean, that He knows by means of it; and from within it, in the manner we explained above. And so it is proven that this Da'at is His knowledge and His foreknowledge, for so says the verse (Proverbs 3:20), "by His knowledge the depths were split." And it will not be difficult for us [to say] that, accordingly, He and His knowledge are not [literally] one—just as it is not difficult for us that He and Chokhmah are not [literally] one, as was explained above. And now, behold, it is known that the Da'at is Tiferet, as we explained in the third Gate, chapter 8; and it is known that the free will of the human being is from the side of Malkhut, for from it downward are the two ways, and "sin crouches at the door," and it is what is called "free will"; and so it is called "the House of Choice," as is known. And now we say that there is a distinction in the foreknowledge before a person sins—even though he is destined to sin—and after he has sinned: for before he sinned, the knowledge of that sin was in Da'at, but it was not making a blemish or impression above, because he had not yet blemished, nor empowered the outer [forces]. And so too in this manner regarding the supernal foreknowledge with respect to charity and the rest of the commandments: for although it is known above, the commandment does not overflow and does not illumine until he performs it; and this is [the meaning of] (Genesis 22:12) "now I know that you fear God." And the intent is that, although the foreknowledge was above, with all this Tiferet and Malkhut were not uniting and overflowing from the side of that knowledge, for it was in potential; but after it came into actuality and the commandment was performed, behold, the knowledge was in actuality, and Tiferet united with Malkhut by means of it. And this is "now I know," which is a term of knowledge and of joining, like "and the man knew," etc. (Genesis 4:1). And likewise regarding the transgression: that supernal foreknowledge which was in Da'at made no impression, because the Holy One blessed be He judges only [a man] as he is there; but after he has sinned, it makes an impression and a blemish above. And now, after we have known this distinction, we shall further know that Tiferet is the attribute of mercy, and Malkhut the attribute of judgment.

And behold, from the side of Tiferet there is the four-letter Name in direct [order], thus: YHVH; and this Name is called "male," for the male is in the secret of mercy—because this Name strengthens mercy over judgment, that is, the yod, which is Chokhmah, over the heh, which is Binah; this is mercy and that is judgment. And likewise the vav over the heh, that is, Tiferet (vav) strengthens over Malkhut, which is heh. And the yod and the vav are Abba and Son, mercy; and the two hehs are Imma and her daughter—or bride and her mother-in-law—which are from the side of judgment. And Malkhut is the Name in reverse, thus: HVHY; and this is [when] the females rule, and it is judgment. And all this has been explained at length in the Tikkunim, and it will yet be explained in the Gate of the Reversal of the Light. And now we say that, just as it is not far-fetched that judgment should prevail over mercy—even though the Ein Sof Himself judges His creatures by means of them—and likewise that it is not far-fetched that Malkhut should sometimes prevail over Tiferet, even though the Ein Sof clothes Himself in them—so it is not far-fetched that Malkhut, which is the free will, should prevail over Tiferet, which is the foreknowledge and the Da'at. And all the more so, since that foreknowledge makes no impression, as we explained; for after an impression has been made, repentance is needed, which is Binah, which is higher.

And behold, the free will will prevail over the foreknowledge in other commandments that a person performs, and he will not sin. And by this may be understood what they said, of blessed memory (in tractate Avodah Zarah, fol. 4[b]), "Israel were not fit for that deed," etc.; and likewise David was not fit for that deed—that is, by means of their making the free will prevail over the foreknowledge. Further, we have gained much doubled good concerning the matter that was difficult for the commentators in the explanation of Rabbi Menachem. According to his view, since the Sefirot are subject to change and limit—even though it is not literally a limit, but in the manner explained in the preceding Gates—if so, how is it possible that the Ein Sof, though removed from this matter to the utmost remove, should join with them and accompany those subject to changes? And in truth this is more and more difficult upon the view of Rashbi—may peace be upon him—who explained above that the very Self of the Godhead literally spreads forth within the Sefirot: how is it possible to say that two opposite things were united, since the Ein Sof is devoid of descriptions and opposites and changes and limit, and the Sefirot possess these matters—and how is it possible to say that the Ein Sof and the Sefirot are all one thing? So much so that some of the commentators said that the matter of His binding and union in the Sefirot is concealed and exalted, just as there is concealed from us also the existence of the union and binding of the soul with the body—even though the body is coarse and thick, possessing the corporeal desires and the rest of the things ascribed to it, while the soul is devoid of the natures of the body and its accidents, and is a refined and spiritual being; if so, how is it possible that they should be united? Rather, surely they are united, and their manner is exalted and concealed from the eye of the created beings, and the eyes of the sages have grown dim from comprehending this matter. And if the soul that is within us is thus, then how shall we have any engagement with the hidden things? This is the sum of their view in the matter. But for us this answer is not sufficient, for the existence of the binding of the soul with the body is explained for us, and it is among the simple matters of this wisdom, as will be explained in the Gate of the Soul; for there is a great affinity of the soul with the body, such that their union and binding is no wonder. And so we say in the matter of the Sefirot and the Ein Sof, blessed be He. For the Ein Sof has attributes; and if they are not attributes in relation to Himself, they are attributes in relation to the created beings. For it is known that He is wise of Himself and great of Himself; and yet, to guide the created beings, He had to display His action to another. And since this is so, He had to emanate an Emanation, and to bring it about in such a way that the greatness and the Chesed would act in this world; and moreover He had to [arrange] that the governance be by means of Him specifically, not by means of another. And if so, in His love for the creation He had to emanate a vessel for His work, such that that Chesed would be united with His piety, and the Gevurah with His might, and His judgment with His being a Judge. And therefore it is found that all the matters of Chesed are ascribed to the Chesed which is the Self; and the Chesed which is the Self, in order to perform its action, needs the Chesed which is the vessel; and the Chesed which is the vessel needs the Chesed which is the Self; and they are united in the utmost union. And it is "like that locust whose garment is of its own [body]"—for the garment without it is a dumb stone, and it, without a garment, has no means for its actions. And so it is with the matter of the Sefirot.

And behold, just as the questioner will not ask, and will not wonder, at the choice speaking creature [the human] that accompanies the garments, which are lacking in perfection, of base worth, of worn-out rags—because he sees that a person is ascribed to those garments, so that even the abstinent do not wholly remove themselves from them, as in the matter of "bread to eat and clothing to wear" that Jacob our father—peace be upon him—requested (Genesis 28:20), though he was the choicest of the secluded contemplatives of his generation, to the point that he drove sleep from his eyes for twenty years—so it should be no wonder, in the supernal matters, that they should be a need of the Godhead, and a union of the Godhead with them; for they are a supernal need, for the governance of the lowly. Even though it is true that the Emanation was not for a need that He had of them, God forbid, but only a benefaction that His attribute freely bestowed, to do good to another, and not that He was compelled—but only by will and love; and this matter, too, will be explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, God willing.
