And it remains incumbent upon us to explain a mighty question that falls under the category of the inquiry with which we have engaged in this Gate, and it is this: that, if it is true—as it is, beyond doubt—that the Creator, the King of the kings of kings, has no change at all, and does not change from matter to matter; and likewise He is not subject to composition, God forbid, for He is simple, and His simplicity is not like the simplicity of the angels, the separate intelligences, for they are contingent beings, and there was a time when they did not exist, as is proven in the words of the Sages, of blessed memory (in Bereshit Rabbah, ch. 3), and especially in Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer, where he alluded that the angels were created on the second day—and if so, they are contingent beings; and from this side is their composition, for they are composed of privation and existence—which is not so with God, who is one, simple, the utmost of simplicity, necessary of existence, and His existence neither lacks nor exceeds; and were the cessation of all created beings to be imagined, no deficiency would reach Him on that account, God forbid; and were their multiplication imagined, He would not be multiplied on that account, God forbid; and were the cessation of all created beings imagined, they would perish and He would stand. And since these premises are true, and fit to be like nails driven into the heart of the believers, how can we restrain ourselves before the modest ones, the masters of [divine] service, who say that the Sefirot are His Self, and that they are emanated from some time—be it much or little? According to their view, there was already a time when they were not in existence; if so, they are contingent beings, and behold, from this side they are composite, like the composition of the angels—and this is contrary to the true faith. And it is true that one can answer this in the manner in which some of the commentators wished to answer, and they said that the coming-to-be and the Emanation is not from the side of the Emanator, for the Emanation itself was concealed in His Self, in the best, most refined, and most excellent potential of the Agent; but now they were revealed and went forth from potential to actuality, and this is a coming-to-be in relation to the created beings, and not in relation to the Emanator. And this matter will suffice to say that the Emanation is no coming-to-be in relation to the Emanator, who is the Self of the simple Ein Sof. But as for the existence of the Emanation itself, namely the Sefirot, which are His Self as I explained, surely we shall not deny that, even though they were concealed, with all this this existence of theirs—which is the existence of their spreading-forth—did not exist. If so, we say that they are contingent of this existence; and since this existence is contingent—for it is possible that it should be and possible that it should not be—even we say that they are not like the existence of God at all, for God is necessary of existence. And now, to repair and settle this matter, let us set forth a fine parable, ascribed to the Emanation, and it is: that a person should depict in his mind a great fire, in the utmost [degree], and from the abundance of the brilliance of its light and the intensity of its heat—if some formed thing should be depicted within that fire, would it not be scorched and perish in an instant?

And behold, He brought into being within it, and brought about by means of it, by the abundance of His power, by His will, a sphere that conceals the fire from all its sides, so that the light should not be revealed at all; and even though that sphere is not of the very self of the fire, nonetheless the light that shines in the sphere and governs it is the bright light prior to the existence of the sphere, and its existence did not change, except that its light was somewhat withheld from what it had been, by reason of the sphere; and there is no change to the light and to the heat, but only to the sphere. Further, He saw in His wisdom that if, within the first sphere, there should come to be a being that arises in His will to come to be, it would not be able to subsist, and the intent would not go forth into actuality, by reason of the abundance of the brilliance of the light and the heat of the fire. Therefore He had to bring into being a sphere within the sphere, so that each and every one of them should conceal the light and the brilliance of the great fire, which warms and illumines toward the surface of the spheres, inward—until the spheres reached the number of ten. And afterward He further brought into being within them spheres, from ten to ten, all of them spheres, garments, and screens to the light and the heat that comes from the roots of the great fire, and chains down by way of the spheres and clothes itself in them, until the inner Creation—which is the middle one, and which is in truth the most external—is able to bear a light, and a sweet heat, equal to its temperament, that will benefit it and not harm it.

And behold, all this is not by reason of the light and the heat, but by reason of the weakness of that Creation, which cannot bear the light and the heat that flows from the fire without intermediaries. And we shall not say that by means of the intermediaries the light and the heat changed, in relation to the heat and light [themselves]; for the first heat and light is the last, and in relation to the existence of the light and the heat themselves, it never changed. And the change is in relation to those spheres and screens, which change and descend, and by reason of which the brilliance of the light does not reach them as at its source.

And behold, the light and the heat that spreads forth within the spheres did not come to be with the coming-to-be of the spheres; rather, on the contrary, it preceded them, as the great fire—which is the source of the light and the heat—precedes [them]; and only the spheres and the vessels that thicken its light came to be, in relation to themselves, not in relation to the light and the heat, whose power then is its power now. And on the contrary, beforehand its light reached a more revealed and more excellent existence than this, except that the spheres clothed it and concealed it. And now, behold, the great fire is the Ein Sof, the King of the kings of kings; and it is the thing signified, here, in the parable of the great fire, by the likeness of some of the properties [of fire], as the commentators were lengthy. And the spheres are the Sefirot, the vessels. And the light and the heat that spreads forth within them is His Self [may He be exalted, the concealed One that spreads forth within the Sefirot—from Asis Rimonim], which is a soul to the soul, and gives life to the Sefirot, and enlarges them and strengthens them, and gives them the power to stand and to serve.

And behold, the light and the heat did not come to be and did not change, except in relation to the renewed vessels. But in relation to the light itself, there is no coming-to-be and no change, for the soul existed beforehand. But in relation to the vessels, He brought into being for them a place in His Self, so that by means of them the living [vessels] might bear the power of His Godhead. Thus far has reached the parable and the thing signified.

And behold, this inquiry has been explained with a fine explanation. And to be lengthy in this is iniquity and guilt; and our intent is only for the honor of the Omnipresent, to establish faith in the heart of the discerning. And when they look upon these our words with good consideration, in this parable, there will be understood and discerned from within it several things sweeter than honey; and the brevity is fine; and may God forgive.

Behold, the intent in this chapter is only to cite a passage of Rashbi—may peace be upon him—that reveals the matter of the attributes in all the facets of the inquiry with which we have engaged in the preceding chapters; and from within it some of the passages that Rabbi David brought to compel his view will be explained. And these are the words of [Rashbi] in the Ra'aya Mehemna (Pinchas, fol. 257b), [on] the thirteenth commandment, the recitation of the Shema: And one must know that He is called "wise" in all kinds of wisdom, and "understanding" in all kinds of understanding, and "pious" in all kinds of pieties, and "mighty" in all kinds of mighty deeds, and "counselor" in all kinds of counsels, and "righteous" in all kinds of righteousness, and "king" in all kinds of kingship—up to the Ein Sof (another reading: up to Keter)—and up to that which has no investigating. And in these grades, by one He is called "merciful" and by one "judge"; and so in several grades, up to the Ein Sof. If so, is there a change between "merciful" and "judge"? Rather, before He created the world, He was called by all these grades on account of the creatures that were destined to be created; for were there no creatures of the world, why would He be called "merciful," "judge"? Rather, on account of the creatures that were destined [to be]. And therefore all the Names are His allusions, after His deeds. In like manner He created the soul in His image, which is called after its actions in each and every limb of the body, which is called "a small world" [microcosm]. And just as the Master of the world is governed in all creatures and in each and every generation according to their deeds, so the soul [is named] according to its deeds in each and every limb: that limb in which it performs a commandment, the soul is called, in relation to it, "compassion," and "lovingkindness," "favor," and "mercy"; and that limb in which it performs a transgression, the soul is called, in relation to it, "judgment," and "wrath," and "anger." But outside the body, toward whom would there be compassion or cruelty? So too the Master of the world, before He created the world and created His creatures—toward whom would He be called "merciful" and "gracious," or "judge"? Rather, all His Names are allusions, and [yet] not allusions; and He is called by them only on account of the creatures of the world. And therefore, when the masters of the generation are good, He is called toward them "YHVH," in the attribute of mercy; and when the generation are guilty, He is called "Adonai," in the attribute of judgment—to each generation and to each human being according to his measure. But not that He has a [fixed] attribute or a known name. In like manner to the Sefirot: for each Sefirah has a known name, and has an attribute and a bound and a border; and by these names the Master of the world spreads forth, and reigns in them, and is called by them, and is concealed in them, and dwells in them, like a soul in all the limbs of the body. And just as the Master of the worlds has no known name and no known place, but rather His dominion is on every side, so too the soul has no known name and no known place in the whole body, but its dominion is on every side, and there is no limb empty of it. And therefore one may not mark it in one place; for were one [to do so], its dominion would be lacking in the rest of the limbs. Nor [may one] call it by one name, or by two, or by three—to say of it that it is "Chokhmah," and "Binah," and that it has "Da'at," and no more; for were one to do so, behold, it would be lacking from the rest of the grades. How much more so the Master of the world, whom one may not mark in a known place, nor call by known names, nor make Him two by them, nor make Him three by them—like the grade of the Chariot, of which it is said "they shall make threefold the holiness to You"; for all His grades and Chariots, all of them are threefold, like the Patriarchs, who are the Chariot—for they are the likeness of lion, ox, eagle, and they are a Chariot to "Adam," of whom it is said, "and the likeness of their faces was the face of a man"; and from the side of the female they rule over "Adam," and the female is a Chariot to them; and therefore it is said of it, "they shall make threefold the holiness to You." In like manner the letters, which are the faces of the living creatures, are threefold, thus: YHV, HVY, VHY—the fourth heh: "they shall make threefold the holiness to You," it [the fourth] is the completion of them all, to complete by them the Name YHVH. But the Master of all—one may not make Him threefold by names or by letters; rather, He is called by all the names, and He has no known name, and each and every name testifies of Him: that He is Lord over all the worlds, the name Adonai testifies of Him. And there is none who knows that there is a person who inherits three hundred and ten worlds—this is [the meaning of] "to endow those who love Me with substance (yesh)," according to his grade, which is called "substance from nothing," and this is the supernal Chokhmah. And there is a person who inherits only one world, according to his grade, as we have established, "each and every righteous one has a world of his own"; and so every human being of Israel inherits worlds according to his grade above. But the Master of the world—one may not mark for Him worlds in number, but rather He is Lord over all worlds, and Adonai testifies of Him. So too YHVH: from it depend all the Tetragrammaton-forms, and it and all its Tetragrammaton-forms testify of the Master of the world, that He was before all the Tetragrammaton-forms, and He is within every Tetragrammaton-form, and He is after every Tetragrammaton-form; and this is the secret of the Tetragrammaton-forms testifying of Him: "was, is, and will be." Judgment, in the reversal of the letters, is Adonai; and therefore the Sages, of blessed memory, said, "the law of the kingdom is law." The name El testifies of the Master of all, that there is no capacity in any name and Tetragrammaton-form and grade—how much more so in the rest of the creatures lesser than it—this is [the meaning of] "and all the inhabitants of the earth are reckoned as nothing, and according to His will He acts in the host of heaven," etc. Elohim testifies of His Godhead, that He is Elohim, and the God of gods, and He is God over all, and there is no god above Him. Tzeva'ot testifies, as it is said, "and according to His will He acts in the host of heaven." Shaddai testifies of Him, that when He said to His world "Enough!" it stood within its border and its bound, and did not spread forth further—and so too to the water, and the wind, and the fire. And so too every name and Tetragrammaton-form testifies of Him: that when He was one, before He created the world, why would He need to be called by these names, or by the rest of the allusions, such as "merciful," "gracious," "long-suffering," etc., "judge," "powerful," "mighty"? And by many of all these names and allusions He is called, on account of all the worlds and their creatures, to show His dominion over them. So too the soul: in relation to its dominion over all the limbs of the body, it is likened to Him—not that it is comparable to Him in itself, for He created it, and there is no god above Him who created Him.

And further, the soul has several changes and accidents and causes that are ascribed to it, which is not so for the Master of all; and therefore it is likened to Him in its dominion over all the limbs of the body, but not in any other matter. End of his words.

And from within it are explained all the parts and sides of the inquiry expounded in this Gate. And now it is our wish to be lengthy in its explanation and in the details of his words, by reason of the abundance of its usefulness.

And further, from within it will be explained most of what we explained in the preceding chapters. And the meaning of "wise in all kinds of wisdom" is because there are many aspects to Chokhmah and Binah, and they are "kinds of wisdom" according to the change and multiplicity of the aspects; and within them all the Ein Sof spreads forth, in order to perform all the actions, for the attributes have no power to perform an action apart from Him. And he said "up to the Ein Sof." The meaning is that all His actions are not like the actions of the attributes themselves, because the actions of the attributes have a limit and an end, according to the apprehension of each and every attribute in the Self that spreads forth into the Sefirot; but the Self that spreads forth into the Sefirot has no end to its actions. And the reason he did not mention Keter at all is because in Keter there is no attribute and no action at all, and it is only a throne and a palace to the Ein Sof, by means of which the Emanation and the Self spread forth within the vessels.

And behold, Keter is a source and a cause to the vessels, and the Ein Sof is a source [and] cause to the Self; and the two of them spread forth as one, the Emanator clothing Himself in the emanated. And for this reason the first emanated [Keter] has no action at all, and the beginning of action is from Chokhmah. "And counselor in all kinds of counsels"—that is, in Netzach and Hod, which are "kidneys that counsel," and by means of the overflowing of the counsel in the supernal court—that is, in the partnership of Tiferet with them, for the principal counsel is from it. And his saying "that He is called," that is, to ascribe the attributes to the Self of the Ein Sof. And this is "and in these grades by one He is called," etc.—that is, that the Self of the Ein Sof is so called by means of the attributes, as will be explained. "By one He is called merciful"—and the intent is "merciful" from the side of the right, and "judge" from the side of the left, that is, the change from judgment to mercy and from mercy to judgment. And therefore he raised the difficulty, how there could be the change. And by this two things are difficult: one, that He has descriptions; the second, that He is subject to changes. And if you say that this is in the aspect of the created beings—

behold, it is difficult that, before the creation of the created beings, He was not called "merciful" and "judge"—and this is a great forced reading, to say that allusions came to be in Him with the coming-to-be of human beings. And therefore he answered that the allusions and the attributes and the changes are forever from the side of human beings, who are acted upon by Him by means of the attributes; and also before the creation of the created beings He was called by these allusions, after the names of the attributes concealed within Him—like the concealment of the flame in the coal, and like the concealment of the fire in the flint—as we shall explain in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, God willing. And He was called "merciful" and "judge" after [the fact] that, in the emanating and spreading-forth of the attributes by means of them, He performs the mercy and the judgment. And this is [the meaning of] "Rather, before He created the world," etc., "for were there no creatures," etc. He compelled [the point] that the descriptions are not from His side but from the side of the created beings—[both] the matter of the descriptions themselves, and likewise the changes; for the allusions are "judge" and "merciful" and the like, and likewise the changes from judgment to mercy and from mercy to judgment; and behold, this matter is necessarily from the side of the created beings, not from His side—meaning, from the side of His aspect before the spreading-forth of the Emanation; for otherwise, how would "merciful" and "judge" be apt of Him—toward whom would He be merciful, and whom would He judge? Rather, what have you to say? That it is applicable only from the side of the spreading-forth of the Emanation and the creation of the created beings. And this is what he said, "for were there no creatures in the world, why would He be called," etc. "And therefore all the Names," etc.—meaning, granted, we have compelled [the point] with respect to the allusions "merciful" and "gracious," which are actions going forth to another, acted from Him toward another; but with respect to "wise" and "understanding" and the rest of the names and allusions, which stand alone in themselves and do not go forth to another, we have no compelling [argument], and we might forever say that they are in Himself, and that He is, after all, a possessor of descriptions and changes. And to this he answered "and therefore"—meaning, since we are compelled to say of some of them that, by means of His uniting with the attributes to act upon human beings, they are those descriptions, even we shall say so of all the rest of the allusions and names, for some of them disclose [the nature of] the others. And this is what he said, "and therefore all the Names," etc.: though they stand alone, they are allusions to Him after the [His] actions. And it is possible that the intent in saying "after His deeds" is His Sefirot, which are His works, and that by means of His Sefirot are His allusions. And the matter is that, before the spreading-forth of the attributes, He was wise in His Self, and His wisdom was in the apprehension of His Self, for He and His wisdom are all one Self; but His wisdom spread forth into the vessel of Chokhmah, to make another wise, and likewise in Binah; and forever, that which spreads forth in Chokhmah and Binah is His Self, which is the source of Chokhmah and Binah. "In like manner He created the soul"—behold, the parable of the soul that we set forth in chapter 4, and it is a fitting parable, that the soul has no corporeal actions—to say, from this aspect it sees and from this aspect it hears—and yet, in conjunction with the body, it acts in the action of the body according to the preparedness of its limbs: there is a limb in which it sees, and a limb in which it hears. And so is the matter with the Ein Sof, who is a soul to the souls: in His conjunction with the attributes, the attributes perform those changes by His power, just as the body acts by the power of the soul. And this is what he said, "He created the soul in His image, which is called after its actions," as explained: that the names of the corporeal actions are ascribed to the soul, because, by means of its conjunction with the body, the actions are performed, as explained. "That limb in which it performs a commandment," etc.—this whole matter is to ascribe the judgment and the mercy to the soul, as in the matter of the Ein Sof. And this is because the human being comprises, in his creation, all the existents, all of them, from the first point to the end of Creation and Formation and Action, as it is written (Isaiah 43:7), "I created it, I formed it, indeed I made it"; and corresponding to the Ein Sof, who spreads forth and illumines and gives life from the beginning of all to the end, so is the soul in the body. And therefore, by means of the body it has actions, and outside the body it has no actions, as in the matter of the Ein Sof, as explained. And therefore there is no parable more fitting than the parable of the soul. And this is what he said, "So too the Master of the world," etc., "allusions and not allusions"—meaning, they are allusions from the side of [His] conjunction with the attributes, and they are not allusions from His own side, for in Him there is no attribute, and no description, and no action. "And by these names," etc.—meaning, they are ten Sefirot, ten names; for the names are the Sefirot, and the Sefirot are the names. "He spreads forth"—that is, the spreading-forth of His Self within the names and the Sefirot. "And reigns in them"—for they have no action except from His side, for He reigns in them according to His will, and by means of Him is their action. "And is called by them"—for by this He is called by them; but not that the names are apt of Him from His own side, but rather from the side that He reigns in them, as explained. "And is concealed in them"—for the Emanation is by reason of the revelation of the Emanator; and likewise "and is called by them," for He has no name and place by which to call Him or to utter Him, except by means of His actions, and this is the cause of His revelation; and likewise they are the cause of His concealment and His covering, so that His Godhead should be revealed only to the fitting; and these are screens dividing between Him and the lower ones. And this is [the point] that the revelation is the cause of the concealment, and the concealment is the cause of the revelation. "And dwells in them," etc.—that is, that the Sefirot and the names, the emanated ones, are a garment to the Emanator, as is known. "And therefore one may not mark it," etc., "how much more so the Master of the world," etc.—to say that He is revealed in Keter and in Chokhmah and the like, for if so, He would diminish His dominion and His actions. And this is what he said, "for were one to do so, behold it would be lacking from the rest of the grades; how much more so the Master of the world," etc. And it is difficult, for in several places in the Zohar it is implied that, when His providence withdraws from the attributes, the world perishes and is consumed in an instant; and according to his words, behold, at the time of His withdrawal He is "lacking His dominion." And one cannot say that "to be lacking His dominion" and "to withdraw His providence" forever is what we said is not fitting, but that for a time it is possible that He withdraws His providence—because, if so, after all, at that time a deficiency would be necessitated, God forbid. For when He withdraws His providence from Malkhut, by reason that it performs judgment, then He would not be called "King," and the Godhead would be found lacking the allusion of kingship; and this is not fitting, for He has no change, neither addition nor diminution, in His allusions and His attributes—from the reason and the great principle that they are ten and not nine, ten and not eleven. And from this reason it is forbidden for us to add to the Sefirot or to diminish from them, because they are the limbs of a supernal form; and with the addition of the limbs one is found adding to their soul, and likewise when one diminishes one of them, God forbid. Rather, surely this is no answer. And the principal answer is as we shall explain in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 3: that the kinds of effluence are three. And the first is the perpetual [effluence], which neither lacks nor exceeds, and it is the Self that spreads forth, which gives life to the attribute; for even though that attribute should clothe itself in harsh judgment, its perpetual effluence is never lacking—for otherwise, even in judgment it would not be acting, but would be like a vessel in which there is no desire, and it would be as though it were not, God forbid; rather, by reason of its soul that overflows in it perpetually, it performs everything. But the intensification that intensifies upon this matter, in order to raise the attribute, and enlarge it, and equalize it to the supernal one, and the like—this is what sometimes withdraws, God forbid; and this is what is explained in the said Gate, in the matter of the three kinds of effluence. Which is not so in the attributes, for there is an attribute whose light spreads forth up to such-and-such a place, and there is [one] up to such-and-such a place—as he concludes, that there is a fourfold Chariot and there is a threefold Chariot. But in the Ein Sof it is not so; rather, "in all is He," and as he explains, "He is called by all the names," because they all draw from Him and have no existence apart from Him; and yet the names are not acquired in Him. And this is what he said, "and He has no known name." Or he means that He has no special name, but rather He spreads forth in them all, as he concludes. "That there is a person who inherits," etc.—the intent is to the soul, which is not comparable to the Ein Sof, God forbid; for above there is a soul that inherits three hundred and ten (yesh) worlds, which is Chokhmah—that is, the soul that merited to ascend to that grade; and there is a soul that merits only [the level] corresponding to the Righteous One, Foundation of the world, and has only one world, that is, in the secret of the inclusiveness of the attributes. For in relation to each and every part of the inclusiveness of Yesod, the soul has three hundred and ten (yesh) inclusivenesses and aspects.

And behold, the soul has a reckoning of three hundred and ten (yesh) worlds in which it spreads forth; but the Ein Sof is called "Adonai," meaning Lord over all the existence of worlds, up to the Ein Sof. And this is the import of the name Adnut [lordship]. And the Name of four letters indicates that He was prior to every Tetragrammaton-form, meaning that He is the essence of the Tetragrammaton-forms, and He is the cause prior to them, like the priority of the cause to the effect. "And He is within every Tetragrammaton-form"—He is the cause of every Tetragrammaton-form, and its subsistence, and its life, and without Him it has no existence; and He is the soul of the Tetragrammaton-forms and their subsistence. "And He is after every Tetragrammaton-form"—that is, that He is their end, at the time when He will gather His spirit and His soul to Himself. It is found that He is the soul of all the Tetragrammaton-forms, and He is their subsistence, and He is the end of all the Tetragrammaton-forms. And this is the secret of "the Tetragrammaton-forms testifying of Him: was," etc.—meaning, the Name of four letters comprises "was, is, and will be" (hayah, hoveh, ve-yihyeh), for these three words are combined from the letters of the Name; and this is the secret of the combined twelve-lettered [Name], which we shall explain in the Gate of the Particulars of the Names, in chapter 9. "El testifies," etc.—that is, that the word "El" is a term of power and strength, as in "and the mighty of the land he took" (Ezekiel 17:13), and "Your righteousness is like the mighty mountains" (Psalms 36:7), and many others like them. "Elohim testifies," etc. And because He is God over all the emanated ones, He is called "Elohim," which is close to a plural form; and this is what he was precise about in his language, saying "that He is Elohim and the God of gods." "Tzeva'ot testifies," etc.—meaning, that He is called "Tzeva'ot" because He is a prince over all hosts (tzeva'ot), to do with them according to His will, as it is written (Daniel 4:32), "and according to His will," etc. "Shaddai," etc.—indicates that He said to the world "Enough!" (dai), that is, to the lower world, the foundation of the earth, and so too to the rest of the elements. And he is lengthy in all this to teach that all the Names are only from the side of the actions that flow from Him for the need of the created beings. But from the side of the aspect of His Self, there is no need for names at all; and there is not in Him any name among the holy Names, how much more so allusions, which literally indicate actions, as he sets forth and proceeds. Thus far has our understanding reached in this delightful inquiry, according as it was poured forth upon us from Heaven. And of the One exalted above all blessing and praise we ask forgiveness and atonement for opening the doors of our lips, for all is for His honor and for the honor of His Name. And this Gate is herewith concluded. And after the Lord has helped us up to here, we journey onward to the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, with the help of Heaven.
The Fifth Gate: The Order of the Emanation

The intent in this Gate is to explain in what manner these Sefirot were emanated, and the matter of their emanation according to their divisions. And the order of their standing will be explained in a separate Gate, with the help of Heaven.
Chapter One:

After we have pursued the matter of the order of the emanation of the Sefirot—as a reader pursues [a path] in the mountains—we found that Rav Sherira Gaon wrote the order of their emanation, and Rabbi Shem Tov ben Shem Tov copied his language in the Sefer ha-Emunot, Gate 4, chapter 11. And these are his words: The first emanation, Keter, etc. The second emanation, Avir [air], which is Chokhmah, etc. The third emanation, Mada [knowledge]—and the mnemonic is "discerning, and he shall know them" (Hosea 14:10)—which is Tevunah [understanding], etc. The fourth emanation is the right arm—and the mnemonic is "long-suffering and abundant in lovingkindness" (Psalms 145:8)—and it is Chesed. The fifth emanation, the left arm—and the mnemonic is "Yours is an arm with might" (ibid. 89:14). The sixth emanation, the central pillar—and the mnemonic is "behold, You desire truth in the inward parts," etc. (ibid. 51:8). The seventh emanation, the everlasting covenant—and the mnemonic is "righteousness calls it to its foot" (Isaiah 41:2), meaning that Malkhut is called "righteousness" [tzedek], receiving from the Righteous One [tzaddik], Foundation of the world. The eighth emanation, the right thigh—and the mnemonic is "pleasures in Your right hand forever (netzach)" (Psalms 16:11). The ninth emanation, the left thigh—and the mnemonic is "His footstool" (Lamentations 2:1). The tenth emanation, the daughter-voice [bat kol]—and the mnemonic is "all glorious is the king's daughter within" (Psalms 45:14). This is the sum of the secret of the ten crowns that the heads of the academies received, etc. End of his words.

And he was very lengthy, and we have abbreviated, by reason of [the maxim] "a person should always teach his students by a short way." But what appears from the explanation of his words is that they were emanated one after another, in order; and this he was precise about in saying "the first emanation, the second, and the third." And so it is proven from several places where we have seen Rashbi—may peace be upon him—counting the order of the Sefirot as KaChaB, ChaGaT, NeHiYaM. And so it is proven from the verse (Job 28[:12]), "but Chokhmah—from where is it found?"—he disclosed in [this] explanation that Chokhmah is emanated and found from "Nothing," which is Keter. And afterward it says, "and where is the place of Binah?"—meaning, Alef-Yod (A-Y), that is, Chokhmah, which is yod, in partnership with Keter, which is alef, is the place and the existence of Binah—indicating the order of these three. And likewise King David, peace be upon him, said (I Chronicles 29[:11]), "Yours, O YHVH, is the greatness, and the might, and the glory, and the victory (netzach), and the majesty (hod), for all (kol)"—which is Yesod, that "grasps in heaven and on earth," and so the Targum renders—and afterward it says "Yours, O YHVH, is the kingship," that is, Malkhut.

Behold, he has proven the order of the emanation. And so it is necessitated that the order of their emanation is one after another, and no more. For it is impossible to say that two were emanated [at once], since each one is a cause to its fellow; if so, it is necessitated that the cause precede the effect. And therefore they were emanated one after another; for were it not so, one Sefirah would be found a cause to two—and this is impossible, for then they would be equal, meaning that, since both are effects of one cause, the two effects are equal; and since they are equal, then by what would they be distinguished? For that which is not a body is not divided into parts. If so, of necessity they are effects one from another, and there are not two effects [emanated] together equally. And surely the words of the Gaon are correct, and they accord with the words of Rashbi in the flow of his language in the Zohar, in his numberings in the order of one after another; and never does a Tanna omit to put Chokhmah before Keter, nor Binah before Chokhmah, and so the rest—indicating their union one with another. And both the Gaon and the Tanna agree and are correct with the verses we explained above, indicating the truth of the matter. And in addition to this, the reasonings and the true premises are agreed upon even according to the words of the investigators. And if so, we have proven clearly that the order of the Sefirot is thus: the first emanation, Keter; and from Keter was emanated, etc.; and Malkhut is the end of the emanation. And what is to be examined closely in the language of the Gaon is what he wrote, "the seventh emanation, the everlasting covenant," etc., the intent being upon Yesod. And it is known that Yesod is ninth, below Netzach and Hod, according to what is agreed in most of the verses explicitly, and especially in what we wrote, that he said "and the victory and the majesty, for all (kol)"—first Netzach and Hod, and afterward Yesod, that is, "for all (kol)," as explained. And likewise most of the sayings of Rashbi—may peace be upon him—in the Tikkunim and in the Zohar, as we have already copied in the preceding Gates some sayings indicating this matter. But while we were gathering lilies and roses in the field of the divine Chokhmah and Kabbalah from Rashbi—may peace be upon him—the Lord brought before us a saying in which he took this way, and by it all will be rectified, with the help of Heaven; and we shall set it as a separate chapter, to give space between one chapter and another.

And these are the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 69, fol. 102b): "Open for me" (Song of Songs 5:2) on the first day, which is the right, of which it is said "You open Your hand," etc. (Psalms 145:16)—"Your hands" (yadeikha) [is read] "Your yods" (yodeikha), this is the yod, which is to the right. "My sister" on the second day, where the heh is. "My dove" on the third day, where the vav is. "For my head is filled with dew" (SoS 5:2) on the fourth day, which is the combination of Yod-Heh-Vav, which is the reckoning of [the word] tal [dew, = 39]; and this is body and covenant, which are reckoned as one in [their] reckoning, which is vav, ascending to one (echad). The upper vav is the central pillar; the lower vav is the Righteous One. The alef shows concerning the two of them that they are one. "My locks"—these are the six extremities, which are the heh, six segments comprised within the two thighs, which are the fifth day and the sixth day, of which it is said "his thighs are pillars of marble (shesh)" (SoS 5:15). "The drops of the night"—this is the lower Shekhinah, the combination of Yod-Heh-Vav-Heh. And why is she called "night"? Because she is the night of the Sabbath; a night of watching she surely is, unto YHVH. End [of quotation].

And behold, in this saying he indicated explicitly that Yesod is adjacent to Tiferet, above Netzach and Hod; and this is surely a great forced reading, and the opposite of his great [view] in most of the sayings. And we shall explain his language, and from within it all will be rectified, blessed be He. "Open for me," etc.—above this saying he explained that Tiferet is the husband of the Shekhinah, who is the beloved knocking at the door of his desired one; and he said that he comes comprised of six extremities, which are the six days of Creation. And now he explains the matter of his being comprised within them, and his explanation is in the verse. And he said that the intent of "open for me" is in Chesed, which is the right, and it is the first day, as is well known. And because, at first glance, the opening has no relation to Chesed—but rather, on the contrary, there is the place of the closing-up and the sealing, in the manner of the kametz, which is in Chesed (and it is a full verse, "and the priest shall take a handful" [ve-kamatz])—therefore he necessitated the matter by the verse "You open Your hand"; and the word "Your hands" means "Your yods," that is, the yod indicates that the existence of the opening is in the place of the yod, that is, in Chesed, in the secret of Chokhmah, which sets its dwelling upon it, as the Sages, of blessed memory, said (Bava Batra, fol. 25): "one who wishes to become wise should turn southward."

And the matter of "and the priest shall take a handful" will be explained in the Gate of the Vowel-Points. "My sister on the second day"—meaning Gevurah, which is the second day, as is well known. And because it was difficult for him that the word "my sister" does not indicate the existence of Gevurah at all, therefore he explained and said "where the heh is," meaning that in Gevurah is the dwelling of Binah, which is the first heh of the Name. And because the existence of Tiferet is by means of Binah—in the manner explained, "He established the heavens by understanding" (Proverbs 3:19)—and from there Malkhut is called "heh," as will be explained, blessed be He, therefore he said that, since the dwelling of Binah, which is heh, is in Gevurah, and from there Malkhut is heh, and from there "He established the heavens by Binah," if so, it is found that from the side of Gevurah, in the secret of Binah, Tiferet and Malkhut are siblings; and therefore from the side of Gevurah he called her "his sister."

And behold, now the word "my sister" is related in the secret of Gevurah. "My dove on the third day, where the vav is"—meaning, she is called "dove" from the side of Tiferet itself, which is the third day, as is known. And to understand the relation of "my dove" to Tiferet, we need [to refer] to what he explained in another place (Tikkun 6, fol. 23): and these are his words: "The supernal Imma nests in the Throne, in the three upper Sefirot. The central pillar comprises six Sefirot, [which] nest in Metatron. The lower Imma nests in the Ophan, of which it is said (Ezekiel 1:15), 'and behold, one Ophan upon the earth.'"

"And further, the Shekhinah, from the side of the Throne, is called nesher [eagle]; and from the side of na'ar [the youth], yonah [dove]; and from the side of the Ophan, tzippor [bird]." End [of quotation], as relevant to our matter. And we shall not trouble ourselves with the explanation of this saying, for it will be explained at length in the Gate of ABYA. And what comes out for us from his words, toward his intent, is that the Shekhinah is called "dove" from the side of na'ar, since Tiferet, comprised of six extremities, dwells there. And for this reason he said, in the case before us, "my dove," from the side of the third day, which is Tiferet; and he said "where the vav is," the intent being to explain that it comprises six extremities, for it is what is signified by the vav. And it is possible to say that the reason he said, in [the case of] Gedulah, "where the yod is," and in Gevurah "where the heh is," and in Tiferet "where the vav is," is a preparation toward his intent below, upon the verse that said (SoS 5:2), "for my head is filled with dew (tal)," which is the fourth day, that is, Yesod—for the matter of tal is the combination of Yod-Heh-Vav—to indicate that he was compelled to count Yesod adjacent to ChaGaT, which are [the gematria] tal; and this is because Yesod is filled with the effluence of tal, which is YHV [=] ChaGaT. "Filled with dew on the fourth day," the intent being upon Yesod, as we explained. "The combination of Yod-Heh-Vav," the intent being that there the effluence of the three Patriarchs—which are the three letters YHV—is made to overflow; and it is also called kol [all] because it comprises all. And therefore he said "which is the combination," meaning the combination of the three letters, which are the three Patriarchs. "And this is body and covenant, which are reckoned," etc. It was difficult for him [what] was difficult for us in the words of Rav Sherira, of blessed memory: that he should have said first Netzach and Hod, and afterward Yesod; and why did he change the order? To this he answered that, since body and covenant—which are Tiferet and Yesod—are reckoned as one, it is fitting to mention it [Yesod] right after Tiferet. And the intent is that, when Tiferet was emanated, Yesod was concealed within it, and Yesod was somewhat revealed in a delightful existence; and for this reason the term "seventh emanation" applies to it. And [the term] that it is ninth or tenth applies to it because there the emanation arrived, and it was the end of all, and it was revealed after Netzach and Hod with an intrinsic revelation that reveals it in itself, and not in the fine existence such as it is in Tiferet. And this is as he sets forth and proceeds: "one in reckoning," etc., "ascending to one." The intent is that Tiferet is vav, and Yesod is the extension of the vav; if so, the two of them together are vav, and they ascend to one, for they are one body. And afterward he explained yet another proof, that they are two vavs, an upper and a lower: the vav in its full spelling [vav-alef-vav] is two vavs with an alef in the middle. The intent is to unite them, that they are one and all one matter. And we said "to unite them"—the intent is that two attributes do not unite unless there comes to be between them a distinct existence that unites them, meaning an intermediate aspect between the two of them, by means of which aspect they unite; and this intermediate aspect is of them intrinsically: not of the upper one, since it is revealed from it, and not of the lower one, since it is concealed from it; rather it is the aspect that mediates between the two of them, and this aspect is called alef, because in it is the power of union, to unite these two attributes. And of this aspect we have a proof from the Sefer ha-Zohar, portion Acharei (fol. 74b), in the matter of A-V-Y, V-Y, H-V-Y, where it says there, in the matter that the vav was removed and the head of [the word] tzaddik—let it be examined in its place, and it will be explained for us in the Sefer Or Yakar. And let us return to the matter of the saying: that, by reason of the two reasons he stated, it is not fitting to separate Yesod from Tiferet; therefore it is fitting that Tiferet should be the third day, and Yesod after it, the fourth day. "My locks," etc.—meaning, that there are extremities that are in Netzach and Hod. And he explained them in another place in the Zohar (Vayechi, fol. 241), and said there "Netzach of netzachim, Hod of hodot." And the intent is upon three aspects, in each one of which the middle is the true Netzach, and the two outermost are called netzachim—they are the two aspects of the extremities: the aspect that Netzach has from the side of Chesed, which is in relation to what it receives from it; and the third aspect, which is in relation to what it overflows. And these two aspects are not in Netzach itself, but are aspects subordinate to it; and Netzach itself is the middle aspect, and the outermost ones are Netzach by accident, not intrinsically, like the middle one. And likewise, in this manner, in Hod. And we have already explained the matter of these three aspects in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof is the Keter, chapter 7—let it be examined there. "Of which it is said, his thighs are pillars of marble (shesh)." It was difficult for him: just as there is Netzach of netzachim, Hod of hodot, there is also Chesed of chesadim, Gevurah of gevurot, as he explained in the Zohar, portion Vayetzei (fol. 155a), in the matter of the twelve tribes of Israel and "all their backs were inward"; and if so, accordingly, it would be found that there are already six extremities in Gedulah and Gevurah. To this he said that the extremities that are in Netzach and Hod are more well-attested in the verse, in his saying "his thighs are pillars of marble (shesh)" [shesh = six]. "The drops of the night, this is the Shekhinah," etc.—for she comprises all that is above, as is known. "And why is she called night?"—the intent is not to ask why she is called "night," for it is clear that she is the attribute of night, and "night" is forever an allusion to Din, as explained in the Values of the Allusions. Rather, the intent of the question is, since the import of the verse is that now "the voice of her beloved knocks" at the door of her house to embrace his desired one, as it appears that he has not yet coupled with her—and we hold, according to the Zohar, that she is called "night" only after her receiving from the male and her union with him. And these are his words in the Zohar, portion Bo (fol. 38b): "We have learned, it is written, 'if there shall be a maiden, a virgin' (Deuteronomy 22:23)—[but] na'ar [youth, masc.] is written. What is the reason? Because as long as she has not received the male she is called na'ar; once she has received the male she is called na'arah. So too, [she is called] leil [night] before she has received the male; and even though 'watching' (shimurim) is written of it, the male was destined to join with her. And at the time when the male joined with her, it is written (Exodus 12:42), 'this is the night (laylah) of watching unto YHVH'—'watching,' male and female; and therefore it is written 'this is the night.' And after male and female are found [together], there is none to praise but the male." End [of quotation].

And at first glance this matter appears [to be] the opposite of reason; for it would have been fitting that, while she has not [yet] received the male, she should be called "leil," indicating the feminine, and when she has received the male she should be called "laylah," indicating the masculine; and likewise na'ar [and] na'arah. But the matter will be understood by what the Sages, of blessed memory, said (Sanhedrin, fol. 22): "a woman makes a covenant only with the one who made her a vessel." And the matter of making the female into a vessel is by means of the male; and the letter that indicates the matter of making the vessel is the heh; and therefore, when she has received the male, she is called "laylah," with a heh, an allusion to her being made a vessel, as a female to receive by means of her husband. And then, with the male having joined with her, her husband having made her a vessel, she is called "laylah." And the matter is that the heh that is in Malkhut is an allusion to three vavs, which are chesed, din, and rachamim. And there is a great distinction between the upper heh and the lower heh: for the three vavs that are in the lower heh are Netzach, Hod, Yesod, and the three vavs that are in the upper heh are Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet. And the union of Tiferet with Malkhut is by means of the holy member, which is Yesod, and the two testicles of the male, which are Netzach and Hod.

And behold, while she has not [yet] received the male—who is the one who sends to her the gift, to adorn herself with these three vavs, so that there may be in her a dwelling upon her at the time of coupling—she is called "leil," or "na'ar," or "tzedek," and the like, indicating that she has not yet received upon herself the light of the male, and that she lacks the adornment, which is the heh, which is three vavs. But when she has received upon herself the member of the male, then these three lights illumine in her—which are Netzach, Hod, Yesod—and there are figured in her beautiful adornments, which are the form of the heh, which is three vavs, like this: ה. And the intent is not that, when she has received the male upon her, the union of coupling itself is effected; rather, the preparation and readying toward the coupling is the matter of "receiving the male upon her" mentioned here—that is, the betrothal and engagement, in that she has received upon herself the name of the husband. And this is her receiving, before the coupling, from the right and from the left, in the secret of "his left hand is under my head" (SoS 2:6), as we shall explain at length in the Gate of Essence and Governance and in the Gate of the Particulars of the Names. And then, with the figuring of the form of the heh—that is, the three vavs—she is surely made a vessel, that is, a receptacle to receive the existence of the three Sefirot themselves, which are Netzach, Hod, Yesod, which dwell in her at the time of coupling literally, in the existence of the heh, which is the existence of the three vavs that are in it, as explained. And now, accordingly, it was difficult for him: he should have said "my locks, the drops of leil," as we said, that he has not yet coupled with her. To this he rectified and said "she is the night of the Sabbath, a night of watching"—the intent being that it is the night of the Sabbath, which is the time of her conjugal due, and a night of watching, the intent being that she is kept for her husband, for YHVH; and if so, since she is at "the door of hope," it is fitting that she be called "laylah," since her time has already arrived and she is adorned—for the word "laylah" is not an allusion to union itself and intrinsic union. Rather, "laylah" means "leil heh," that is, the leil that is Malkhut in the secret of the intensity of Din has already become "laylah," the meaning being that the male has illumined her and adorned her in the secret of the heh, which is chesed, din, rachamim, white, red, green—the secret of the three vavs mentioned above. And in truth, this is not union but adornment; for upon these three colors he explained, in the matter of the rainbow, in portion Noach (9:16), "and I will see it, to remember the everlasting covenant"—"and I will see it" [the rainbow], like a bride adorning herself for her husband with colors, and then "to remember the covenant," which is the union. Behold, [it is stated] explicitly that the existence of the light of the heh, which is three colors, and these three vavs, are only adornment. And even though he said "once she has received the male upon her she is called na'arah," this is because these colors are not hers except from the side of the male, as explained, and not because there is then literally complete union; for if so, it would be fitting that she be called by the name of the male, or by a word that intrinsically indicates the male, not "laylah" and "na'arah," for in truth the heh is principally in the female. Rather, surely, as explained, the principal union is not in this matter, and its principal [mode] is one, which is called "laylah," which is the adornment; and her being called "laylah" is the allusion to her adornments, while she sits and awaits her bridegroom—when will he come to the chamber to unite. And this is what he said: "a night of watching," it is "surely unto YHVH"—meaning, that her being called "laylah" means "leil," the one who waits for her husband, who is not lacking the adornment but [only] awaits her husband.

And the matter of the verse "a night of watching, it is unto YHVH"—"this is the night, unto YHVH." The meaning of "a night of watching," etc., is the matter of her sitting and awaiting—for this is the import of "watching"—"this is the night," etc. And it is found that "laylah," with a heh, and "a night of watching, it is unto YHVH," are all one matter. And this is what the verse explained: "a night of watching, it is unto YHVH"; "this is the night," etc. And his saying "the drops of the night"—the intent is that all these limbs, which are the days, are filled with effluence and abundant good, which is the drop of seed fitting for the night; and afterward, "open for me," etc. End [of quotation].

And behold, our intent in this saying is completed, and it has been explained in it that it is already fitting that Yesod be after Tiferet, prior to Netzach and Hod—and this by accident, not by nature, for its customary [place] is ninth. And the reason for the change of practice in this saying, Rashbi—peace be upon him—explained in his language, in saying "body and covenant are reckoned as one"; and since the intent of the verse is the matter of union and coupling, therefore he united Tiferet and Yesod, which are body and covenant, that unite together toward the coupling. And we may already examine somewhat from this in the words of the Gaon, in his saying "the seventh emanation, the everlasting covenant, and the mnemonic is 'righteousness calls it to its foot.'" And was it hidden from the Gaon that Yesod is called "yesod," and it is a full verse, "and the Righteous One is the foundation of the world"? Rather, the intent is to explain the union of Malkhut with Yesod—she being the one called "tzedek" [righteousness], grasped at the foot of Yesod, in that she joins to Tiferet; and therefore he gave it precedence, to indicate its existence prior to the netzachim. And to its existence after the netzachim he directed in his saying "the sixth emanation, the central pillar, and the mnemonic is 'behold, You desire truth in the inward parts.'" And was the verse "You give truth to Jacob" hidden from the Gaon, for it is the most well-attested? Rather, [it was] to explain to us how it [Tiferet] is united with the inward parts [tuchot], which are Netzach and Hod: and the intent of the verse is "behold, truth"—which is Tiferet—"You desire," overflowing desire and satiety, "in the inward parts (batuchot)," which are Netzach and Hod. And great is the power of the Gaon, who intended to explain to us two matters in one utterance. And behold, the matter of the precedence has been explained, and we shall speak further in the coming chapters. And the sum of the matters is that the emanation is emanated one after another: for Keter emanated Chokhmah, and Chokhmah emanated, etc., up to the emanation of Malkhut. And it is a correct view, agreed upon from the verses, and from reason, and from the words of the holy Tanna, Rashbi, and from the words of the Gaon.

The intent in this chapter is to explain another view, contradicting this. And it is the Kabbalah of my teacher and master, the pious one, our honored teacher Rabbi Yosef Karo—may God preserve and keep him. And these are his words: "Behold, I have come to make known to you the truth of the matter and the secret of secrets—these [things] to know: that when delight-in-delightings, the Ancient of Ancients, the Ein Sof, arose to create worlds, there struck forth from Him one striking, and there shone one shining, which comprises three. And as the Rabbis said, 'and one point, it comprises three'—length, and breadth, and depth. And so that shining was one, and comprised within it were three—these are Keter, Chokhmah, Binah. Afterward, each one of these three struck forth from itself one shining that comprises two. Chokhmah struck forth from itself one shining that comprises two, which is Chesed and Netzach; and with Chokhmah itself it was three. And Binah, too, struck forth from itself one shining that comprises two, which is Gevurah [and] Hod; and with Binah itself it was three. And Keter struck forth from itself one shining that comprises three, which are Tiferet, Yesod, Malkhut—because, since it is closer to the Ein Sof and resembles it (for it too is very concealed, after the manner of the Ein Sof), therefore in the shining that it brought forth there were comprised three, after the manner of the Ein Sof. And now, since Keter, Chokhmah, Binah were one shining, and Malkhut goes forth from Keter and Abraham from Chokhmah, it was as though both went forth from one place. And for this reason Abraham said of her (Genesis 20:12), 'and indeed she is truly my sister, the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother'; and behold, these ten Sefirot were completed for them." End of his words—[in keeping with] the description of his righteousness and his piety. And the sum of his words is that Chokhmah emanated Chesed-Netzach [ChaN], Binah emanated Gevurah-Hod [GaH], and Keter [emanated] Tiferet-Yesod-Malkhut [TYM].

And behold, this matter is necessitated from reason. For since Chesed is by its nature lovingkindness, how is it possible that Gevurah should be emanated from it, Gevurah being Din and a strong fire? And likewise, how is it possible that, Gevurah being Din and a strong fire, it should be a cause to Tiferet, which is mercy? This is impossible—to say that the action of the effect is the opposite of the action of the cause. Rather, of necessity we say that Chokhmah, whose foundation is Chesed, is a cause to ChaN [Chesed-Netzach], whose actions are lovingkindness in their root, which is Chesed. And likewise GaH [Gevurah-Hod], which are Din, their foundation is Binah, from which the [powers of] Din are aroused, as we shall explain at length in the matters of these inquiries in the Gate of Essence and Governance. And therefore it is expounded in Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer: "by ten utterances the world was created, and they are included within three—within Chokhmah, and within Tevunah, and within Da'at." He indicated that, although they are ten, they are included within three—which are Chokhmah, root of the line of Chesed; Tevunah, root of the line of Din; and Da'at, root of the line of mercy. And the reason he said "Da'at" and not "Keter," we shall explain at length in the said Gate. All this indicates the strength of my teacher's view, that it is correct and true. But it is somewhat difficult, for in the Zohar it is expounded: "the waters departed [from] darkness"; and a proof (Genesis 25:19), "Abraham begot Isaac"—meaning that Gevurah is an effect of Chesed; and this is a great forced reading, and at first glance the opposite of reason. And likewise they also expounded in the Sefer ha-Bahir, "the waters conceived and gave birth to gloom," indicating that the cause and the source of Gevurah, which is the gloom, was Chesed, which is the waters. And how difficult this matter is to settle, for it is the opposite of reason, as we explained—for how is it possible that Din should be an effect of Chesed?

And further, Rashbi—peace be upon him—explained the opposite of this, in saying that the [powers of] Din are aroused from the side of Binah, as we shall explain in the said Gate—indicating that the cause of Gevurah is Binah, and from there [come the] judgments, and it is its cause. And besides these two views that we have set forth concerning the emanation, there is yet a third view, which is the view of Rashbi—peace be upon him—and it is explained in many places: that Keter emanated Chokhmah, and Chokhmah emanated Binah, and Binah emanated the whole structure together. And this was explained from the saying that we copied in the Gate of Self and Vessels, chapter 7. And so it is agreed in several places, that the plantings of the Emanation were in Binah, and from there they were planted below, to the place of their emanation. And in this way he proceeded also several times, in several places. And at first glance it appears that this view is the one agreed upon in most of the words of Rashbi—peace be upon him. And to necessitate this view there is no need, for it is very well-attested. And now, to whom shall we flee for help, and who will arbitrate for us between the three views, all three of which are the words of Rashbi—peace be upon him? And upon which of them all shall we lean, to say, "this is the straight way, let us walk in it"? And when these views have pressed upon us, we say: we have no way to exempt ourselves from rectifying these views according to their measure, until there remains for us no doubt, neither small nor great. And of God we ask the help.

Before the emanation of the emanated ones, the simple Ein Sof was in the utmost simplicity, concealed in the utmost concealment. And His Godhead was not revealed to another, by reason of the absence of the existents, by means of which there is some revelation of the loftiness of His unity. And the Sefirot were in their potential, concealed in Him, in His potential, in a fine and concealed existence, as befits His unity. And let not the heart of a person wonder at our saying that they were concealed in Him, and let him not hasten to reply, "if so, it is found that the Sefirot already existed in Him—there is necessitated from this multiplicity and change." For this is not among the questions of the wise, but rather an enticement of the intellect. And the reason is that, even though we say that the Sefirot were concealed in Him, our intent in this matter is not to say that the Sefirot were literally as they are now; rather, they were unified in His unity, in true and strong union. And we shall set forth a fine parable: to the flint stone, from which fire is brought forth by the striking of iron, and from the fire there goes forth lightning. And now, in truth, it is not correct [to say] that that fire was literally within the stone, and that the stone was divided into a multiplicity of parts according to the parts of the sparks scattered from it—this, surely, the intellect of the discerning will not judge. Rather, on the contrary, that fire was concealed within the stone and unified in it in true and strong union, in such a way that there is no division or separation at all between the stone and the fire within it. So is the matter with the Self of the simple Godhead: before the spreading-forth to govern the lower ones, the Sefirot were unified in His Self and bound to Him in a mighty and strong bond, until [the term] "existence of the Sefirot" would scarcely apply to it at all—but rather the true union. And this union, and the fineness mentioned, is the source of the Sefirot concealed within Him, which are called the supernal Tzachtzachot, from which yet other tzachtzachot were emanated, to which the term "tzachtzachot" does not yet even apply, as will be explained in the Gate of the Tzachtzachot, with the help of Heaven. And when it arose in His simple Will to reveal His Godhead and to do good with His concealed attributes to another, He brought forth the privation into existence, and emanated from His simple light a first Sefirah, which is called Keter. And this Sefirah, by reason of the abundance of its fineness, is not revealed at all, even after its emanation—how much more so that the existents should be by means of it. For, by reason of the abundance of its adherence to its source, [the term] "Something" (yesh) does not even apply to it, but only "Nothing" (ayin). And even the name "Nothing" does not apply to its simplicity, except in its conjunction with Chokhmah and Binah. And the reason is that "Nothing" applies only to a thing whose existence is in some measure apprehended as necessitated, and one asks concerning this apprehension, "what is it?", and they reply, "nothing"—to indicate that it is a thing not [fully] apprehended, but the intellect has already apprehended it and necessitated it, to the point that one asks concerning it "what is its matter?", and the reply is "nothing." But Keter, by reason of the smallness of the apprehension in it—for the lower ones have no apprehension of it at all—the word "Nothing" is not necessitated of it in its aspect toward the Emanator, but only in its aspect toward the ones emanated from it, which is its partnership with Chokhmah and Binah; [in that aspect] it is called "Nothing." And so "Nothing" (ayin) alludes: alef = Keter, yod = Chokhmah, nun = Binah, as is explained in the words of Rashbi—peace be upon him—in many places, and as is explained in the Gate of the Values of the Allusions, blessed be He. [Its fineness reaches so far] that it is even called, in some places, "Ein Sof," by way of accident; and likewise it is called "the Cause of causes," by way of accident; and likewise several epithets that indicate concealment. And Chokhmah, in relation to it, is called "Something" (yesh). And this is its saying "Something from Nothing," meaning Chokhmah from Keter. And even though Chokhmah was emanated, it is still the utmost of fineness, and the existents cannot be revealed by means of it, for, by reason of the abundance of its fineness, they call it by the name "Thought"—for, just as Thought is privation and not [an actualized] existent, so Chokhmah is fine, and the existents toward [actual] governance are [there] in privation—even though it is not like the fineness of Keter, since it is called "Something." And although we said that it is called "Something," the intent in "Something" is not literally apprehended somethingness, complete somethingness, God forbid; rather, the intent in the word "Something" is in the distinction between "Nothing" and "Something"—not complete somethingness, but as the negation of "Nothing," and not affirming "Something" at all. And even the word "Something" does not apply to Chokhmah in respect of its aspect toward Keter, except in respect of its aspect toward Binah and its conjunction with it; for thus is "Something" (yesh) explained: yod = Chokhmah, shin = Binah, as is explained in the Gate of the Values of the Allusions. And therefore, even though the two Sefirot were emanated, by reason of the abundance of their nearness to their source, the existent cannot come into being.

And the intent in this matter is not that the Sefirot could not be emanated at all, for they were already being emanated, all of them in Keter, and all of them in Chokhmah. But the matter is a concealed secret, and it is not our way to exaggerate matters, God forbid, but [only] to reveal them. And the matter is that mercy is near the source, because it is not so subject to changes; and the more [a thing] draws near to the source, the more [it is] mercy. And [this is] not by reason of the fineness, as many have thought—that the spreading-forth was the cause of the Din; for this, to us, is a rejected view, as will be explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance. Rather, the reason is that "in the light of the King's face is life"; and the more the Sefirot draw near to the Emanator, the more the Din is diminished from the Sefirah that is the root of Din, and it is so refined that all becomes light and life, the Will of the Benefactor; and the decrees of Din do not act, and are nullified, and its powers do not go forth into actuality to act, by reason of the nearness of the emanated ones to the Emanator. And the powers of Din were rising in thought, and not [being] actualized. And this is the secret of "and these are the kings," etc., "and he died, and there reigned," etc. (Genesis 36). And the principal governance is from the side of the masters of Din, as the Sages, of blessed memory, explained: "He saw that the world could not endure; He associated with it the attribute of mercy." But, with all this, the principal governance is by Din, except that He associated with it the attribute of mercy, a mere association. And therefore, when the first two grades existed—which are Keter [and] Chokhmah—the powers of Din were not revealed at all. And from this we shall know the reason that the line of Din journeys last. For it would have been fitting that Binah be second—for, just as Gedulah is first and Gevurah second, and Tiferet, the deciding one, is third, so too [among] the supernal roots it would have been fitting that their emanation be thus: first the emanation of Chokhmah, root of Chesed; and second the emanation of Binah, root of Din; third Keter, root of mercy, the deciding line. But, by reason of the abundance of their nearness to the source, it is impossible for Din to decree its decrees and to judge its judgments, for "in the light of the King's face is life"; and therefore the emanation had to be drawn out, and the root of Din was not emanated until the third grade, as we shall explain.

And this matter is explained in the Zohar, in the Idra de-Nazir (fol. 128a). These are its words: "It is taught: the Ancient of Ancients, the Concealed of the Concealed, before He had prepared the adornments of the King and the crownings of the crowns, beginning and conclusion there was not. And He was engraving and measuring within Himself, and He spread before Himself one hanging [parsa], and on it He engraved [and measured] kings; but their adornments were not established. This is [the meaning of] 'and these are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom before there reigned a king over the children of Israel' (Genesis 36:31)—the first king, [corresponding] to the first of 'the children of Israel.' And all those engraved [ones] were called by names, and were not established, until He set them aside and stored them away. And after a time, He withdrew into that hanging and was arrayed in His adornments. And it is taught: when it arose in [His] Will to create the Torah and He brought it forth, immediately it said before Him, 'whoever wishes to be arrayed and to be made, let him first array His adornments'—the Concealed of the two thousand years." End [of quotation].

And the meaning of "the Ancient of Ancients" is the supernal Keter. And it is called "the Elder of elders." And the intent is that it is prior to the prior ones. For Keter is "elder" in relation to Chokhmah and Binah, which are "elders"; and this is "the Ancient of Ancients"—even in relation to the elders, which are Chokhmah and Binah, it is elder and concealed, to indicate its fineness, for it is an elder concealed and exalted above the concealed supernal ones. "The Concealed of the Concealed"—meaning, concealed from the concealed ones. The intent is that, even from those Sefirot that are in concealment, it is concealed. "Before He had prepared"—meaning, before the revelation of the adornments of the great King, which is Keter, which had already been emanated, except that it was not revealed; and its concealed Sefirot and its matters are called "the crownings of the crowns," for they are a crown to the crowns of all the Sefirot. And the intent is: before the revelation of the adornments of the King and the crownings of the crowns. "Beginning and conclusion there was not." The meaning is: Chesed and Din were not in the world. For Chesed is called "beginning," as they said, "we begin with merit first"; and therefore Chokhmah is called "beginning," and in it is the beginning of the revelation of the line of Chesed. And "conclusion" is called Binah, for it is the line of Din, as is known. And these are the beginning of the existents and their privation: for in Chokhmah is the beginning of their existence, and in Binah is the completion of their circuit, in the secret of the Jubilee, where the existents return upon their being completed, to complete the circuit of seven years seven times. And therefore he said that "beginning and conclusion there was not." And one should not say that the line of mercy, which is the middle, did not exist at all, for it already existed somewhat, being the emanation of Keter, which is the Ancient itself. And therefore we say [that only] "beginning and conclusion," which are the two extremities, "there was not." "And He was engraving and measuring within Himself." The meaning is: the Sefirot and the extremities, in the secret of the aspect of Din, were being emanated within the existence of Keter, and there they were being engraved, and were not [being] established—for the world could not be governed by means of them, because of the Din that was not [yet] revealed, as explained. And when He saw the fineness of the existents and the smallness of the Din, He emanated Chokhmah and began to incise within it the existents, and to bring them forth to the revelation of Din in their existence. And this is what he said: "and He spread before Himself one hanging," that is, Chokhmah, which is a veil and a screen that conceals Keter and closes it off. "And on it He engraved the measure of kings." And "their adornments" [tikkunohi] are the powers of Din—not His external powers, meaning the actual master of Din, but the matters of Gevurah and its judgments, and the worlds that are in it, which are called "the measure of kings," that is, the kings of Edom, as he sets forth and proceeds. "And their adornments"—that is, the rectification and the emanation and its revelation—"were not established." The meaning is that it was not yet possible for the Din to be emanated and to be revealed, by reason of its nearness to its source.
And behold, in Chokhmah it is in great fineness and near the Emanator, and therefore the secret of mercy prevails.

And further, the secret of the emanation from the side of the [powers of] Din "was not established." This is [the meaning of] "and these are the kings who reigned"—meaning, the powers of Din that arose in thought to be emanated were not emanated and were not revealed, by reason of the fineness of Chokhmah; and therefore it is said of them "and he died," that is, concealment. And so Rashbi explained in the Idra further on, and said that the intent is not that they were nullified, God forbid, but that they were concealed, until the emanation was emanated, and from there these worlds were revealed in the fitting place, after the manner of the Sefirot—for they were being revealed in Keter, and afterward in Chokhmah, but the emanation was not rectified there, until they were emanated to their place and to their line, as is fitting.

And the matter of "and he died, and he died" is the concealment of the world of Din and its line, which were not able to be revealed by reason of its intensity. And his saying "before there reigned a king over the children of Israel": the meaning is "the first king" [is Binah], and "the children of Israel," the first—that is, "Israel," the first—is Tiferet. And this is because the verse said "before there reigned a king over the children of Israel," meaning: before Binah, which is "king," should reign and be emanated, and before Israel, which is Tiferet. And this is the existence of the revelation of those worlds in Chokhmah. And it said "in the land of Edom," the intent being "in the place of Din"; for there He was incising the world before Himself—that is, the line of Din—and the worlds were being concealed, not revealed, because Binah, where the beginning of Din is, had not yet been emanated. "Until He set them aside and stored them away." The meaning is that they did not literally die—which would imply that they were nullified—but rather "He stored them away," that is, He concealed them, as he explained there, in the [matter of the] adornments of Zeir Anpin. And they were concealed, after the manner of the Sefirot themselves, which are concealed in Chokhmah, as we shall explain. "And after a time He withdrew into that hanging." The meaning is that the cause of the revelation is the cause of the concealment, and the cause of the concealment is the cause of the revelation. And the matter is that, in the concealment of the strong light and its being clothed in a garment, it is revealed.

And behold, the light is concealed, and in truth it is revealed; for if it were not concealed, it would not be revealed—like the likeness of one who comes to gaze at the ray of the sun: by reason of the revelation of the ray of the sun is its concealment, for a person cannot gaze at it by reason of the abundance of its brilliance; and when he conceals it and gazes at it through screens, then he attains to gaze at it with his eye and it does not harm him. And so is the matter with the emanation: that it conceals itself and clothes itself in order to be revealed. And this is what he said, "and after a time"—meaning, after this incising, as we shall explain—then "He withdrew into that hanging." The meaning is: the supernal Keter withdrew, with Chokhmah, and emanated Binah; and there it was rectified, for from there is the beginning of the revelation of Din, as is known, for from Binah the [powers of] Din are aroused, as we shall explain in the Gate of Essence and Governance, with the help of Heaven. "And it is taught: when it arose in [His] Will." He brought this baraita to support what is expounded. "It arose in Will"—that is, Keter. "To create the Torah"—that is, Chokhmah, which is the supernal Torah, prior by two thousand years, etc. And the intent is that by means of it shall be the governance and the line of Din.
