"And He brought it forth immediately," etc.—meaning, that He emanated it to the existence of Chokhmah, outside of Keter; "and it said before Him," that is, a parable to the existence of the worlds and the line of Din, which were not revealed in Chokhmah, and were dying and being concealed. And this is the matter of its saying [this] before its Emanator—like the matter of the hanging that he mentioned at the beginning of the discourse. "Whoever wishes to be rectified and to be made," etc. The meaning is that it is impossible for the concealed ones and the existents to be revealed unless Keter, which was not [yet] ready, be revealed further, as explained above. And afterward, when there was revealed yet a third grade—that is, in Binah—then it would be possible for the existents and the line of Din to come into being as is fitting. And he called Keter "the Concealed of the two thousand years." The meaning is: Keter is concealed from Chokhmah and from Binah, which are the two thousand years. For every Sefirah is comprised of ten, ascending to a hundred; and ten times ten are a hundred, and ten times a hundred are a thousand. It is found that Keter is concealed by [the] two thousand years. And he called it "concealed" because, at such a time, it was concealed even from the two thousand years—for so he called it above, "the Ancient of Ancients, the Concealed of the Concealed," as explained. And then, after Keter had rectified itself in what would be revealed and made ready by means of Binah, then it was possible for the existents to be revealed and emanated. And with the preface of this saying, the matter of the return of the Sefirot at the Jubilee, in the fiftieth year, to Binah will be understood—and why they do not return to Keter, which is a finer existence, more excellent and more exalted. And the reason is that in Binah they are there in [the mode of] the revealed existence of the Sefirot; but from Binah upward, if they ascend, they are concealed as in their priority. And there is no advantage [such] that they should be nullified, God forbid; for there is no revelation of the Sefirot except from Binah downward, where the line of Din is in force. And with this saying will be understood what is expounded in Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer—and these are its words: "Before the world was created, the Holy One blessed be He and His Name alone existed. And it arose in [His] thought to create the world. And He was incising the world before Himself. A parable to a king who wished to build a palace: if he does not incise in the ground its foundations and its exits, he does not begin to build. So too the Holy One blessed be He was incising the world before Himself, and it did not stand until He created repentance." End of his words.

The meaning of "before the world was created": the intent is, before Binah was emanated—for she is called "world," as we shall explain in the Gate of the Values of the Allusions—the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Name alone existed. Now many explain it [thus]: "the Holy One, blessed be He" is the Ein Sof, and "His Name" is Keter. But this is a great difficulty for us, for the word "the Holy One, blessed be He" does not properly apply to the Ein Sof, since the word "blessed" [implies one who] is a recipient of effluence. And even if we explain that its meaning is "the source of the blessings," we have already explained, in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof is the Keter, chapter 5, that the source of blessing is Keter according to the view of Rashbi, peace be upon him. Therefore we say that "the Holy One, blessed be He" is Keter, and "His Name" is Chokhmah.
And the notion of "Name" [referring] to Chokhmah is not strange, for the meaning of "Name" everywhere is a garment, as we shall explain in [the Gate of] the Values of the Allusions (s.v. "Name").

And behold, the garment of Keter is Chokhmah. And if we explain it according to their way: "the Holy One, blessed be He" is the Ein Sof, and "His Name" is Keter; and "it arose in thought" is Chokhmah; "to create the world" means the emanation of the existents as the line of Din, which are the world in truth, and after their name Binah is called "world."

And behold, the existents and the line of Din arose in thought and were engraved within her [Chokhmah], after the manner of the hanging "upon which He was engraving," etc.; and this is [the meaning of] "He was incising the world before Himself." Yet it did not endure, by reason of the subtlety—like the matter of the death of the kings that we explained above—for by reason of the great subtlety of Chokhmah and her nearness to her source, no existent there is revealed and no Din is made manifest, "for in the light of the King's face is life." [This continues] until He emanated Binah, for there is the revelation of the matters; and this is what it said, "until He created repentance."

And behold, there has emerged for us from this that the existence of the existents and their revelation is by means of Binah; and he was precise in calling her "repentance" (teshuvah), for there is the "returning" (teshuvah) of the circuit and its return after the Jubilee.

The intent in this chapter is to explain further the matter of the three first ones in their emanation. And it is this: that the principal governance of the lower beings is only by means of the six extremities—namely Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod, Yesod—and these are the streams that judge the world for good and for ill, according to the will of their Possessor.

And behold, these six extremities are a likeness to the Tree, which requires planting and transplanting. The intent is that there is needed, first, a concealed mode by which the watering of this Tree shall take place; and these are its roots, fixed and planted within Binah; and thence "the river issuing from Eden" waters the garden of delights, so that it may bear fruit after its kind "whose seed is in it" upon the lower earth, which is Malkhut. It emerges that these extremities—that which was designated by us in the preceding chapter by the name "the existents" and by the name "the root of Din"—[have] three necessary modes: the mode of planting, which are the roots; the mode of transplanting, which are the branches of the Tree; and the mode of the fruits [the Sefirot], which are below, the place where the actions are emanated.

And behold, since the matter of the existence of the Emanation requires these three things: when it arose in His will that their planting be in Keter, it would not endure; and likewise in Chokhmah, by reason of their nearness to their source, as explained—and the existents within them were [held] in the power of the simple mercies, and Din was not seen in them as the governance requires, as explained. Therefore, when the extremities reached Binah, there was their first planting, and there [was] the existence of their root, so that from there their effluence might flow to them by means of the concealed roots within Binah. And their root that is in Binah is from their root that is in Chokhmah, and their root that is in Chokhmah is from their root that is in Keter. And there in Binah [is] the first mode for the extremities, in a mode revealed to Din and to mercy. For in Chokhmah, although their mode is there too—as he testified in saying "and He was engraving," etc., that He incises within her, in the hanging, [which] indicated that their mode is in Chokhmah, as we shall explain—yet in Binah there was revealed a mode manifest to Din and to mercy, after the matter that "[mercy] and judgments are aroused from her," as we shall explain in the Gate of Essence and Governance. And afterward, from Binah they were transplanted to their own place—that is, the second mode for the extremities, which is their actual place, where they are the six extremities, all of them shining and effecting their action. And they are like the substance of the Tree that draws sustenance from its roots: so the Sefirot draw sustenance from their roots concealed in Binah, and this is the second mode for all the extremities. Afterward the Tree bears its fruits, which are the actions of the Sefirot effected by means of Malkhut, as is known.

And the matter of these six extremities: they are doubled—six for Din and six for mercy. And these are the twelve existents within Tiferet, which are the twelve boundaries that are the officers of the Teli, the sphere, and the heart [Teli, galgal, lev], whose sign is TaGaL. And they are "world, year, soul"—sign: OSheN—for these three are Binah, Tiferet, Malkhut, in which are the three modes of the extremities; and therefore the boundaries were depicted in these three places, as we shall expand on at length in the Gate of the Particulars of the Names, chapters 7, 8, 9, [and] 10. And now that we have called attention [to the fact] that the mode of the extremities could not be revealed by means of Keter and Chokhmah, let us proceed to explain the order of their emanation until their arrival at Binah; and afterward we shall explain, in a separate chapter, their emanation from Binah downward.

Behold, when it arose before Him to emanate Keter, at the time of its emanation there were within it the ten Sefirot, this one within that and that within this, each concealed within its fellow, and all of them within Keter. However, the seven Sefirot were not [the ones] revealed within Keter; rather, the [ones] that were principally revealed within it were Chokhmah and Binah. It emerges that in Keter [there is] a point composed of three points revealed within it, which were made from three lights that are concealed roots—namely, primordial light, clear light, [and] dazzling light—as we shall expand on in the Gate of the Tzachtzachot.
And behold, within these three points the Sefirot were concealed, as we shall explain in chapter 6, with God's help.

And behold, Keter emanated Chokhmah and emanated into her all the Sefirot, which are comprised within three points; and they are three aspects within Chokhmah, corresponding to the three first ones, which are the three brains that we explained from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof is the Keter, chapter 7, with the help of Heaven.
And behold, Chokhmah emanated Binah, and within her [are] three points in which the whole Emanation is comprised, and they too correspond to the three first ones.

And behold, it was not at the time of the emanation of Chokhmah or of Binah that the Sefirot were emanated within her; rather, in the matter of the emanation of each and every Sefirah of these three first ones there were six aspects. The first aspect: the concealed aspect, prior to its revelation, [hidden] in the Sefirah that emanates it; and it is so concealed that it is well-nigh absent. The second aspect: it is a revealed [aspect] that is manifested and seen within the Sefirah that emanates it. The third aspect: revealed in itself at its fitting place—and this is the [proper] existence of the Sefirah. The fourth aspect: to place within it the power whereby the upper Sefirah is able to emanate the Sefirot within it and to receive all the rest of the Sefirot. The fifth aspect: it is to place within it the power whereby it is able to emanate the Sefirot concealed within it to their revealed existence in its own self. The sixth aspect: revealed at their fitting place. And the matter is thus: at first the Ein Sof emanated Keter, and Keter was concealed and unrevealed—"air that is not grasped." Afterward the Ein Sof struck within it and emanated it [as] a revealed aspect. Third, He struck within it and emanated it at its fitting place. Fourth, afterward He struck within it and emanated within it the power that it might be able to receive the Sefirot. Fifth, He emanated within it the power that the Sefirot might be seen within it. Sixth, He emanated within it the power that it might be able to emanate the Sefirot to their fitting place—that is, in Chokhmah, [Keter being] revealed relative to itself. And in the manner of these six aspects pertaining to Keter from the side of the Ein Sof, so [is] the manner of Chokhmah from the side of Keter—except that the last three aspects of Keter are the first three of Chokhmah. How so? The first [of Chokhmah] is revealed in Keter, yet not a manifest revelation, but [only] its existence there—this, then, is the fourth that he stated regarding Keter, that He placed within it the power that it might receive the Sefirot, which are the existence of the Sefirot in concealment. And the second of Chokhmah, which is revealed in itself within Keter, is the fifth of Keter, which is that He placed within it the power that the Sefirot might be seen within it. And the third of Chokhmah, which is revealed at its own place, is the sixth of Keter—that is to say, [that] the Ein Sof emanated within it the power that it might be able to emanate the Sefirot to their fitting place. Further, the fourth pertaining to Chokhmah—which is that He placed within her the power that she might receive the Sefirot in her own self—is the first aspect of Binah, which is the mode of her emanation in Chokhmah in concealment. The fifth pertaining to Chokhmah—which is that He placed within her the power to reveal the existence of the Sefirot in Chokhmah itself—is the second [pertaining] to Binah, that there was revealed within Chokhmah a somewhat-apparent revelation. The sixth pertaining to Chokhmah—which is that He placed within her the power to emanate the Sefirah to its fitting place—is the third [pertaining] to Binah, that she was emanated to her place. Further, the fourth pertaining to Binah, which is the first [in this reckoning], is to place within her the power that she might receive the extremities—and this is the first mode for them, the first aspect. Further, the fifth pertaining to Binah is to place within her the power that the existence of the extremities might be seen in her, an apparent revelation—and these are the "roots" explained above. Further, the sixth pertaining to Binah, which is to place within her the power that she might be able to emanate the extremities to their own place. Thus the mode of the emanation of the three first ones has been stated.

And the matter of these aspects [is] like "nails firmly planted," in which there is no doubt at all, for we have derived them from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, concerning the Emanation. And we know that when the one who delves descends to the depth of Rashbi's words by means of these our words, his soul will bless us.

And behold, the mode that the extremities have, in the manner of complete concealment within Keter and within Chokhmah, is that which is designated by the "incising" mentioned in the passage in Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer; and likewise the matter of the "engraving" and "incising" mentioned in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him. And the intent in their saying "He was incising the world," and likewise the matter of "He was engraving, and they were not established," is not that He was literally observing whether it were possible to be established—that is, for the line of Din to be revealed there, God forbid—for there is no doubt before Him, nor any lack of knowledge. Rather, it is the mode of the sources of the Sefirot concealed in Keter and in Chokhmah, as above.

And behold, the matter of these four arrays—which are Chokhmah, Binah, Tiferet, and Malkhut—the four letters of the Name come as an allusion to them, in that within each and every one of them are comprised all ten Sefirot, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Four-Letter Name.

And behold, the fifth array, which is Keter—the thorn of the yod—by reason of its great subtlety is not mentioned in the Name. And the four arrays, which are Chokhmah, Binah, Tiferet, [and] Malkhut, Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in [the] portion [of] Bereshit, each one separately, in a place of its own, many times. And Rabbi Abba mentioned all four of them together in [the] portion [of] Tazria (folio 43), and these are his words: Rabbi Abba said: "How manifold are Your works, O YHVH" (Psalms 104:24)—how many are the works of the holy King! And they are all concealed in Chokhmah. This is [the meaning of] what is written, "All of them in wisdom You made." They are all comprised in Chokhmah, and they do not issue forth except by known paths toward Binah; and from there all was made and all was rectified, as it is said, "and by understanding it is established." And concerning this, "all of them in Chokhmah"; "You made"—in Binah. "The earth is full"—"the earth," this is the Assembly of Israel, for from there she is filled from all, as it is said (Ecclesiastes 1), "all the streams go to the sea," etc. "Your possessions"—for she brings them forth afterward. This is [the meaning of] "These are the generations of the heaven and the earth when they were created"—"with heh He created them"; and therefore, "the earth is full of Your possessions." Thus far his words.

And behold, this passage lacks nothing of what we require. He said, "and they are all concealed in Chokhmah." The meaning: although it appears that they are in Chokhmah—since her "making" is with her—nonetheless they are not revealed in Chokhmah; rather, in Chokhmah they are closed and concealed [in] the utmost concealment. And he established the matter by saying "this is what is written," etc.—the meaning [being]: by this [reading] the verse is understood that said, "All of them in wisdom You made," and afterward "the earth is full." Now there is a difficulty in it: for "the earth" is certainly Malkhut, and "Chokhmah" means Chokhmah literally; and if so, how is it possible that the mode of the existents is [drawn] from Chokhmah to Malkhut, with no difference of aspect between them but a single grade? For Chokhmah is the first cause of the existents and Malkhut the fourth effect, and there are two grades between them apart from Chokhmah and Malkhut—and how did Scripture mention them together with respect to the existents? Rather, what have you to say? That "he split the verse with a sharp knife." And the meaning of "all of them in Chokhmah" is not that they are in Chokhmah intrinsically, but [that they are] comprised within her—and this is what it says, "and they are all comprised in Chokhmah." And he was precise [in deriving this] from the expression "all of them," which is an expression of inclusion; and therefore there is no escaping that they go out by means of the paths to the outside—that is, to Binah, where [is] the cascade of the paths, and where they rest from their running. And this is what it says, "and they do not issue forth except by known paths toward Binah." The meaning: perforce their issuing is from Chokhmah to Binah. And if so, Binah is the second array for the extremities, which are the existents. "And from there all was made," etc.—it was difficult for him, for there is no [logical] necessity in that [alone], since it is already possible that their making be in Chokhmah while they pass through Binah merely in passing, and that they effect there no acquisitive, existential action at all. Therefore he said that it is not so, but "from there all was made and all was rectified," etc.—and thus their making and their rectification were principally by means of Binah. And for this he brought a proof from the verse, "and by understanding it is established." The meaning: and by Binah—which is also called "understanding" (tevunah), as explained in [the Gate of] the Values of the Allusions—by her the Sefirot and the existents and the deeds are established and set firm.

And behold, accordingly, the word "You made" perforce does not refer back to Chokhmah, but [is] a matter on its own—namely, the "making" of Binah, in [the production of] their existents and their establishment by means of her. And this is what it says, "and concerning this, all of them in Chokhmah"—the meaning [being]: all of them are comprised in Chokhmah; and here they split the verse. "You made"—this is the making of Binah and the rectification of the existents and their revelation in her. "The earth is full," etc.—it was difficult for him, for he had established that the making is in Binah on the grounds that it is impossible that the existents be emanated from Chokhmah to Malkhut, that is, from the [one] extreme to the [other] extreme; and on the strength of this he said that "You made" refers back to Binah. And now, even accordingly there is a difficulty, for between Binah and Malkhut there is likewise a second grade—namely, "year," which is Tiferet, that is, the place of their transplanting, as explained above. And to this he replied that [as for] "the earth is full," the word "the earth" is Malkhut in [the] aspect of her receiving from Tiferet. And this is what it says, "this is the Assembly of Israel." The meaning of "this": as he said, it is impossible to escape [the conclusion] that "the earth" is called Malkhut in her aspect of receiving from Tiferet—for this is the [assembly that] gathers and is gathered from "Israel," which is Tiferet. And likewise "the earth" receives from "the heaven," and "heaven and earth" are Tiferet and Malkhut, as is known. It emerges that her aspect called "earth" and her aspect called "the Assembly of Israel" are all one thing, and both [are] in the secret of her receiving from Tiferet. And how much more so now, when it says "the earth is full"—for the "fullness" of the earth is the streams that are emanated into her, which are the extremities issuing from Binah: branches that receive from their roots and bring forth in Malkhut "the fruit of His deeds." And this is what it says, "for from there"—that is, the aforementioned Binah—"she is filled from all"; the meaning [being]: from all the streams, which are the third array. And he established the matter from the verse, "all the streams go to the sea, yet the sea is not full." It appears that the filling of the sea is by means of the streams, which are the extremities comprised in the great stream, which is the stream [of] Tiferet. And since it said "the earth is full," certainly the intent is that she was filled by means of that which fills her, which is Tiferet—for it comprises the third array, that is, the Sefirah itself and the extremities.

And behold, now there are found in this verse four divisions, [which] are the four arrays. The first array is Chokhmah, and there the existents are concealed [in] the utmost concealment—and this is what it says, "all of them in Chokhmah." And the second array, which is the array of the roots, is Binah, and it is alluded to in the verse by the word "You made"; and one should not wonder at the matter of "making" [being attributed] to Binah, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Values of the Allusions (s.v. "making"). And the third array is the array of Tiferet, and it is alluded to by the word "is full," according to the way we have explained. And the fourth array is the array of Malkhut, alluded to by "the earth," and her [role] is to bring the matters forth into their realization below. And this is what it says, "for she brings them forth afterward." And the meaning of "afterward" [is] after these grades mentioned above; for now it is well [understood that] "she brings them forth afterward." But according to what had entered our minds—[namely] that [it ran] from Chokhmah to Malkhut—the explanation of the verse was difficult, since the array of Malkhut is not [immediately] after the array of Chokhmah. But now that he has explained that in the verse three arrays were mentioned—which are "in Chokhmah" and "in Binah" and the extremities, that is, Tiferet—this is [the meaning of] "Malkhut brings them forth afterward," that is, after Chokhmah and Binah and Tiferet in their order. This is [the meaning of] "These are the generations of the heaven and the earth." And the meaning of "the generations of the heaven and the earth," which are Tiferet and Malkhut, [is] that the generations cannot be in the earth except by means of the heaven, which is the male that emanates into the female. "With heh He created them." The meaning: although we say that Tiferet and Malkhut begot and brought into being the generations and the existents, our intent is not that the two of them together brought them into being equally, [such] that the two of them together would constitute a single array. Rather, the intent is that Tiferet, with its extremities, displays the actions and emanates them to Malkhut, and they are one array; and Malkhut displays them below, and she is another array. And this is what Scripture says, "when they were created—with heh He created them," for the creating was with heh alone. And therefore Tiferet came in concealment in the verse, and it did not mention Tiferet in the verse; for it would have been fitting to say, "and heaven and earth are full of Your possessions." Why did it conceal "the heaven" by the word "the earth is full," as we have explained? Rather, certainly it wished to guard, lest we fall into error and say that heaven and earth brought the existents into being together, the two of them in a single union, [such] that the two of them would be found to be a single array, and there would be only three arrays. For this [reason] it said, "the earth is full of Your possessions," for Malkhut is the fourth array, like Tiferet and the extremities themselves; and that which fills the earth, which is Tiferet and the extremities, is the third array on its own. Thus far has reached the explanation of the passage. And from it we have learned the matter of these four arrays; and these four arrays have ever so many proofs, far clearer than these. But since each of the four is, on its own, in a passage of its own—one here and one there—we have not seen [fit] to be lengthy with proofs, [confining ourselves] only to [this] short, lovely, and sweet passage.

After we have occupied ourselves in the preceding chapter with the matter of the emanation of the three first ones, and have said that the three of them were comprised in a single point, which is Keter—now we say that what we said, that all the Sefirot were comprised within them, is according to this order: that in the supernal Keter were Tiferet, Yesod, and Malkhut, which are related to the middle line, the line of mercy; and in the point [of] the very root of Chokhmah were comprised Gedulah and Netzach, which are related to the right line, the line of Chesed; and in Binah were comprised Gevurah [and] Hod, which are related to the line of Din, on the left side. This matter is necessitated [by reason of] the secret of the actions, as we shall explain in the Gate of Essence and Governance, with the help of Heaven, and as explained above in chapter 3 in the words of my teacher, may God preserve and keep him. And afterward, when the will arose before Him to emanate Chokhmah by the power of Keter—behold, when He had emanated her, He thereafter emanated within her and emanated first Binah, and afterward Tiferet, Yesod, and Malkhut, [though] not in a revealed mode like the revelation of Binah. And although we said "Tiferet, Yesod, and Malkhut," nonetheless Yesod does not yet rise in name at all, but only [as] the double-faced [du-partzufin].

And behold, the beginning of the revelation of the double-faced is in Chokhmah alone. And on this account it is found that the matter of the double-faced—although their root is from Keter—does not rise in name with respect to the matter of their emanation except in Chokhmah alone, since there they were [first] revealed, because they had a first journey from Keter to Chokhmah. Thus in Chokhmah there are now four grades in the emanation. The first is Binah, and she is revealed in her [Chokhmah], because even in Keter she came in [one] point [one of the three comprised within it—from Asis Rimonim], all the more so now. And the second is the emanation of the double-faced, and they are revealed, but not like Binah, since in Keter they were concealed, and now there was revealed only a slight revelation. And the third is the emanation of Chesed and Netzach, and they are concealed, for they have not yet journeyed from their place. And the fourth is the emanation of Gevurah and Hod, which have no revealed mode at all, since even their source—which is Binah—was as yet concealed in Chokhmah and had not been emanated. Afterward Chokhmah emanated Binah, by the power of Keter, by the power of the Ein Sof. And at the time of Binah's revelation there was emanated within her own self the secret of the concealed line of Din, for so it is fitting, [since] they are from her own self and she is their root. And immediately upon the emanation of Binah, Chokhmah emanated within her, by her [own] power, Chesed and Netzach, and by the power of Keter, the double-faced. It emerges that Binah has emanated within her three kinds of emanation: the first, her being revealed; and the principal [part] of the double-faced—which the supernal Keter emanated in Chokhmah, and Chokhmah, by the power of Keter, emanated them in Binah—it emerges that Keter Himself emanated them, and from Him they were, as explained.

And behold, this emanation [of the double-faced] is more revealed than the rest of the emanation within Binah, for it has a second journey: first they journeyed from Keter to Chokhmah, and afterward from Chokhmah to Binah. And the second emanation is the line of Chesed, which are Gedulah [and] Netzach; and this is more revealed than the line of Din, but not so much as the line of mercy, since it has only the first journey, which is from Chokhmah to Binah. But the line of Din is still set in its root, which is in Binah herself, and has not journeyed hither and thither—although it was revealed by means of the [general] revelation, [in] that its root was somewhat revealed. And with this premise the reason is settled why there is no Din except from Binah [downward], and not from Binah upward: because Binah is the root of Din, and even within Binah it has no revelation, all the more so from Binah upward. And also with this premise is understood the reason why Tiferet and Malkhut ascend as far as Keter, as is proven in the Tikkunim—which is not the case for Chesed and Netzach, which never ascend from Chokhmah upward, since their root is in Chokhmah. And it is now found that Tiferet and Malkhut ascend as far as Binah, and there they have a source and a revealed root; further, they ascend into Chokhmah, and there they have a revealed source and a root present—though not like their root in Binah, which is more concealed; further, they ascend as far as Keter, for there is their concealed root. And Chesed and Netzach ascend as far as Binah, and there they have a revealed root; further, they ascend into Chokhmah, and there they have a root more concealed than their root in Binah; and from Chokhmah upward they have no ascent, since they have no root above but [only] the root of their root, which is a root in Chokhmah—and although they are comprised in this root as well, [it is] in great concealment. And Gevurah and Hod ascend as far as Binah alone, and there is their root; and from there upward they have no root except the root of their root, which is the root of Binah, and they are there in great subtlety, as explained. And this is the reason that Din is from Binah downward. And likewise this is the matter of "and these are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom," which Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained—[as] explained [in chapter 4]. And although we said that they have no ascent from there upward, [it is] not, God forbid, that they have no ascent at all—for "who has touched this and remained clean?" Rather, the intent is [that] a single attribute, or two attributes, have no ascent; but when all three lines unite to ascend, each and every line to its root, then they are exalted even as far as the Ein Sof, as explained in the preceding chapter concerning the three points. And likewise, even regarding a single attribute, it may be that Keter descends upon Gevurah, and the like. And let us return to our matter. Behold, after all the extremities had been emanated in Binah in the order stated—behold, by the power of Chokhmah, Binah emanated the Chesed within her, together with the Netzach that is comprised in her with Chesed. And the reason He gave Chesed precedence over Gevurah is that "one opens with [the argument for] acquittal first"; and therefore He was compelled to give Chesed precedence. And to emanate Tiferet in its [usual] way is impossible, since Tiferet is the mediator between the extremities—and if there is no dispute, what is there to mediate? Therefore He was compelled to emanate Chesed first. And afterward Binah, by the power of her own self, emanated Gevurah and Hod comprised within Gevurah—for Netzach is a branch of Chesed and Hod a branch of Gevurah. And afterward Binah emanated, by the power of Keter, the double-faced, to be mediators between the right, the line of Chesed, and the left, the line of Din. And since the precedence of the double-faced precedes, in their emanation, Gedulah and Gevurah—as is proven above, that they are prior, [in] that their emanation is from Keter—therefore they have a mode [ranking] above Chesed and Gevurah. And this is the reason that, most of the time, we count Tiferet as the seventh from below upward, to indicate that it is above Chesed and Gevurah, in the secret of this supernal aspect [of it], which is prior to Gedulah and Gevurah, and which is its concealed aspect, [that] in the secret of its concealment in Binah. But from the side of its emanation below, it is the fifth from below upward, which indicates its being below Gedulah and Gevurah in the order of its emanation. And likewise this matter [applies] to Yesod, as we explained above in chapters 1 and 2.

And behold, it is now found that three Sefirot were emanated: Chesed from the side of Chokhmah, Gevurah from the side of Binah, [and] Tiferet from the side of Keter—and all by means of Binah. And there is now no room for the disputant to dissent and to say that seven were emanated together from Binah; for so it is, that within each and every one of the three patriarchs one branch was emanated. And thus the words of the Gaon are likewise correct, that they were emanated in [sequential] order, for so the matter was, [in] that each and every one precedes its fellow, as we have explained; and thus the words of my teacher, may God preserve and keep him, are [also] correct. Afterward Chesed revealed Netzach by the power of Chokhmah; and afterward Gevurah revealed Hod by the power of Binah; and afterward Tiferet revealed the Yesod concealed within it by the power of Keter. And it will indeed be found, in truth, that Yesod, with respect to its aspect, [together] with Tiferet, is prior to Netzach and Hod—even though it is posterior, for the reason we explained regarding Tiferet.

And behold, afterward—through our many iniquities—the moon was diminished and was banished from her place, and descended to be the tenth, below Yesod, and Yesod became the ninth, as we shall expand on this matter in the Gate of the Diminishment of the Moon.

And behold, this exposition is hereby set in order and settled according to its proper measure, and all the views are brought to completion together with the view that obligates [the conclusion] that they were emanated one after another in [sequential] order, as we have explained. For first Keter was emanated; and afterward Chokhmah was emanated from Keter; and from Chokhmah, Binah was emanated; and from Binah, Chesed was emanated—for so it was, [in] that, although its root is in Chokhmah, it was emanated by means of Binah. And afterward Gevurah was emanated from Chesed—for, although its root is from Binah, we do not deny that by way of Chesed it was revealed to its place, and [that] it passed through her [Chesed] in a manner of passage, by way of a parable to the human intellect. And thus he was precise [in] the language of Rashbi, peace be upon him (Bereshit, folio 32b), who said, "the waters departed and begot darkness"—the meaning [being]: they conceived darkness, for there was a conception, [in] that they conceived from the darkness, after the manner of [the son] that is emanated from the male into the belly of the female, and the female conceives from him—and his root is not from the female but from the male, who deposited him in the belly of the female. And likewise Chesed conceived from Gevurah, and the root of Gevurah was emanated into it from Binah. And likewise Tiferet was emanated, by the power of Keter, from Binah, by way of Chesed and by way of Gevurah, to its fitting place; and afterward Netzach was emanated from Chesed, by way of the grades, to its fitting place; and afterward Hod was emanated from Gevurah; and afterward Yesod from Tiferet, in the manner of the Sefirot mentioned; and afterward Malkhut, by means of the diminishment. And thus the words of Rashbi, who obligated [the conclusion] that they were emanated sevenfold from within Binah, are explained—for so it was, [in] that there the seven Sefirot were found together, and from within her they were emanated below, as explained above concerning the three kinds of emanation within Binah. And thus the words of my teacher, may God preserve and keep him, are explained [with] sufficient explanation; and this is the foundation of our intent regarding the order of the Emanation. [This is so] even though we have no need of the reason why from Keter three were emanated, and from Chokhmah two, and from Binah two—since the matter of the double-faced has already been explained, that the two of them are one, and "they were two halves of one body," and Yesod within them unites them, and "body and covenant are reckoned as one"; and by means of one of these two reasons all is set in order.

And further, [the reason is] that the secret of the line of mercy, which mediates between the right and the left, [has] its principal mediation between Gedulah and Gevurah—in the secret of the element of air and the element of earth, both of which together mediate between fire and water, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Mediators; let it be examined in its place. Nonetheless, we do require that reason for the matter of Da'at, which is the root of mercy, in the matter of "and they were all comprised in wisdom, understanding, and knowledge [Chokhmah, Tevunah, and Da'at]," which we wrote above in chapter 3; and the matter will be explained at length in the Gate of Essence and Governance.
And behold, with this the chapter is concluded, and this gate is completed—by the grace of the One who graciously grants knowledge to man.
The Sixth Gate: The Order of Their Standing:

The intent in this gate is [to treat] what we have seen—[namely] that the later Kabbalists depict for themselves figures concerning the Sefirot, this one saying thus and that one saying thus; and in truth not one of the views is fully satisfactory. And in this gate we shall explain the figure of most of the views, and we shall reveal the way that a person should choose for himself.
Chapter One:

Concerning the figure of the Sefirot—that is to say, the order of their standing—the views concerning it are many, and the Kabbalists have depicted for themselves figures on large parchments (yeri'ot) and called them an "ilan" [Tree]. There is one who wished to depict them in the figure of an alef. How so? They divided the head into three parts: the [first] to the supernal Keter, and the right side of the head [of the] alef [to] Chokhmah, and the left to Binah. And the line that is below the yod—which is the vav of the alef—its right "head" he called Chesed, and its left "head" Gevurah, and the middle Tiferet. And from the appearance of its loins downward: that which corresponds to the right [is] Netzach, and that which corresponds to the left [is] Hod, and that which is between the two [is] Yesod, and the lower thorn [is] Malkhut. And this is its figure:

Behold, they intended to depict the figure of the supernal Man in the figure of an alef, to allude that the whole of it is a perfect union: although we say "ten Sefirot"—which indicates separate things—the whole of it is a perfect union, and this he indicated by the likeness of an alef. And there is some support for this view in the words of Rashbi in Sefer ha-Tikkunim (Tikkun 55), and these are his words: "Come and see: this skull is [the letter] alef, like this; it has four sides, [and] in them YHVH is one and His Name is one—there is none else besides Him," etc. Thus far [his words].
And although his words and his figure are not exactly as above,

nonetheless, from it [it] appears that the intent of the Name—which is ten Sefirot, as is known—is alluded to in the figure of the alef, to allude to ten Sefirot unified [in] a perfect unity, an equal unity. And this is what it says, "in them YHVH is one and His Name is one"—the meaning [being] to indicate that He and His Name are unified, although His Name indicates ten Sefirot. And behold, the existence of the alef indicates the union.

And the matter of the ten digits and the ten digits—its place is not here, and it will be explained in the Gate of the Soul, chapter 8. And others depicted the figure of the ten Sefirot in the figure of an alef, like this:

And it is true that the first figure is the most acceptable, for it is close to the tradition [Kabbalah] in the hand of most of the Kabbalists, as we shall explain. And the intent of these Kabbalists is not to say that this is literally the secret of their standing—for in the [reality of the] mode of this figure there are no channels, nor right and left intrinsically (that is to say, Chesed and Din)—but rather their intent is to indicate the complete union: just as the alef means "one," so the ten Sefirot are a perfect unity. And he further intended by this to make the figure of a patach at its [upper] thorn, above Keter, to allude that Keter is not a first cause, God forbid, but [that] above it [is] the sole Lord who rules over all of them and emanates effluence upon them; and one patach below, at Malkhut, to allude that the intent of all this is for the governance of the lower beings, and that it [Malkhut] is a passage for the effluence emanated from the First Cause to His creatures, as we have explained in the preceding gates. Further, another figure Rabbi Moshe de León wrote in the Sefer ha-Shem that he composed, and he said that it depends on the view of Sefer ha-Bahir; and some Kabbalists followed this way, and in particular because they wished to rely on it [to support] the matter of "their end is embedded in their beginning"—for the end, which is Malkhut, is embedded in the beginning, which is Keter. And its figure is like this:

And their view concerning this figure, in the matter of "their end is embedded in their beginning," is not settled at all, as the one who delves will see with his intellect; rather, the matter of "their end is embedded in their beginning" is a great secret explained in the Tikkunim in the words of Rashbi, and we shall explain it in the Gate "From Below to Above". Further, there are those who wrote a figure close to the agreement of the Kabbalists, and it is like this:

And Rabbi Moshe de León likewise copied it in the Sefer ha-Shem, and wrote: "And this view does not arise well according to the Kabbalah." But Rabbi Shem Tov ben Rabbi Shem Tov annotated upon it in the margin, [and] these are his words: "In my humble opinion, this view does not conflict with the other views, and it is very deep. And he counted ten Sefirot from the known Keter, whose name is like the name of its master—it is the supernal Keter, the sole Lord; and this is called in Sefer Yetzirah 'He sealed the height' (with yod) [with YHV], and it is called Keter like it, for it encompasses all the Sefirot. And this is the secret of Thought emanated from the supernal Keter—[namely] Chokhmah, that is to say, the more revealed [one]; and it, by the power of the Ein Sof, brings forth the actions, [so as] to act in the likeness of the female, [and] therefore it is on the left. And Binah is called thus [because] she is between the two; in the secret of the Da'at hidden in her [which] is the emanation of the known Keter, in the secret of [the] supernal Keter. And this is the secret of the three names that the Name revealed to Moses at the bush; and the second, in the second name, is entirely the likeness of the female. Concerning this [there is] a very deep secret." Thus far [his words].

And behold, he intended to give a reason for Binah's being in the middle, [and] for Chokhmah's being on the left. And the beginning of his words may be understood somewhat by the reasoning of the view that is his, which we wrote in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof is the Keter, chapter 3. But in truth, [to engage in] length concerning this reasoning—that Chokhmah is on the left, and Keter on the right, and Binah in the middle—is a vain exercise, for it is a strange and rejected reasoning; for they hold that Chokhmah is Din, and Binah mediates between Chokhmah and Keter. And this view is null, as we shall expound at length in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 5. And the correct view, the received [one], agreed upon in the mouth of all the Kabbalists, is this; and Rabbi Moshe de León wrote it in the Sefer ha-Shem, [and] these are his words: "And there is another view, comely and very acceptable, surpassing them all, and it is true: that the three upper ones are like a segolta." And it is this:

And [these are] the gracious words of a wise man, for it is fine sifted flour. And this way was adopted by Rabbi Yehudah Chayyat in his book, and he gave a sign for the matter: "segolta, segol, segol"—for the three first ones [are] a segolta, the three second ones a segol, and the three third ones a segol, and Malkhut receives from all of them, below all of them. However, concerning Malkhut he wrote things that are forbidden to hear—and may his Master forgive him. And this figure is likewise agreed upon and necessitated from the words of Rashbi in many places. And in the interpretation of the points [vowels] he holds that the three first ones are a segolta, the segolta's allusion being among them; and likewise he holds that the segol [signifies] the three patriarchs, and at times he holds that they are Netzach-Hod-Yesod [NHY]—[which] indicates that this view is agreed upon and necessitated. He further explained, in another place—and it is a great proof for this view—[and] these are his words, in Sefer Ra'aya Mehemna (Beha'alotekha, folio 153): "And Chokhmah, Chesed, [and] Netzach shall be on the right, for on their account David said, 'The right hand of YHVH does valiantly, the right hand of YHVH is exalted, the right hand of YHVH does valiantly.' And three on the left shall be bound together, which are Binah, Gevurah, [and] Hod. And three grades of the middle—Keter, Tiferet, [and] Yesod—which bind [the] right and [the] left." Thus far [his words].

Behold, he explained explicitly that Chokhmah, Chesed, [and] Netzach are on the right, and Binah, Gevurah, [and Hod] are on the left, and Keter, Tiferet, [and] Yesod [are] in the middle. And according to their order known to us, it is necessitated that they be in the manner that we depicted above. And the being of Malkhut beneath Yesod is necessitated, for she receives from him, and he is the "best man" between her and her husband, and it is necessitated that she be beneath him.

And further, [it is necessitated] because she is the gate of entry, as is necessitated from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, [in] places too many to number. This matter was further explained in the Tikkunim (in Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, folio 112), [and] these are its words: "And the nine Sefirot are arranged in threes upon the central pillar, like this: Chokhmah-Chesed-Netzach, Keter-Tiferet-Yesod, Binah-Gevurah-Hod; Malkhut is the tenth to them and the fourth to them." Thus far [its words].

And the intent is clear: that the Sefirot are arranged three [by] three. And once we have known this matter, of necessity their order is: Keter, Tiferet, Yesod in the middle—because Tiferet and Yesod are intermediaries and mediators between Din and mercy, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Mediators. And therefore their depiction in this figure that we depicted above was required. It was further explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 69, folio 101b), [and] these are its words: "Keter over Chokhmah and Binah is a segolta—a cholam over a tzeirei. A segol is a dot beneath the tzeirei. Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet below. Netzach, Hod, Yesod in the middle is a shuruk; and so, when Tiferet is in the middle, it is a shalshelet." Thus far [its words], for our matter.

And behold, he said that Keter [is] over Chokhmah and Binah in the figure of a segolta. And he said that Tiferet [is] below Gedulah and Gevurah, and this is a segol. [It is] true that at times it [Tiferet] will be exactly between Gedulah and Gevurah, and then it will be in the figure of a shalshelet—and this is what it says, "when Tiferet is in the middle, it is a shalshelet." And likewise Yesod [is] between Netzach and Hod, and they are a shuruk, which are three dots in one row—although they are not diagonal, as is its norm. Thus far. Thus, from these passages, the figure that most of the commentators depicted for the Sefirot is necessitated; and it is a correct reasoning, and there is no doubt in it.

After we have stood, in the preceding chapter, to set up the matter of the Emanation in the figure upon which all the Kabbalists, or most of them, have agreed, and we have necessitated it by means of some passages from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Tikkunim—we have seen [fit] to copy here the reasoning of the author of Me'irat Einayim, [showing] that from these passages there is a refutation of his words, [for] he is opposed to all the Kabbalists. And these are his words, in [the] portion [of] Terumah. First he wrote, in the name of Rabbi Shem Tov, one figure, and it accords with the agreed-upon figure and does not conflict with the figure that we necessitated in the preceding chapter, except in the three first ones; and this is its figure:

And although the order of these three first ones is the reasoning of the author of Me'irat Einayim and the view of Rabbi Todros ha-Levi in Sefer ha-Ma'arekhet—and Rabbi Moshe de León likewise wrote something of this reasoning—

Behold, from the passages that we necessitated in the preceding figure, in the preceding chapter, there is found an explicit refutation of their words, and there is no need to be lengthy. He further wrote in Sefer Me'irat Einayim, in the aforementioned portion, [and] these are his words: "Behold, I depict for you the figure of the ten Sefirot in their correct, true positioning, for [the one] to whom the Name, may He be blessed, has given eyes to see and a heart to understand; and I have not seen one in a thousand among all the Kabbalists who perceived this matter, apart from my teacher, from whom I received [it]." And this is it:

And whoever says of this form that it is reversed—he is of a perverse generation; and if the speaker's intent is good, his mind is reversed. He seeks to see the hinder parts, whereas we [see] the face, for it is said, "I have set YHVH always before me," etc. And although the Sefirot are nothing but holy spirit—spiritual thoughts, unified one to another [in] a true union, and all unified in the Ein Sof, in [literally] the Ein Sof—and above there is neither right nor left, but rather these incline rightward, to acquittal, and therefore [the right] is called right and mercy, and these incline leftward, to liability, and therefore [the left] is called left and Din—nonetheless, behold, David, peace be upon him, said, "I have set YHVH always before me," etc. (Psalms 16:8). And over and above all this, our Sages of blessed memory said (Yoma, folio 53): when a person takes three steps [back], he gives "peace" to his left first, because the Shekhinah is opposite him; and thus he bows to the right of the Shekhinah, and afterward gives "peace" to his right, which is the left of the Shekhinah. Thus far [his words].

And we have several responses to him. First, regarding what he said—that he [the opponent] seeks to see the hinder parts, whereas we [see] the face: even according to him there is no substance in this reasoning, for so it is fitting not to gaze upon the face, as it is written (Exodus 33:23), "and you shall see My back, but My face shall not be seen." And even [as for] the hinder parts—how many "hinder parts of hinder parts" are [the ones] that are seen!—all the more so [is it not fitting] to gaze upon the awesome face (see in Tikkun 69, folio 111, in what was said concerning "you shall not be able to see My face"). And this is the opposite of the correct view.

And further, [the truth is] that the matter is the opposite of his view, for the face is in this order: right opposite right, and left opposite left. And [there is] a proof from the matter of the tefillin: for the first portion, Kadesh—which is Chokhmah—is at the right of the reader and the left of the one laying [the tefillin]; and the portion Ve-haya im shamoa—which is Gevurah—is at the right of the one laying [them] and the left of the reader. But according to his view it should be the opposite, for the one laying [them] lays [them] right opposite right and left opposite left, and the reader, who is opposite him, would have the left toward the right and the right toward the left. And there is no [valid] response from [the fact that] Ve-haya ki yevi'akha—which is Binah—and Shema—which is Gedulah—are in [direct] correspondence: Shema, Gedulah, at the right of the one laying [them], and Ve-haya ki yevi'akha at his left. This is no response at all; for, on the contrary, Chokhmah and Gevurah are the principal [proof] for this matter, for several reasons: for it is fitting to arrange Chokhmah to the right, since it is the rightmost, the head of all the Sefirot, and Gevurah [is] the principal leftmost, [tending] to liability. And why should we reverse these, which are principal, on account of two [others] that are [only] the root of the right and the left?

And further, [the proof holds] because Shema, too, [is] at the right of the reader in the aspect of Ve-haya im shamoa; and likewise Ve-haya ki yevi'akha [is] at the left of the reader in the aspect of Kadesh. And this is a compelling proof—what it is impossible to say of Kadesh and Ve-haya im shamoa—that, with respect to the aspect of all of them, Kadesh is always at the left of the one laying [them] and the right of the reader, and Ve-haya im shamoa at the right of the one laying [them] and the left of the reader. And this is certainly a refutation of the words of the author of Sefer Me'irat Einayim.

And [there is] a further proof from the ascent of the altar, for there [is] the foundation of the union, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar (Bamidbar, folio 120); and we have copied [its] language in the Gate of Self and Vessels, chapter 1, and in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter 21.

And behold, the ascent of it [the altar] was by the ramp, and the ramp was on the south of the altar; and when [the priest] was ascending, he would turn to the southeast corner, which is the right of the one ascending. And were it true as the words of Sefer Me'irat Einayim, it would be fitting that he turn to his left, for there [would be] the right opposite him; and it would be fitting that the ramp be on the north of the altar, so that in his ascent by the ramp he would turn to the left of the one ascending—that is, the right that is opposite [him]—and turn to the northeast corner, in this order, etc. Rather, what have you to say? That [as for] this figure, there is no doubt that it is reversed, and the true figure is the figure agreed upon in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, [namely] that the right [corresponds] to the right and the left to the left. And therefore they expounded, "every turn that you turn shall be only to the right"—and this is the actual right of a person, [such] that "a left opposite him" and "a right opposite him" have no place there. And likewise they expounded concerning Abraham our father, peace be upon him, that all his turnings were to [the side of] Chesed. A further response to what he wished to derive support [for] from the verse "I have set YHVH always before me": it is no proof, for David, peace be upon him, would say so on account of the fear of the Name [being] before his face all the day, and he would think as if the Shekhinah were opposite him perpetually, and he [were] like a servant before the King, so as not to waver from his service, neither little nor much. And [as for] what he wished to derive support [for] from the matter of the three steps—shall we, then, set aside all the rest of the matters of the [Temple] service and bring a proof from a single detail, [namely] the matter of the steps?

Furthermore, there is no proof at all; for [though] you raise an objection against me from the view of Rava, who said "his right" [means] the right of the Holy One, blessed be He, [and] "his left" the left of the Holy One, blessed be He—I [can] support myself from the view of Abaye, who reckoned "his right" [as] his own right and "his left" his own left literally, [so as] to reckon that the matter of the steps is like the intent of the other commandments and deeds. Until Rava taught him that the meaning of "his right" is, that is to say, the right of the Holy One, blessed be He, [and] "his left" the left of the Holy One, blessed be He—the opposite of the other things. And the reason is that now, when one comes to take leave, he comes to teach a person not to think that his words are for naught and in vain, God forbid, but rather that he should be assured that his words were heard—like a person who speaks with the King in the inner chamber and takes leave of the King in peace and love. Or it is possible [that it is] to show a person his faith: that even though he unified the supernal worlds by the "hinder parts" that are seen, nonetheless the Holy One, blessed be He, hearkened to him by the "awesome face." Therefore, when he comes to take leave, he gives peace to the right of the Holy One, blessed be He, which is his [own] left. And in this manner we can explain the verse "I have set YHVH always before me," etc. Or it is possible that we should say that the matter of the peace[-giving] in this is for the [angel] who receives the prayer and makes it into crowns for his Master—even though he said "the right of the Holy One" and "his left." So too they said (in tractate Berakhot, fol. 7): Rabbi Ishmael said, "I saw Aktariel Yah YHVH Tzeva'ot," etc.—and he is the one who receives the prayers, and he is not the King of Glory; for if so, he would not have said "I saw" literally, God forbid. And as is known, Aktariel is a prince on high and not a god. And nevertheless there is no difficulty [in] his saying "Yah YHVH Tzeva'ot," for the angels are called by the name of their Master, by the Glory that hovers over them. And so it says concerning Abraham (Genesis 18:3), "And he said, my Lord [Adonai], do not pass on," and the Sages, of blessed memory, explained that he said [it] to the greatest of them—and the intent is the Glory that hovers over and clothes itself in them, which is the Shekhinah. And so [it is] in the matter of Aktariel, for concerning the Glory that clothes itself in him it says "Yah YHVH Tzeva'ot." And so [it is] in the matter of "He who makes peace," that he gives peace to the right opposite him and to the left opposite him because the Glory hovers over him and clothes itself in him; and there a literal left and a literal right apply. And this secret depends on the knowledge of the matter of the angels; it will be explained in the Gate of the Palaces.

Furthermore, another response, namely: in that it is well known that man—his forms, his structure, his limbs, his arteries, and his sinews—is the likeness of a supernal reflection. And man is a supernal shadow that became corporealized and thickened in this world, and he is the likeness of a supernal reflection appearing in this world. If so, it is fitting that his right [correspond] to the right of the supernal things and his left to the left of the supernal things—like the matter of the shadow, whose right is opposite the right of its root. And this matter is a root and a fundamental principle in faith and in piety.

Furthermore, that in truth there is above neither right nor left, but all is right and all is left. And a great proof [is] from the matter of the Tablets, which were one of the supernal branches whose spirituality became corporealized and thickened for the honor of Israel; and the Sages, of blessed memory, testified concerning them (Shekalim, fol. 16) that the Ten Commandments were visible in them from every side and from every direction and from every corner. And if in [something] corporealized [it is] so—that there is in it neither right nor left, but all is right and all is left—how much more so, and a fortiori, in the fineness of the spiritual that is elevated above every cause, may it be praised and exalted. And if we decree right and left, it is in the aspect of merit and liability, as in the matter of what they said, "these incline to the left, to liability, and these incline to the right, to merit." And it is known that the matter of merit and liability is in our terms, not in the terms of the spiritual [realm]—rather in the terms of its actions toward its creatures. If so, His right is our right and His left is our left, and there is no distinction between this and that.

And the matter of the steps is according to one of the ways we explained. And we find ourselves learning that the principal, correct figure in this is according to what we drew in the previous chapter and established from the views of Rashbi, peace be upon him: three to the right, three to the left, three in the middle, and Malkhut receiving from them all. This is what emerges from the words of most of the Kabbalists. And there is yet [another] vision, and we shall explain it in the coming chapters, with the help of the Rock and His salvation.

After we have occupied ourselves in the previous chapters with the investigation of the figure of the standing of the pure and holy Emanation, and the figure agreed upon in the mouth of all the Kabbalists has emerged by our consensus—it is our wish to disclose to the ear of the discerning, concerning this figure, what its essence and its matter are and what the intent of its depiction is. And before everything, it is necessary to preface: although we say "right" and "left," there is there neither right nor left in their place, [and] neither back nor face. Rather, the matter of the Sefirot is as we shall explain.

And behold, it is known that every cause encompasses what it causes, and every cause encompasses its effect, and the effect is encompassed by its cause—just as the point of the earth is in the middle of the firmament, and the firmament surrounds the earth, and the firmament is the cause of all the things that are beneath the heavens, by the will of the Maker; as is well known among the investigators, that the motion of the spheres is the cause of the compounding of the elements. And Rambam, of blessed memory, explained [this] in the fourth [chapter] of Hilkhot Yesodei ha-Torah, and said that the motion of the spheres necessitates the compounding of the elements in the lower world. And likewise the diurnal sphere encompasses all the spheres and is their cause, to the point that it turns them [in] the opposite of their [own] motion—which is from west to east—and it turns them from east to west, by the will of their Maker. And above all, encompassing all, is the sphere of the Intellect. And so [it is] with the ascent of the grades, for each and every one encompasses all the grades that are below it. And this appears [to be] of necessity, and in particular when one examines the chapters of the Account of Creation, he will rejoice and be glad, and the love of this premise of ours will be the more steeped in his heart. And there is a proof for this from the dictum of Resh Lakish (in Chagigah, fol. 12), and these are [the] words: Rabbi Yehudah said, there are two firmaments, for it is said, "Behold, to YHVH your God belong the heavens and the heaven of heavens." Resh Lakish said [there are] seven, and these are they: Vilon, Raki'a, Shechakim, Zevul, Ma'on, Makhon, Aravot. Vilon serves no purpose except [that] it enters at morning and goes out at evening and renews each day the work of creation, for it is said, "who stretches out the heavens like a curtain [dok]." Raki'a—[the firmament] in which are the sun and moon, stars and constellations, fixed [in it], for it is said, "And God set them in the firmament of the heavens." Shechakim—[the firmament] in which millstones stand and grind manna for the righteous, for it is said, "And He commanded the skies [shechakim] above," etc., "and He rained down upon them manna to eat." Zevul—in which are [the heavenly] Jerusalem and the Temple, and an altar is built, and Michael the great prince stands and offers an offering upon it, for it is said, "I have surely built You a house of habitation [zevul], a place for You to dwell in forever." And whence [do we know] that it is called heaven? For it is written, "Look down from heaven and see, from Your holy and glorious habitation [zevul]." Ma'on—in which are companies of ministering angels who recite song by night and are silent by day, for the sake of the honor of Israel, for it is said, "By day YHVH commands His lovingkindness," etc., and what is the reason, etc.—thus far [the passage], to our purpose.

And behold, to say that these seven firmaments are the seven firmaments [i.e., spheres] that the astronomers counted is impossible—for he said that in one of these seven are the sun and moon, stars and constellations; and if these seven firmaments were the seven [spheres] that the astronomers counted, it would have been fitting that he count eight: seven for the seven planets, and one for the constellations. And such is not his intent, for he said that the sun and moon, stars and constellations are in one of the seven firmaments, whose name is Raki'a. And to explain that the Sages, of blessed memory, dispute with the astronomers—holding that the sun and moon, stars and constellations are fixed in a single sphere alone—[that too] is impossible. And therefore the sages of Israel do not dispute with the sages of the [other] nations except [on the question of] whether the sphere is fixed and the constellation revolves, or the constellation is fixed and the sphere revolves; but as to the number of the spheres they do not dispute.

Furthermore, the sages of Israel did retract and concede to the sages of the nations that the constellation is fixed and the sphere revolves; but as to the number of the spheres they do not dispute. And since the constellation is fixed and the sphere revolves, a multiplicity of spheres is necessitated according to the number of the constellations, which differ in their courses—and this is compelling. And the correct reason for this is that the totality of all the nine spheres is in one firmament. And likewise all the rest of the firmaments are supernal worlds, and in each one of them are many, many firmaments. And the sages who speak on the matter of the Account of Creation have already said that the number of the firmaments is like the count of [the word] "the heavens" [ha-shamayim] mentioned in the verse (Ezekiel 1:1), "the heavens were opened and I saw visions of God"—and their number is nine hundred and fifty-five; for the closed mem of "ha-shamayim" amounts to six hundred, it being the second letter of the doubles [the final mem]; and they are all included in a short number, [whether] seven firmaments, or nine, or five—for all of them have support and corroboration; and there is no place to elaborate.

And behold, when he said "the sun and moon, stars and constellations," he there included the totality of all the firmaments that the astronomers counted. And this is no wonder, for the astronomers counted similarly [in another case]: they said that the sphere of the moon is one, whereas they [also] said explicitly that they are three; and likewise all the spheres, their number is eighteen, as Rambam explained in the third [chapter] of Hilkhot Yesodei ha-Torah. And so [Resh Lakish] included them all in one firmament—and this reasoning is sufficient and correct by way of the plain sense. But in truth he counted in these firmaments none but spiritual matters, as is explained in the Zohar and the Ra'aya Mehemna; and so he designates those spiritual things by the term "firmaments," since they all encompass the world and the spheres. And so [it is with] everything, for the higher the grades ascend, the [more] they surround the grades within them. And so, in this manner, [is] the matter of the Sefirot: for they are all within Ein Sof, the King who reigns; and within Keter, Chokhmah; and within Chokhmah, Binah; and within Binah, Chesed; and within Chesed, Gevurah; and within Gevurah, Tiferet; and within Tiferet, Netzach; and within Netzach, Hod; and within Hod, Yesod; and within Yesod, Malkhut. And within Malkhut, Beriah; and within Beriah, Yetzirah; and within Yetzirah, Asiyah. And in them are included the matter of the Account of Creation and the Account of the Chariot. Thus the chariots are found within Malkhut. And the Sages, of blessed memory, explained in the chapters of the Chariot [matters] concerning the chariots and the thrones. And within those things that are in the chapters of the Chariot [are] those things that are in the chapters of the Account of Creation; and within those things that are in the chapters of the Account of Creation, the spheres; and within the spheres, the earth; and within the earth, at its navel, are seven earths. And concerning this matter of seven earths we were astonished by this very existence, to the point that it arose in our mind to say that the matter of the seven earths stated in the Account of Creation and in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, is the matter of the climes that the astronomers divided. Until God, in His mercy, favored us and brought to our hand many dicta that refute this view and concur that there are literally seven earths within the earth. And these are the words of the Zohar, Parashat Vayikra (fol. 9b): Rabbi Yehudah opened: "And God said, let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters." Come and see: at the hour when the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world, He created seven firmaments above, [and] created seven earths below; seven seas, seven rivers, seven days, seven weeks, seven years, seven times, [and] seven thousand years that the world is to be. The Holy One, blessed be He, [is] in the seventh of all. Seven skies [another reading: firmaments] above, and all is one. And in each and every one [are] ministers, stars, and constellations that serve in each and every firmament; and in all of them are those chariots, these upon these, to receive upon themselves the yoke of the kingship of their Master. And in all the firmaments there are chariots and ministers differing one from another, these upon these: some of them with six wings and some of them with four wings; some of them with four faces, some of them with two faces, some of them with one; some of them flaming fire, some of them water, some of them spirit—as it is written, "He makes His angels spirits, His ministers a flaming fire." And all these firmaments [are] these upon these, like the layers of an onion, these below and these above. Each and every firmament goes and trembles from the fear of their Master; by His mouth they journey and by His mouth they stand. And higher than all of them [is] the Holy One, blessed be He, who carries them all by His strength and His might. In like manner [are] the seven earths below, and they are all inhabited—except that these are higher and these are lower. And the land of Israel is higher than all of them, and Jerusalem [is] higher than all the inhabited world. And our companions, the dwellers of the south, saw in the books of the ancients and in the Book of Adam that thus He divides all those earths, [such] that all of them are found below in like manner to those firmaments above, these upon these and these upon these. And between each and every earth [is] a firmament that separates between this and that; and therefore all the earths are distinguished by names, and between them are the Garden of Eden and Gehinnom; and among them are creatures differing one from another, in like manner to those chariots above—some of them with two faces, some with four, some with one, and the appearance of these is not like [that of] those. And should you say: behold, all the inhabitants of the world came forth from Adam—and did Adam descend to all those earths and beget children? And how many wives did he have? Rather, Adam was found only in this world, the highest of all, which is called Tevel (the earth-realm humans inhabit), as it is written, "playing in His Tevel [His earth]." And this Tevel is joined to the firmament above and is bound to the supernal Name, as it is written, "and He shall judge Tevel in righteousness"—"in righteousness" indeed. And therefore the children of Adam are found in this higher [earth] that is called Tevel, and they are higher than all, in like manner to that which is above. What is the reason? Just as above, over all the firmaments there is a firmament higher than all, and above [it] is found the Throne of the Holy One, blessed be He—as it is said, "like the appearance of a sapphire stone, the likeness of a throne, and upon the likeness of the throne a likeness like the appearance of a man upon it above"—so too here, in this Tevel is found the King of all; and what is He? Adam [a man]—that which is not found in all the lower [earths]. And those lower ones, whence do they come? Rather, from the residue of the earth and the aid of the firmament above, creatures come forth differing one from another. Some of them [are] in their garments [clothed], some of them in husks like those worms that are found in the earth, some of them in red, black, and white husks, and some of them of all colors. Thus are all the creatures of this kind. And they do not endure in [continued] existence except [for] ten years or more. And in the Book of Rav Hamnuna the Elder it is explained further: that the whole inhabited world revolves in a circle like a ball, these below and these above; and all those creatures differ [according to] the difference of the air [climate] in each and every place, and they stand in their existence like other human beings. And therefore there is a place in the inhabited world where, when it is light for these, it is dark for those: for these [it is] day and for those night; and there is a place where it is all day, and no night is found in it except [for] one brief hour. And this which is stated in the books of the ancients and in the Book of Adam the First, thus it is. For so it is written, "I praise You, for I am awesomely wondrous; wondrous are Your works," and it is written, "How manifold are Your works, O YHVH." And concerning this, all is well; and this secret has been delivered to the masters of wisdom and not to dividers of boundaries, because it is a deep secret of the Torah. In like manner [there is something] in the sea, in which there are many creatures differing one from another, as it is written, "This [is] the sea, great and broad of hands," "there ships go," etc. And all depends one upon the other and is bound one to the other, and all [is] in like manner to that which is above; and in all the worlds [there is] nothing ruling over them all except Adam, and the Holy One, blessed be He, [is] above him. Rabbi Nehorai the Elder set out upon the Great Sea, and the sea raged, and all those who were in the ship perished. And a miracle was wrought for him, and he descended by known paths into the heart of the sea, and came out beneath the sea to one inhabited [land]; and he saw [some] of those creatures, all of them small, and they were reciting a prayer, and he did not know what they were saying. A miracle was wrought for him and he ascended. He said: Happy are the righteous who toil in the Torah and know the hidden things of the supernal secrets! Woe to those who dispute their words and do not believe! From that day on, when he would come to the study-house and they recited words of Torah, he would weep. They said to him: And why do you weep? He said to them: Because I transgressed against the faithfulness of the words of the Rabbis, and I fear the judgment of that world. Thus far [the passage].

And we know that these things are difficult for the human intellect and terrifying [to] the heart of those who examine [them]. And it is not fitting for one who believes in their tradition to doubt them; for not in vain did the Zohar adduce that Rabbi Nehorai doubted [it], even though he was [one] of the great ones of Israel and of the transmitters of the [oral] tradition, as is evident from the Midrashim and from the Gemara—whether we wish to say that he was Rabbi Meir, who is Rabbi Nehorai, as is explained in tractate [Eruvin] (fol. 13), or whether we say that he was other than him, as is evident from the words of this passage, that he was prior to Rashbi, peace be upon him, or in his time, and was a man of renown and distinguished in his generation. And so it is evident in Midrash Ruth from the Zohar, and likewise in Sefer ha-Bahir. And despite the abundance of his piety and his wisdom, he doubted it and was punished in the matter of the loss of the ship, and saw with his [own] eye [some] of the matter; and therefore those who remain shall hear and fear and shall sin no more presumptuously.

And behold, from the words of the passage it is understood how they themselves were not expert in this matter with clarity; as is evident from his proofs from the Book of Adam the First and from the Book of Rav Hamnuna, it appears that the words were faint in their hearts and not settled, as the examiner will see and read. And the matters are compelling of themselves, by the power of the true tradition, and there is no [room] to question. And even though there results from this, for the examiner, a doubt or doubts—as happens to us—it is fitting to conceal them and hide them, since they have at present no resolution, so that no one of those slack in [the study of] the words of the Sages, of blessed memory, will come and gibe from his words. And therefore let us hope [that] the mercy of God will favor us with the knowledge of this in truth, without error in the heart. And at present there is nothing to convey to another at all except the strength of the faith transmitted in this from this passage. And [as for] the rest, our eyes are toward YHVH our God, until He favors us and brings forth our judgment to light; and therefore we shall not bring ourselves into the explanation of the passage, neither much nor little. And however it be, behold, it is compelling from this passage that at the navel of the earth there are seven earths, this within that, in the manner of the spheres; and in this manner we ascend from the point of the earth up to the First Cause, the Ein Sof, blessed be He, and all the things are within it. And with this we can understand what they said, "He is the place of the world, and the world is not His place."
