And "the glory of God is to conceal a matter," and this matter does not necessitate, God forbid, a place for His glory, may He be exalted—even though there are those who say that permission has already been given to ascribe place, [that is,] rank. And even from this we flee; rather, [we say] that His glory fills the whole earth. For even of the ninth sphere they said that from it upward place ceases, and it is without place—how much more so, higher and higher. And what we say here concerning the matter of a Sefirah within the Sefirot—and in these matters—the intent is not that the plain sense of the things is so, God forbid, for this is a criminal iniquity and is a fire that consumes unto destruction; for one who believes in things like these, God forbid, corporealizes the Godhead, and this is the opposite of the perfect faith that He is not a body nor a force in a body. And likewise all the Emanation, since it is close to Him, is divested of body and its accidents; for each one nearer [is] nearer than its fellow, [more] sanctified than its fellow. And what we say [as] "this above that" is priority of rank, not priority of place, as we shall explain. And let the examiner set these words of ours before his eyes, and let him not be among those who think evil, and let him not think that He is one who occupies place; for on the contrary, He is the place of the world and has no place, and He brought forth the place in which every occupier of place came to be. And before the creation of the occupiers of place, He had to create the place in which the occupiers of place would be created. And the investigators have already agreed that from the ninth sphere upward there is no place, and the tenth sphere of the Intellect, which is the holy [one], abides without place and is a place for the occupiers of place that are below it. And let this suffice for us, to be shown to the examiner; and to his God let him return, and let him keep lovingkindness and justice; and one must beware of error, for in these matters the unwittingness of study mounts up to [the level of] willful sin. And we trust in our Maker that one will not come, through our words, to error, God forbid. For concerning the like of this it is said (Ecclesiastes 12:9), "and he weighed and investigated and set in order many parables"; and they expounded in the Gemara (Eruvin, fol. 21), "the Torah was like a basket that has no handles"—although this is expounded in the Gemara concerning the safeguards of the Torah, nonetheless it alludes also to our intent: that the Torah was like a basket that has no handles, until [Solomon] set in order the parables, by corporealizing the fine matters, and from there the spiritual is understood. And how many matters like these are in Sefer ha-Bahir; and how many of the dicta of the Sages, of blessed memory, [serve] to corporealize the matter of the Godhead, in order to make [it] understood and to break [it for] the ear. And therefore the examiner must be cautious and guard himself.

In this chapter it would have been fitting to explain the order of the Sefirot from cause to effect, in truth, without cavil, and likewise the order of the Sefirot as to their being ten. But it is included in the coming chapters, with God's help, and from them we shall find well explained the order of the Sefirot from cause to effect without cavil and the order of the Sefirot as to their being ten; and [as for] turning the bag inside out, why should I [do so]?

After eras and eras have passed for us concerning this figure that [the previous chapters] furnished us, God illumined the eyes of our intellect in it, and God brought before us holy ones speaking, and we rejoiced in them as over all wealth, since we found in them a support and a stay. Firstly, the author of Sefer Me'irat Einayim—and this is the form of his words: This is the figure of the standing of the ten Sefirot, without essence or change, may His name be blessed and exalted; and this is what the verse said (Job 26:7), "He suspends the earth over nothingness [belimah]." And do not say it is not [so], for it is so; and when you count from your right to your left you will find ten, and you will see that Keter is a house for them all and the source of them all. It turns out that what is prior in the Emanation is great and encompasses all, and what is posterior in the Emanation is small and encompassed by all and composed of them all; and this is like the layers of an onion. And just as this lower earth is small and is in the middle of all the created beings, like a mustard-seed in a ring, and behold it is composed of all the elements and is in the middle of all, like the heart in the body of a man—so, as it were, [is] the Atarah (the diadem).

And therefore it is called the land of the living, and the heart. And look and see that the Atarah is composed of the Righteous One [Yesod] and of all the supernal ones, unified with them and encompassed by them all and receiving from them all. And so [too] the Righteous One, and so Hod, and so Netzach, and so Gevurah, and so Chesed, and so Binah—each includes all, and they are unified one in another, and each one is composed of them all, and they are all unified in it; and all is unified in Ein Sof, in the Cause of causes. Thus far [his] words. And it is a proof compelling [to] our view, letter by letter, word by word.

And further, we have a proof and a stay in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (fol. 165a), and these are [the] words: Rabbi Yossi said: There are nine firmaments, and the Shekhinah is the tenth. For should you say [that] because it is written "ten" [the Sefirot are counted] apart from the Shekhinah—if so, the Shekhinah would be the eleventh, standing over ten. Rather, certainly they are nine, and they are the nine days that are between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur, and Yom Kippur is the tenth. In like manner [is] the Mishkan, which is ten curtains. Ten firmaments [are] a secret of secrets that was not delivered except to those who know wisdom. And all is in the secrets of the holy Lamp [Botzina Kadisha], who reveals the secret of each and every firmament and those ministers who serve in each and every one. Seven firmaments are above, and seven firmaments are below, in like manner to that which is above. There are seven firmaments in which are stars and constellations to govern this world, each according to its way, as is required for it. In all of them the seventh is preeminent—except the eighth, which conducts them all and stands over them all, as it is written, "extol Him who rides upon the Aravot." Who is "He who rides upon the Aravot," and what is Aravot? Rather, this Aravot is the seventh firmament. Why is it called Aravot? Because it is composed of fire and water together, from the side of the south and from the side of the north, and it is mixed [me'orav] of the two sides. Thus far [the passage], to our purpose. And the explanation of the passage: above the [present] matter, Rabbi Chiya expounded on the explanation of the verse "And you shall make the Mishkan [of] ten curtains," etc.; and Rabbi Yossi found difficulty in the verse that said "And you shall make the Mishkan [of] ten curtains"—and it is known that the Mishkan is the Shekhinah, Malkhut. If so, how did he say that one should make ten curtains, which are the ten Sefirot, over the Mishkan, which is Malkhut? It turns out, accordingly, that the Sefirot are eleven—and this is the opposite of the truth, that they are ten and not nine, ten and not eleven, as is explained in [the] gate "Ten and Not Nine." For this [reason] he said that the ten curtains do not necessitate ten Sefirot apart from the Shekhinah; rather, "there are nine firmaments." [That is to say,] nine Sefirot alone are over the Shekhinah, and the Shekhinah is the tenth. And he adopted the wording "nine" and did not say "there are ten firmaments and the Shekhinah is one of them"—which would be more precise, [namely] that the Shekhinah too is called a firmament, as is explained from his words. The reason [is] that the place of the error and the mistake was because he said "And [you shall make] the Mishkan," which is the Shekhinah, "[of] ten curtains," as [if] it appears that ten Sefirot are over Malkhut. And to guard ourselves from this corruption [of understanding], he said, against the error, "nine firmaments," and the Shekhinah, which is the Mishkan, is the tenth to the firmaments—and that is what he said, "and the Shekhinah is the tenth." "For should you say [that] because it is written 'ten,'" etc.: that is, that should you wish to say that, from the fact that the verse said "And you shall make the Mishkan [of] ten curtains" and did not say "nine curtains," it appears that they are ten apart from the Shekhinah, God forbid—if so, you will be saying that they are eleven, and the Mishnah in Sefer Yetzirah said "ten and not eleven." And therefore he did not wish to say [otherwise], but [rather], "if so, the Shekhinah is the eleventh." And in his mentioning the words "the eleventh," who does not know the Mishnah that said "ten and not eleven," and "one who adds to ten is not of the [proper] number"? Rather, certainly they are nine, etc. And it is not Rabbi Yossi's intent to say that Yom Kippur is Malkhut and the ten days of repentance are from above downward—for it is already explained in the Zohar and the Tikkunim and in several places that Yom Kippur is in Binah, and the testimony to this [is] the five afflictions; and it is a foretaste of the World to Come, as the Sages, of blessed memory, said (Berakhot, fol. 17a), "In the World to Come there is no eating or drinking," etc. Rather, Rabbi Yossi's intent is only to tell us that the Sefirot are ten, in the likeness of those days, which are only ten. And if the Sefirot were eleven, the days would be eleven. And just as the days are nine and Yom Kippur is the tenth, so it is fitting concerning the matter of the Sefirot, for the Mishkan itself [is] the tenth. And the matter [is] that the ten days of repentance are days that are in repentance, which is Binah; and behold, the yod is repentance itself—that is to say, the supernal grade within it—and it is included in [the] ten days, which are the ten Sefirot, and it is of the [number of the] days. So [too] the matter of the Mishkan itself: it is the tenth curtain and the tenth Sefirah. And the intent of the verse in saying "And you shall make the Mishkan," etc., the intent [is] that you shall make the existence of the Mishkan such that it be composed of ten Sefirot, which are ten curtains, and the whole ten, that is the Mishkan—not that the Mishkan is one and the curtains ten by themselves, as you might have thought, for if so they would amount to eleven; rather, the Mishkan, that is the totality of the ten curtains. And that is what Rabbi Yossi said, "in like manner [is] the Mishkan, which is ten curtains"—[that] is to say, the Mishkan is the gathering of the ten curtains, which is what we say, [that] Malkhut is composed of ten, as we explained in the previous gates and shall explain in [the] gate "Essence and Governance," blessed be He. "A secret of secrets," etc.: he extolled the wisdom and its excellence. "Who reveals the secret in each and every firmament, and those ministers," etc.: the intent [is] that in each attribute [there are] several angels appointed over the matter of the action of that attribute, and the angels receive the power of the action from the supernal roots by means of ministers that draw near to their source—they are those whom we shall explain in [the] Gate of the Holy Palaces. And from those near to the roots, who sit first in the palace of the King, [there] chain down many thousands and myriads of myriads, from grade to grade and from cause to effect, until they reach this world. And this matter has been explained in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, [in] places too many to number. And these angels mentioned are called ministers to those supernal firmaments, which are the Sefirot. And that is the intent of Rabbi Yossi here, in his saying "seven firmaments are above"—the explanation [being]: seven Sefirot alone are the principal ministers for the governance of the world; and therefore the building of the world [is] seven days, with the Sabbath day, since the principal governance [is] with these seven. And just as above there are seven conductors, so in the lower firmaments the conductors of the world are seven—that is, the seven planets. And he said that above six firmaments is a seventh firmament, more excellent than the six that are below it, and it is called Aravot, from the language of "mixing" [erev], for in it two attributes are mixed—that is, its blending between judgment and lovingkindness; and Aravot is Tiferet, which mixes them. And he called it "seventh," even though it is fifth below Gedulah and Gevurah, for the reason we explained in [the] Gate of the Order of the Emanation, in chapter six. And he said that there is an eighth firmament riding over all, that is, Binah, which is the mother crouching over the young.

And behold, the explanation of the passage is comprised, and from it we have learned the matter of the Emanation—that they are in the likeness of the spheres that surround this world, this within that, like the layers of an onion; and for this reason he called them firmaments, and their governance [is] like the governance of the lower firmaments, and they are spheres encompassing all that is within them, like a mustard-seed in a ring. And blessed is God, who made His lovingkindness wondrous to us in a besieged city, and we found ourselves corroboration and a stay from the words of the Zohar—[they are] all of them according to Rashbi, as is known—and there is no doubt in this matter.

After we elaborated, in the previous chapter, on the figure of the Emanation and its standing, and established it and confirmed it and upheld it as is fitting—it is fitting to see that this figure is found to demolish the whole edifice that we built in the previous chapters concerning the matter of the figure of the Emanation, [namely] that they are three rights and three lefts and three middle [ones]. And accordingly, this is not [consonant] with its [other] figure, for they are all one within another and there is in them neither right nor left. Now, [since] this and that are the words of Rashbi, it is not fitting to say that his words contradict one another, some of them against others. And likewise the author of Sefer Me'irat Einayim, who wrote that figure that we wrote above in chapter two, and afterward wrote this figure and retracted within the span of an utterance—and he said above that one who denies the first figure is [of] a generation of perversities, etc.—and this is a great difficulty. And to resolve this matter, let us say: a question was asked among the investigators concerning the angels, which they designated by the name "separate intellects," and they said: since they are simple, spiritual, and far from all the accidents of body, if so, by what are they distinguished into the number ten? And Rambam, peace be upon him, wrote the matter of this question in the second [chapter] of Hilkhot Yesodei ha-Torah, and these are [his] words: "And by what are the forms distinguished one from another, seeing that they are not bodies?" And he answered: because they are not equal in existence, but each one of them is below the rank of its fellow, and it exists from its [fellow's] power, this above that, and all exist from the power of the Holy One, blessed be He. Thus far [his] words.

And the intent [is] that he there elaborated on the negation of body and its accidents in [the case of] the angels, and it was difficult for him: since they are far from the accidents of body, and since beings equal in existence are not distinguished one from another except by the accidents of body, and since the angels have no accidents of body—if so, by what are they distinguished, [such] that they are ten grades, as he himself counted? And he answered: because they are not equal in their existence. The explanation [is] that it is true [that] those equal in their existence are not distinguished except by the accidents of body; and the angels, which are distinguished even though they have no accidents of body—the reason is because they are not equal in their existence, but [are] effects one of another, and each one of them is below the rank of its fellow, etc. And the master Rabbi Shem Tov ben Shem Tov, in Sefer ha-Emunot, Gate 4, chapters one, two, [and] three, established with clear proofs that their view is not correct. And these are [his] words: Behold, according to their view, there is nothing between the Cause of causes and them except that this one is a cause to the effects [proceeding] from it; and we have no power to know a single thing of [any] difference between the First Cause and the last of them, etc., except [the relation] from cause to effect—that is to say, they are all unified in a complete unity, for there is among them neither conjunction nor separation, and they have no place at all, for they are not body nor a force in body, but [are] separate intellect[s]; but the cause is above what it causes and the cause is above its effect, and it turns out that the First Cause is a cause to them all, and the first effect is a cause to all the effects that are below it, and they are above the lower ones.

And further, the master refuted this view concerning the angels, because it is compelling from the words of the Sages, of blessed memory, that the angels were created on the second day or on the fifth day, according to what the Sages, of blessed memory, disputed in this (in Bereshit Rabbah, ch. 3); and he said that if the angels were [as] the unity of the [divine] Name, how is it possible to say that they were created after the creation of heaven and earth? And it is impossible, just as it is impossible to say that they preceded the First Cause.
And further, how does the language of "creation" [rightly] apply to them?

And further, he established [the point] from Parashat Vayera, from the vision of Abraham, who saw them in the likeness of men, and he established there that it cannot rightly be said that it was in a prophetic vision. Thus far his objections.

And behold, he established, on the basis of these questions, that they [the angels] are fine entities, corporealizing themselves in a fine and pure body; and for this he adduced [proofs] from the words of the Sages, of blessed memory, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Palaces, with God's help. And now we ourselves ask concerning the matter of the Sefirot, exactly like their question: since we elaborated, in the previous gates, on the matter of the Sefirot and their distancing from body and its accidents—if so, by what are they distinguished, if they are equal in their existence? And we shall answer according to their answer, that their distinction is in that they are not equal in their existence: for Keter exists from Ein Sof, and not so Chokhmah, whose existence is from Keter; and not so Binah, which exists from Chokhmah; and not so Chesed, whose existence is from Binah; and not so Gevurah, whose existence is from Chesed; and not so Tiferet, whose existence is from Gevurah; and not so Netzach, whose existence is from Tiferet; and not so Hod, whose existence is from Netzach; and not so Yesod, whose existence is from Hod; and not so Malkhut, whose existence is from Yesod. And behold, now they are distinguished one from another, in that each one is a cause to its fellow. And now, concerning the Sefirot, what Rabbi Shem Tov found difficult in the words of Rambam will not be difficult for us, because the Sefirot preceded the creation of heaven and earth and do not fall under time, but on the contrary, they are a root to time. For the six Sefirot are a root to the six days, and the seventh is the Sabbath day, as will be explained in the Gate of the Values of the Allusions, with God's help. And concerning them the Sages, of blessed memory, said (Bereshit Rabbah, ch. 3), "this teaches that an order of times existed before this." And it will also not be difficult for us [to explain] that they appeared to the prophets, for the prophets never apprehended the very Sefirot themselves at all; and even to Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, it was said (Exodus 33:23), "and you shall see My back," etc. And what we say, that the prophecy of Moses our teacher was in Tiferet and [that] of the other prophets in Malkhut—and likewise what we say, that Netzach and Hod are the two prophets of truth—the intent in all this is not that they apprehended the Sefirot literally, but [rather] that from there [is] their nourishment; but their intellection was in the palaces. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained, as we shall explain in the Gate of the Palaces, in chapter two, in the second palace, with God's help. Since his difficulties will not be difficult for us, if so, when we ask: since the Sefirot are belimah, as we explained in the previous gates, [then] by what are they distinguished?—we too shall say that they are distinguished in that the one is a cause to its fellow, as if we should mean that there is no distinction between Keter and its Emanator except that the Emanator is a cause to the emanated. And beyond this they are unified [in] the utmost union; but between Ein Sof and Keter, by reason of Keter['s] being emanated and not Emanator, and Ein Sof Emanator and not emanated, there is much distinction, as explained above in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof is the Keter and in the Gate of Self and Vessels. And this is clear, that Keter is emanated and Ein Sof the Emanator [is] not emanated. But by reason of their descent, the Sefirot do not descend from it except in the manner [of relation] that [obtains] between Emanator and emanated and that [obtains] between cause and effect; and likewise Chokhmah descends from Keter, and Binah from Chokhmah, and likewise the other Sefirot, like the descent of the effect from the cause. And the matter [is] that Malkhut apprehends Yesod, but not to the measure that it apprehends itself. And Yesod apprehends itself, and apprehends Malkhut with [a] more complete [apprehension] than Malkhut apprehends itself. And likewise it does not apprehend Hod to the measure that it apprehends itself. And Hod apprehends itself more than Yesod apprehended [it]. And likewise it apprehends Malkhut with [a] greater apprehension than Yesod apprehends [it], and how much more so Malkhut itself. And likewise Netzach—its knowledge of itself will be more elevated than Hod apprehends [it]. And likewise Yesod apprehends [it] more than Hod apprehends [it], and how much more so Yesod [apprehends] itself. And likewise it apprehends Malkhut more than Yesod apprehends [it], and how much more so Malkhut itself. And in this manner, too, the apprehension of Yesod in Hod will be more elevated than the apprehension of Malkhut in Hod; and likewise the apprehension of Hod in Netzach will be more elevated than the apprehension of Yesod [in it]; and likewise their apprehensions, one over another, will be elevated, up to the first grade.

And this matter [is] a great principle in [the realm of] existence, as we shall expand the explanation in Sefer Or Yakar, with God's help. And we know that it will be difficult in the eyes of the examiner that, accordingly, it turns out that Chokhmah is not unified with the Emanator, and likewise Binah with Keter—since that which is an effect from it, this is its cause, and the bond of the effect [is] with its cause, not with the cause of its cause, intrinsically. We shall answer to this: that it is true [that] the questioner has aimed well and is right in his ruling that they are not unified from this side; but they are unified from another side, each one in them all and all in each one, by [virtue of] the aspect of their inclusiveness from [the number] ten.

And behold, accordingly, Keter has with Gevurah ten unifications, namely: the Keter-within-Keter with the Keter-within-Gevurah, and the Chokhmah-within-Keter with the Chokhmah-within-Gevurah, and in this manner the other grades; and so for all the Sefirot. And since it has been explained that, by way of inclusiveness, the Sefirot ascend in their existences without end—as we shall explain in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter two, with God's help—therefore [the matter] will ascend in unification without end. And this is by [reference to] the [relative] measure of their unification and their bond [as] the emanated [Sefirot] themselves. But in the Emanator they are unified in two respects: the one, by [reference to] their bond with their hidden root above, as is explained in the Gate of the Tzachtzachot; and the second, in the aspect of the light of the Self that spreads within the grades, which is the Self of the Godhead, not divided into these parts except by means of the Sefirot, as explained in the Gate of Self and Vessels. And the Self that spreads is unified in its source, like the ray of the sun unified in the sun, and in the likeness of the soul unified in its powers that spread through the body. And the Sefirah itself is unified in the Self that spreads [in the] utmost union, just as the soul is unified with the body, for reasons that we shall explain in the Gate of the Soul.

And behold, after the matter of their bond and the matter of their unification and the matter of their distinction have been explained—that they are in the likeness of cause and effect, cause and what it causes—the Emanation is found [to be] a jointed lampstand, [its parts] unified and bound [in] the utmost union, bond, and longing. And concerning this matter a covenant was cut for those who occupy themselves with the wisdom of the Pardes. And this was the claim of Elisha, [namely] that through this he became Acher [the Other]. And this was the sin of Adam the First, who came to dismantle the tent and was found dismantling on the Sabbath, and therefore he was [held] liable. And one who contemplates this matter, [this] occupation, must beware lest he do according to their pattern; and therefore let the examiner occupy himself with this chapter, and in it he will find rest for his soul, and his soul will abide in well-being, and he will dwell secure with none to make him afraid.

After the matter of the bond of the Sefirot among themselves and their bond with the Emanator has been explained in the previous chapter—when the examiner contemplates it with good diligence, he will find good taste and knowledge and the compelling [force] of the matter of itself, and the truth will show its way. And he will find, accordingly, [that] the Sefirot—when we come to liken them and to depict them, by way of likeness, to the human intellect—[one] will be compelled to believe that they are one above another. For Ein Sof the Emanator is the Cause of all causes and the Source of all causes, and the first effect from it is Keter; and Keter [is] a cause and a cause to Chokhmah, by the power of the Emanator that overflows from its light upon it; and Chokhmah is a cause and a cause to Binah, by the power of the Emanator, by means of Keter, in [its] emanating the light of the Emanator by means of the first emanated [one], Keter, upon it. And so for all the rest of the Emanation: for Binah [is] a cause to Chesed, and Chesed a cause to Gevurah, and Gevurah a cause to Tiferet, and Tiferet a cause to Netzach, and Netzach a cause to Hod, and Hod a cause to Yesod, and Yesod a cause to Malkhut. Behold, they are ten grades, ordered one above another, thus: Keter, Chokhmah, Binah, Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod, Yesod, Malkhut. And of what is fitting to know [is] that, apart from this order, they have another order. And the reason for this [is] that each Sefirah has two causes: the one, its cause—that after the preceding [one] was emanated, it was emanated. The example of this [is] that even though the true cause of Netzach is Chesed, nonetheless, because of the order of its emanation, its cause is none but Tiferet, as we elaborated concerning the matter of their emanation in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, in chapter six.

And behold, they have two aspects to their cause and their source: the one, the order that we explained above, one upon another up to the ten; the second, the order of their effluence and their source, according to their division. There is [one] whose aspect is lovingkindness [Chesed], and it must incline to the line of Chesed; and there is [one] whose aspect is judgment [Din], and it must incline to the line of Din; and there is [one] whose aspect is mercy [Rachamim], and it must incline to the line of Rachamim, and it aligns itself between these two lines, toward the mean.

And behold, the matter of these their aspects is their subsistence and their effluence that is poured out upon them. And it turns out, accordingly, that they have two aspects to their causes: the first aspect, the cause of the order, as explained; the second aspect is the nourishment and the effluence and the subsistence. And even though, from the side of the aspect [pertaining] to the order of the emanation, their order [being] one above another is compelling—when we look to the side of their nourishment, which is the cause of their subsistence, they are found [to be] in another arrangement; for we see [that] Keter emanates into Chokhmah and into Binah—if so, it is compelled from this that it is the cause of both of them. And from another side it is compelled that Chokhmah is the cause of Binah and Keter the cause of Chokhmah—if so, it is compelled that [they] be ordered in the likeness of a segolta, thus:

Keter; and one channel, which indicates the preceding cause—and their order is Keter, Chokhmah, Binah. And from the side of Keter's emanating into Binah, it is necessitated that there be a channel from Keter to Binah; and the matter of the channels will be explained in a gate of its own. And from the side of Chokhmah's emanating into Chesed, and Binah into Gevurah, it is compelled that Chesed be beneath Chokhmah and Gevurah beneath Binah—which indicates that Chokhmah is the cause of Chesed and Binah the cause of Gevurah. And from the side of Tiferet's drawing sustenance from Keter and from Chesed and from Gevurah, it is compelled that it be opposite it, indicating that its cause is Keter. And from the side of its drawing sustenance from Chesed and from Gevurah, it is compelled that it be between the two of them, to indicate that it is caused by both of them. And from the side of its being sixth in the Emanation, it is compelled that it be drawn somewhat below the two of them, as we have depicted. And from the side of Netzach's being seventh in the Emanation, it is compelled that it draw sustenance from Tiferet. And from the side of its drawing sustenance from Chesed, it is compelled that it be beneath Chesed. And so Hod, in this way, [is] beneath Gevurah. And Yesod is compelled to be beneath Tiferet, for from there is its principal nourishment, and it is its cause from the side of the pouring-forth [of effluence]. And from the side of its drawing sustenance from Netzach and Hod, it is likewise compelled that it be between the two of them. And from the side of its being ninth to them all, it is compelled that it be drawn downward, to beneath them all, as we have depicted.
And Malkhut, from the side of its being tenth, below Yesod, is drawn below Yesod.

And behold, after the matter of the agreement of the figures upon one matter has been explained, it is fitting to explain this matter that is found in the Zohar many times: "ascending and descending" [salka ve-nachta].

And behold, the matter of ascent and descent indicates corporeality, and this does not properly apply at all; and with this premise all will be explained. Namely: since the matter of their being one above another does not intend the existence of place, God forbid, as we have explained, but rather the matter of rank and priority from cause to effect, as explained above at length—

behold, the matter of ascent and descent likewise will be in this way. As, for example, Malkhut: before she was driven down to the tenth grade, she was in the seventh grade, beneath Tiferet, in her rank and her subtlety, so much so that she was a cause to Netzach and Hod and Yesod. And when sin caused [it] and she was driven from her place, she descended, and her lights were coarsened and darkened, until she does not have the capacity to be a cause to Netzach and Hod; rather, on the contrary, she is their effect and needs them and receives light and effluence from them—and this is the matter of her descent. And so the matter of her ascent: that she be refined so much that she return to Tiferet, and Tiferet be her cause, and she be a cause to all that is beneath Tiferet, owing to the abundance of her brilliance and her light. And likewise, in this way, when we say that one attribute among the attributes ascends to another attribute higher than it, the intent is this matter: that because of the effluence that that higher attribute poured into the lower attribute, it was refined until it ascends from grade to grade, until it becomes a cause to the other attributes that are beneath the attribute that overflows upon it—and this is called that that attribute "ascended" to the other. And therefore it is explained in the Zohar many times, and in particular in the Commandments [Pikkudin], the commandment "to bless" (in Parashat Ekev, fol. 271a), etc., that it is impossible for any attribute to ascend to another attribute unless it first receives from it abundant effluence in its [own] place, so that, by the measure of the abundance of the effluence, so will it be raised from grade to grade. And there are times when the effluence is not so intensified, and it does not ascend as far as the attribute that overflows upon it, but to another attribute that is beneath it, and from there it receives from it—like Malkhut, who at times ascends as far as Yesod alone, to receive effluence from her husband, Tiferet; and this indicates that Malkhut was refined until she ascended from being tenth to the ninth, and was not refined so much as to be actually seventh, near to Tiferet; rather, from that grade she receives from him. And this is the matter of ascent and descent mentioned in the Zohar concerning the attributes; and this is enough of a remark on this matter. And with this the interpretation of all the matters has been explained, and [that] the figure agreed upon in the mouth of all the Kabbalists is the truest—and not that there is an actual figure there, God forbid, nor a place of their standing, nor face nor back, nor right nor left, except from the side of Din or of Rachamim, according to their nourishment, each and every one according to its pouring-forth and its nourishment. And indeed, the key to all these matters is that being a cause or an effect [and the grades' being one beneath another — from Asis Rimonim] is in the two ways explained above; and with this it is clear that sometimes this depiction will obtain and sometimes another, all according to the pouring-forth [of effluence]—though it is true that this is the customary and the constant one.

After we have already roused ourselves, as much as is needed, concerning the matter of the order of their standing in the preceding chapters, there remains an obligation upon us, in the matter of this inquiry, to save the inquirer from error. For perhaps he will be in doubt and say: since it is true that the Sefirot have a number, as explained in the preceding gates, and the number necessitated in them is ten—if so, when we come to their matter we shall say that the place of the end of Malkhut is the beginning of Yesod (that is to say, in the way of spirituality, from effect to cause), and the place of the end of Yesod is the beginning of Hod; for what is Hod is not Yesod, and what is Yesod is not Hod, and what is Hod is not Netzach—for they are distinct, [by] what [lies] between cause and effect; and behold, the effect is not the cause, and the cause is not the effect.

And behold, accordingly it turns out that, even though they are unified [in] a complete union, nonetheless they are, in this respect, distinct, as explained above. And now, behold, Keter is the effect of the Ein Sof, and the Ein Sof is its cause; if so, what is Keter is not the Ein Sof, and what is the Ein Sof is not Keter—and behold, it turns out that the Ein Sof has a limit, God forbid, [namely] what is not Keter; for the place of the end of Keter is the beginning of the Ein Sof. And on the face of it, this question is the place of the error to which a person is brought [when he comes] to contemplate this; and it is an error and a great confusion. And the laying to rest of this doubt is clear, and there is no place for this question at all. And the reason is that the power of the cause is in the effect, and the effect is not bereft of its cause. That is to say: when we say "this is Keter," we do not on that account necessitate that it is not the Ein Sof, God forbid. For on the contrary, there is no place for the effect apart from the cause; and behold, the effect draws sustenance from it, and its being is its cause—in the likeness of the soul within the body. For you cannot object that what is body is not soul, and what is soul is not body; for this claim does not properly apply, for two reasons. One: because the soul is certainly the cause of the body, and there is no body without a soul, and what is body is the soul—for the soul gives life to the body, and the body is nourished from the soul, and it is impossible to depict that the soul be annulled from a part of the body unless it return to dust. But the living body is certainly a garment to the soul; and therefore it is compelled that what is body be soul, for it is the cause of the body, and a living body cannot be brought into existence without a soul. However, our saying "a soul without a body" does apply properly, for there is indeed a place for a soul without a body, since the soul is not the effect of the body. And so are the matters with the Ein Sof and those that are its effects: for it is not possible to bring into existence an effect without a cause, and what is an effect—certainly the power of the cause is within it. However, a cause without an effect does apply properly; for the cause has an aspect in its own right, from the side of what does not need the effects, and it has an aspect that spreads forth and shines in the effects and gives life to them. And in this way we shall understand the matter of the Sefirot themselves: for on account of this reason it is compelled that the power of Keter be in Chokhmah, for it is a cause to it and it is its vitality; and so the power of Chokhmah in Binah, for the cause of Binah is Chokhmah, and it is its vitality; and so the power of Binah is in Chesed, for it is a cause to it and it is its vitality; and so the power of Chesed in Gevurah, for it is a cause to it and it is its vitality. And with this will be understood what is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (fol. 167), that the five times "water" in the Account of Creation are on the second day, in Gevurah—and since Gevurah is the power of fire, how is it possible that the power of water be in it? Rather, [it is] in this way. And so the power of Gevurah in Tiferet, for it is a cause to it and it is its vitality; and so the power of Tiferet in Netzach, for it is a cause to it and it is its vitality; and so the power of Netzach in Hod, for it is a cause to it and it is its vitality; and so the power of Hod in Yesod, for it is a cause to it and it is its vitality; and so the power of Yesod in Malkhut, for it is a cause to it and it is its vitality. And it turns out, accordingly, that Malkhut is Yesod, and Yesod is Hod, and Hod is Netzach, and Netzach is Tiferet, and Tiferet is Gevurah, and Gevurah is Gedulah, and Gedulah is Binah, and Binah is Chokhmah, and Chokhmah is Keter, and Keter is the Ein Sof. And not this alone, but [it] spreads forth in them all, so that it cannot properly be said "this is Malkhut and not the Ein Sof," God forbid; rather, Malkhut too has within it the power of the Ein Sof. And not this alone, but in this way is the vitality of the Sefirot, and the vitality of the chariots, and the vitality of the angels, and the vitality of all the work of creation, from the first point to the last. And this is "and You give life to them all" (Nehemiah 9:6), and the Sages, of blessed memory, explained: "and You bring them all into being." And so they explained "and You give life to them all"—and it is all one matter. For since He brought them into being and brought them into existence from Nothing, it is compelled that they be poured upon from Him, and that all draw their vitality from Him; and since He gives life to them, it turns out that He brings them into existence and brings them into being at every time and at every moment and at every hour.

And behold, bringing-into-being and giving-life are all one matter for them. And by this matter will be understood "and in His goodness He renews every day, continually, the work of creation"—which is the effluence that overflows to give them life and to make them stand and to set them in their [proper] character. And if, God forbid, the withdrawal of His effluence from them should arise in the mind, in a moment they would perish. And they are but renewed, in the secret of the renewal of His light; and it is the effluence of a river that does not cease but is renewed, like the waters of the river, which at every moment are renewed. And let us return to our matter: for the Ein Sof, the King of kings of kings, rules over them all; for His Self pierces and descends by way of the Sefirot and between the Sefirot, and within the chariots and between the chariots, and within the angels and between the angels, and within the spheres and between the spheres, and within the elements and between the lowly elements, and within the earth and between the earth and its offspring, and unto the last point that is in the abysses—"the whole earth is full of His glory." And this is what Rashbi intended in the Tikkunim (in the Introduction, fol. 3b), in his saying: "And the Cause over all shines in the ten Sefirot of Atzilut and in the ten of Beriah, and shines in the ten classes of angels and in the ten spheres of the firmament, and does not change in any place." Thus far [his] words.

And he was precise in his saying "and does not change," to guard lest we say that, since He spreads forth in this measure, it turns out that He changes according to the change of the garments, God forbid; for this he said "and does not change in any place." And the rest of the words of the passage will be explained in the Gate of ABYA.

And behold, when the inquirer sets his intellect upon the rightness of the concealment of the King of kings of kings, we shall set him further upon the matter of the Sefirot, of which we said above that Keter is in Chokhmah and Chokhmah in Binah, etc. There is yet [another] chosen order for them, namely: that the power of Malkhut is in Yesod, and the power of Yesod in Hod, and the power of Hod in Netzach, and the power of Netzach in Tiferet, and the power of Tiferet in Gevurah, and the power of Gevurah in Gedulah, and the power of Gedulah in Binah, and the power of Binah in Chokhmah, and the power of Chokhmah in Keter—which we cannot say [in the case of Keter, namely] that the power of Keter is in the Ein Sof. And the intent is not to say that it is not in the Ein Sof, God forbid, as will be explained in the Gate of the Tzachtzachot, with God's help; rather, in the way in which we necessitate this order in the Sefirot, we do not necessitate that the power of Keter is in the Ein Sof. And the matter is that the matter of "the Shekhinah among the lower beings is a supernal need" has already been explained, and we shall expand the explanation of it in the Gate of Essence and Governance, with God's help. And the matter is that Keter needs Chokhmah, for from the side of its shining to Chokhmah, the Ein Sof shines in it; it turns out that in this aspect Chokhmah is a cause to Keter, and the power of Chokhmah is in Keter. And in this way for all the Sefirot. And it turns out [that] the power of Malkhut is in Yesod, because [Malkhut] is its cause in the respect that Yesod needs it in order to receive from Hod, which is above it; and so the power of Yesod in Hod, because Hod needs it in order to receive from Netzach, which is above it; and so the power of Hod in Netzach, because [Netzach] needs it in order to receive from Tiferet, which is above it; and so the power of Netzach in Tiferet, because Tiferet needs it in order to receive from Gevurah, which is above it; and so the power of Tiferet in Gevurah, because Gevurah needs it in order to receive from Gedulah, which is above it; and so the power of Gevurah in Gedulah, because Gedulah needs it in order to receive from Binah, which is above it; and so the power of Gedulah in Binah, because Binah needs it in order to receive from Chokhmah, which is above it; and so the power of Binah in Chokhmah, because Chokhmah needs it in order to receive from Keter, which is above it; and so the power of Chokhmah in Keter, because Keter needs it in order to receive from the Ein Sof, which is above it. And we cannot say that the power of Keter is in the Ein Sof, for He needs nothing other than Himself, and all need Him, and He is the source of all, and all draw from Him; He is the cause of Himself, and there is no cause prior to Him, God forbid. And concerning the matter of these two inclusions in the Sefirot—which are from below upward and from above downward—[it is] explained many times in the Zohar, and in particular in Parashat Vayetze (fol. 158), on the matter of the tribes, where Rabbi Chizkiyah said: "'The mountains of spices'—who are the 'spices'? These are the six sons of Leah, who include six others; and they are twelve, and they are six, because each one is included in its fellow." Thus far [his] words.

And in the way that we have explained, it is clear—only that the inclusion is in one of two modes: either the upper ones in the lower ones, or the lower ones in the upper ones. This matter is further explained in the Zohar on the Song of Songs, on the verse "seven and seven pipes," and there he explained the inclusion from below upward, as is explained; and we shall not copy its language here, because it needs a broad explanation, and it is explained by us in its place. This matter is further explained there on the verse (Song of Songs 1:2) "Let him kiss me," etc. And with this will be understood the matter of "that the right is included in the left and the left in the right," which comes in the Zohar many times; and it is a key to several gates.
And behold, this chapter is concluded and this Gate is completed, as we were shown from Heaven; and praise [be] to God, blessed be He, who has helped us. Amen.
The Seventh Gate: The Gate of the Channels:

The intent in this Gate is to explain the matter of the channels, concerning which the commentators have agreed that they are between each and every Sefirah, [and] by means of which the Sefirot draw their effluence one from another. And so we shall explain what their matter is, and the intent in them, and their figure, and their number.
Chapter One:

Before anything [else], we say that the term "channel" [tzinor] is derived from the language of "Deep calls unto deep at the sound of Your channels [tzinorekha]" (Psalms 42:8). And the meaning of tzinor is a pipe made [as] a way by which water comes from place to place. And the Kabbalists applied this [term] to the way of the effluence that is poured from attribute to attribute. And many times the Kabbalists designated the stopping of the effluence by the expression "the breaking of the channels," and likewise "the ruin of the channels," and the like; and these things are not as their plain sense. And the matter is that every Sefirah that receives from its fellow, at the time when it wishes to receive, certainly an arousal must ascend from it to the upper one, so that by means of its arousal the upper one will be aroused and pour effluence into it; and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in many places. And the proof of the matter is from the verse (Genesis 2:6) "And a mist went up from the earth," and afterward "and watered," etc. And we have set this matter apart, to explain it with sufficient explanation in the Gate of Essence and Governance, with God's help. And since the matter is so, therefore when a Sefirah wishes to receive from the Sefirah above it, the lower attribute must shine toward it a shining face, so that by the light of its face, gazing upon the light of the [upper] Sefirah, it will arouse it, and abundant effluence will be poured into it, and its face will shine from the light of the upper Sefirah. And not from all the faces together is it aroused to receive, but particular faces opposite particular faces, according to the will of their Emanator. And as the faces opposite the faces multiply, the channels multiply, as we shall explain in the coming chapters. And the general rule is that the light that is aroused from this one to that one and from that one to this one, by means of which the effluence is poured forth, is called a channel. And the parable for this is the sight of the eye, of which most of the natural philosophers said that a subtle light goes out from the eye and strikes the thing seen, and draws in that light, and from within it apprehends the thing seen. It turns out, according to their view, that the light that is aroused from the eye to draw in the sight would be called a channel, by way of parable: for just as the channel is a passage for the water, and by means of it the water is drawn to the desired place, so the light that goes out from the eye is a channel for the sight, to draw by means of it the thing seen into the eye. And so is the matter in the Sefirot: the light that goes out from the lower one to the upper one, and from the upper one to the lower one, is designated by the name "channel," because by means of it the effluence is drawn from the upper Sefirah to the lower Sefirah. And just as, when a person hides his eyes from seeing, that channel is stopped and the eye does not draw in the sight—and this matter would be designated the breaking of the channel and its stopping—so in the matter of the Sefirot: when, through the multitude of sins, the faces turn aside, and that light is not aroused, and the Sefirah does not draw the effluence from its fellow, this is designated by the name "the breaking of the channels and their stopping." And now, with this matter, how much sweeter than honey is the parable of the stories that we set forth in the Gate of Self and Vessels, chapter four.

And behold, this matter is explained in the Zohar in many places, and in particular in Parashat Vayikra (fol. 15), and these are its words: "For it is taught: at the time when the Holy One, blessed be He, looks upon the world and sees that the deeds of human beings below are worthy, the Holy Ancient One is revealed in Zeir Anpin, and all those holy crowns gaze face to face, concealed, and all of them are blessed. Why are they blessed? Because they gaze one upon another in a straight way, not turning aside to the right or to the left. This is what is written: 'their faces behold [one another] straight.' And all of them are blessed and water one another, until all the worlds are blessed and all the worlds are found as one; and then it is called 'YHVH is one and His Name is one.' And when the sins of the world multiply, the Holy Ancient One is concealed, and they do not look face to face. And then judgments are aroused in the world, and thrones are cast down, and the Ancient of Days is concealed and is not revealed. This is what is written: 'I beheld until thrones were cast down, and the Ancient of Days sat,' etc.—for those supernal crowns that water all the others do not stand in their subsistence (in our Zohar the reading is le-okmei be-kiyyumaihu, 'to sustain [them] in their subsistence') (lo, 'not'). And who are they? The Patriarchs. 'And the Ancient of Days sat'—and was not revealed. And then the wicked of the world overturn mercy into judgment." Thus far [its] words.

From within it the matter of the channels and their rectification is explicitly explained: that it is at the time when the Emanator wills to pour forth [effluence]; and then the Holy Ancient One—which is Keter, Arikh Anpin—pours light and effluence to all the Sefirot, and the faces, which are the matter of the Sefirot, are set straight opposite them, and the effluence multiplies. However, when the faces turn aside to the right and to the left through the sin of the generation, then the channels are ruined and no effluence is poured forth. And there are many [passages] like this passage in the Zohar that reveal this matter, and there is no need to go on at length, for they are recognizable as words of truth. And now that the essence of the channel and what is meant by it have been explained, we shall further explain the number of the channels upon which the commentators have agreed. And the number of the channels: three are drawn from Keter—one to Chokhmah, and one to Binah, and one to Tiferet. A further three (a variant reads: four) are drawn from Chokhmah—one to Binah, and one to Chesed (a variant reads: and one to Gevurah), and one to Tiferet. A further two (a variant reads: three) are drawn from Binah—(a variant reads: one to Chesed), one to Gevurah, and one to Tiferet. A further three from Gedulah—one to Gevurah, one to Tiferet, one to Netzach. A further two are drawn from Gevurah—one to Tiferet, and one to Hod. A further three are drawn from Tiferet—one to Netzach, and one to Hod, and one to Yesod. A further two are drawn from Netzach—one to Hod, and one to Yesod; and, in the view of some, one to Malkhut. A further one channel is drawn from Hod to Yesod; and, in the view of some, one to Malkhut. A further one is drawn from Yesod to Malkhut. Their total is found [to be] twenty-two, as the number of "By you [bekha = 22] shall Israel bless, saying" (Genesis 48:20). And it is our wish to depict their figure here, so that understanding them will be easy in the eyes of the discerning; and this is their figure:

<small>(Says the editor: We have depicted this figure, the one agreed upon according to the view of the author—namely, four from Chokhmah and three from Binah—for so he depicted and explained in his Sefer Or Ne'erav, part six, chapter two. But in this composition he wrote the view of the commentators, and omitted two channels—one from Chokhmah to Gevurah and one from Binah to Gedulah—and added two channels, one from Netzach to Malkhut and one from Hod to Malkhut. And it is not agreed upon, as he explained in chapter three and proved from the Zohar, Parashat Noach):</small>

Since in the preceding chapter we have planted the Tree of Life for the knowledge of good, and [shown] how the deeps [call]—"deep calls unto deep at the sound of the channels"—it is fitting for the inquirer to take care in working it and in keeping it, so that we shall not need to depict it again in the coming chapters, God willing. And now we shall explain what these callings serve.
And behold, from Keter three channels go out:

The first channel [is] to Chokhmah. From this channel is the beginning of the spreading-forth of the supernal world; and they are the shining face from which the whole world was illumined by the glory of its emanation, and from there all the Sefirot were revealed. And they called its name "the Hidden Channel," since there is none more hidden than it; for the joining of Chokhmah to Keter—it is not known how and in what way—so much so that, almost, by way of that channel Chokhmah at times draws sustenance in effluence from the Ein Sof by means of Keter; for there is the hiding-place of the Cause of causes. And this matter Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 52, fol. 84), and these are his words, on the verse "YHVH Adonai is my strength [cheili]," etc.: "What is 'my strength' [cheili]? The might of all, from above. Cheili—the strength of yod [cheil yod]; and this is Abba, whose might, whose welling, is the Ein Sof (a variant reads: a welling that has no end)." Thus far [his] words.

And because the inquirer might imagine to reject this proof of ours by saying that at times Keter is called Ein Sof, we have seen fit to explain the passage, so that from within it it will be compelled that "Ein Sof" is the actual Ein Sof. And this is its explanation. "What is cheili?"—the reason being that above he explained all the rest of the verse, and now he asked of the word cheili, what its meaning is. And he answered, "the might of all, from above," and the intent is the Ein Sof. And because to the Ein Sof neither name nor word properly applies, for this he said that the meaning of cheili is from the language of power, and the intent is [that] the Ein Sof is the one who gives power and strength and might to all the Sefirot. And because this matter might already apply properly to Keter—for Keter too gives power and strength to all that is below it—therefore he lengthened his language and said "the might of all, from above," meaning: the one who gives power to all, and who is above all, there being none above Him; and that is the Ein Sof. And because, since cheili means the supernal power, I might have said that the meaning of cheili is the strength of Keter, for this he said "the strength of yod," that is, Chokhmah, which is called yod, as is known. And what he said, "and this is Abba," follows along with the rest of the explanation of the passage, and there is no [need] to go on at length. And they said that to this channel, which is from Keter to Chokhmah, the right strap of the head-tefillin alludes—that is, with the allusion of the housing [bayit] being to Keter—and from this channel went forth "living waters, flowing from Lebanon" to Chokhmah.

The second channel goes out from Keter to Binah. From this channel Binah receives effluence [of] abundant good from Keter. And they said that from it the perfumed wine spreads forth to Binah, and Binah brings it out from potential to actuality; and the perfumed wine spreads forth as far as the altar, in order to set right the dish of the pot gone rancid on account of the transgressions of Israel, and there, on account of [our] iniquities, they pour it out as a libation. For here "libation-wine" [yein nesekh] does not apply, for there is no touch of a gentile here. And they meant, in their saying "to set right the dish gone rancid," something like what was explained in the Zohar (perhaps he means Zohar, Balak, fol. 189a-b; see there) concerning Isaac: that there was mixed in his wine the wine of Esau, poured out [in order] to bless him; and Jacob brought him of the spiced wine, of the good wine, as it is written (Genesis 27:25), "and he brought him wine"—and then the power of mercy was added to him. And likewise, from this channel mercy is poured to Binah, to suckle the power of the milk to the children, so that our eyes be "washed in milk," and they grow quiet and rest, as we shall explain in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter six. And then, as they are washed in milk, the red eyes are whitened; and this is by the power of this channel, which pours the power of the milk from the supernal whiteness. And this channel is hidden. And they said that it is the left strap of the head-tefillin.

The third channel goes out from Keter to Tiferet; and from there is the way of its ascent to Keter, to receive effluence and abundant good to pour forth to the four flocks of sheep that are beneath it, and they are Netzach, Hod, Yesod, Malkhut. And by way of this channel it ascends to join Father and Mother in the secret of their union, by means of Da'at, as explained above in the Gate of Whether the Ein Sof is the Keter. And by means of the effluence poured upon it from Keter by way of this channel, it has the power to incline toward Chesed; for because it draws sustenance from Chesed and Gevurah, it stands between the two of them, even; and when effluence is poured upon it from the supernal whiteness, then it inclines toward Chesed. And this channel is called "the middle line," together with its continuation as far as Malkhut. And the commentators explained that this channel is what Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, sought to know, and He answered him, "for no man shall see Me and live" (Exodus 33:20). And these are words of [mere] prophesying, for Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, never asked about this.

A further three channels are drawn from Chokhmah. The first, to Binah: it is that by which the thirty-two paths are drawn from Chokhmah to Binah—and they are the twenty-two letters and the ten utterances, which are hidden in Chokhmah, "koach mah" (the power of "mah"), and Binah brings them out from potential to actuality; so the commentators explained. And it is possible that this is the channel by which was the spreading-forth from Chokhmah to Binah in the Sefirot themselves, at the beginning of the Emanation, as explained in the Gate of the Order of the Emanation, with God's help. And by way of this channel Chokhmah is hidden within Binah, as is explained in the Zohar in many places.

The second channel is drawn from Chokhmah to Chesed. By way of this channel the effluence of lovingkindness [chesed] is drawn to Gedulah from Chokhmah. And by way of this channel the seventy-two bridges are drawn to Chesed, as we shall explain in the Gate of Essence and Governance, chapter sixteen. And the seventy-two bridges are in Chokhmah—"koach mah"—in potential, and in Chesed in actuality. And so "Chokhmah" amounts to seventy-three, which are the seventy-two bridges with Chesed hovering over them. And likewise, by means of this channel is drawn "the good oil upon the head, running down upon the beard, the beard of Aaron," as we shall explain in the Gate of the Values of the Allusions, under the heading "oil"—that the principal [source] of the oil is from Keter, by means of Chokhmah, to the priest, the man of Chesed. And because its root is in Keter, therefore shemen ["oil"] in atbash amounts to bet-yod-tet [21], which is Ehyeh, and it is a holy Name. And likewise, by way of this channel the [effluence of] Chokhmah descends to Chesed, as they, of blessed memory, said: "One who wishes to become wise should turn south"; and through this the yod of the Name is at times designated in Chesed, as is customary in the Zohar and in the Tikkunim.

The third channel is drawn from Chokhmah to Tiferet; and this we have found only with the author of the parchment (Yeri'ah) [a particular chart of the Tree]. And possibly the reason is that Tiferet is the son of Chokhmah and Binah, and behold, it is compelled that the power of the father be in the power of the son, and likewise the power of the mother; for "there are three partners in a person." And possibly by way of this channel is the matter of "Israel arose in thought." And for this matter there is disclosure from many places in the Zohar and in the Idra, as will be explained in Sefer Or Yakar, with God's help.

A further two channels are drawn from Binah. The first, to Gevurah. And the commentators explained that it is to quiet the judgment of Gevurah and the power of the husks. And it is known that Binah pours into Gevurah in two modes. The one is judgment and might [gevurah]—for Binah is called "the worker of mighty deeds (gevurot)," and "from its side judgments are aroused," as we shall explain in the Gate of Essence and Governance. And this is specifically when it pours through this channel alone, which is from its own self. However, when it receives through the channel that it has from Keter and pours through this channel into Gevurah, then the effluence is to quiet the judgment and the might. And in this way is drawn the weakening of the husks, which are the officers of the judges, from outside; and when the judgment is annulled, their power is annulled, since they do not effect their action.
The second channel [is] from Binah to Tiferet.

Behold, this channel will be explained in the way that we explained above concerning the third channel, which is drawn from Chokhmah to Tiferet. And by way of this channel Tiferet ascends to Binah. And by way of this channel Binah established Tiferet, as in the matter of "He established the heavens by understanding" (Proverbs 3:19), as will be explained in the Gate of the Modes of Existence, and was explained in the Gate "Ten and Not Nine."

A further three channels go out from Chesed. And the first of them, to Gevurah. And likewise from Gevurah the power of the fire of Gevurah goes out to Chesed, to dry the moisture of the water of Chesed; and the power of the water of Chesed [goes out] to quench the fire of Gevurah—for so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained. And with this will be understood a matter in which one thing opposes another: that the south is hot and dry, and the north cold and moist—and it would have been fitting to be the reverse. And what is explained on this is set forth in the Gate of Essence and Governance, in chapter eleven, and in the Gate of the Values of the Allusions, in the name of Rashbi, peace be upon him. Many have explained that between [the ends of] this channel is Tiferet, which is what combines them. But by what we have explained it is better settled: that apart from Tiferet they have a channel together; and this agrees best with most of the words of the Zohar. And by means of this channel Chesed is included in Gevurah and Gevurah in Chesed, without the joining of Tiferet, as is explained in the Zohar and explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance. The second channel goes out from Chesed to Tiferet. And they said that from this channel thirty-five princes are drawn to Tiferet, and Tiferet brings them out from potential to actuality; and they are those who incline rightward, toward merit—so the commentators explained. And likewise, by means of this channel are also drawn seventy-two powers that are joined to the seventy-two Names, as is known—which are the 216 lights: seventy-two of the right, seventy-two of the left, seventy-two of the middle. And Tiferet is what brings them out from potential to actuality and mediates them toward the right. And likewise, by means of this channel is the matter of the mediation, in combination with that of Gevurah.

The third channel goes out from Gedulah to Netzach; from there is the principal nourishment of Netzach, from Chesed. And the secret [is] "pleasantness at Your right hand forever [netzach]" (Psalms 16:11). For it is the emissary of Gedulah, and the principal action of Netzach is in lovingkindness [chesed]. And just as in Chesed there are seventy-two powers for the Name of seventy-two, so there are in Netzach as well. For the three Patriarchs are the three vavs—va-yissa, va-yavo, va-yet (Exodus 14)—and likewise they are Netzach, Hod, Yesod, and in them too is the Name of seventy-two. So Rashbi explained in the Tikkunim.

A further two channels are drawn from Gevurah. The first, to Tiferet. And the commentators explained that from there are drawn thirty-five princes who incline leftward, toward the scale of guilt, and Tiferet brings them out to actuality. And likewise, from within this channel are drawn seventy-two powers that are joined to the seventy-two Names, as is known—which are the 216 lights, and seventy-two of them are of the left; and by means of this channel and that of Chesed, it is the mediator between them, as we have explained. And further, by means of the aid of these channels, of Chesed and of Gevurah, he is united with his bride, in the secret of (Song of Songs 2:6) "His left hand is under my head, and his right hand embraces me," and as we shall explain in the Gate of Essence and Governance. And we have already written a little of this in the preceding gates.

The second channel goes out from Gevurah to Hod, and by means of it is the principal nourishment of Hod from Din, as we explained above in the Gate "Ten and Not Nine." And the commentators explained that by means of this channel the negative commandments are drawn from Gevurah to Hod, and in Hod is their explication; and likewise the positive commandments from Chesed to Netzach, by means of the channel that it has from it. And it is possible that Gedulah and Gevurah are the principal powers of the positive commandments and the negative commandments, and by means of Netzach and Hod they are revealed, just as the other actions that are in Chesed and in Gevurah are revealed by their means.

A further three channels are drawn from Tiferet. The first, to Netzach; and by means of it [Netzach] draws a little sustenance from the redness of Gevurah, for the sake of the blending, as is explained at length in the Gate "Ten and Not Nine," in chapter four. And there is one who did not write this channel, nor the one going out from it to Hod. And this is a void opinion; and this [channel] is agreed upon, as we have explained.

The second channel goes out from Tiferet to Hod, to sweeten its judgment a little. And this is on account of its inclining—the whiteness toward the redness—as is explained in the said Gate and will be explained in the Gate of the Colors. And by means of the two said channels the dew pours forth and descends from the heavens, [which is] Tiferet; then they [Netzach and Hod] "grind manna for the righteous"—Yesod and Malkhut, Tzaddik and Tzedek. And it will be explained in the Gate of the Values of the Allusions, under the heading "Shechakim."

The third channel goes out from Tiferet to Yesod. And by means of it Yesod receives abundant good, to unite the groom with his bride; for by means of it her sustenance descends, and it is the best man. It turns out that this channel has two actions. The one: the sustenance that overflows to the woman by means of the intermediary, and likewise the sustenance of Yesod itself. And the second action: that it is the way of her ascent to be united with her husband, after she has been adorned "as a bride adorns herself with her jewels."

A further two channels go out from Netzach. The first, to Hod. And the commentators explained that by means of this channel they are united to ascend (to the heavens). And it is possible that by means of this channel is the grinding of the manna, in a slight evenness of blending, before its coming to Yesod. And by means of this channel, and likewise the channel that is from Chesed to Gevurah, and likewise the channel that is from Chokhmah to Binah, is the union of Tiferet and Malkhut, in the secret of their inclining to the right and to the left. For Tiferet is in Netzach and Malkhut in Hod: YHVH in Netzach, Adonai in Hod; and by means of Yesod the two of them are united together, and YAHDVNHY is made. And so they are in Chesed and Gevurah—the male to the right and the female to the left: YHVH in Chesed, Adonai in Gevurah; and the two of them are united in Tiferet. And so they are in Chokhmah and Binah—the male to the right and the female to the left: YHVH in Chokhmah, Adonai in Binah; and the two of them are united in Keter—and not actually Keter, but in the secret of Da'at, which is the union of Chokhmah and Binah.

And behold, it turns out that these three channels—that from Chokhmah to Binah, and that between Gedulah and Gevurah, and that between Netzach and Hod—are for [set] times; that is to say, for the times of the union of Tiferet with Malkhut.
And the matter of these unifications is explained in the Tikkunim [Tikkun 18, fol. 33a].

The second channel goes out from Netzach to Yesod. For by means of this channel and the one opposite it is the blending and the mediation that Yesod mediates between Netzach and Hod. And by means of these two channels is the power of the seed, and by their means it is ripened—as is known, that Yesod is the member, and Netzach and Hod are the two testicles of the male.

The third channel goes out from Netzach to Malkhut. And by means of it "a thread of lovingkindness [chesed] was drawn over Esther," and by means of it she receives effluence from Chesed before the coupling. And likewise by means of Hod—for she needs to receive effluence from two places, from the right and from the left, in the secret of (Song of Songs 2:6) "His left hand is under my head," etc. And it will be explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance, with God's help, in chapter twenty-one.

A further two channels go out from Hod. The first, to Yesod; and its rule has been explained above. And the second, to Malkhut. And the author of the parchment explained that from this channel the primordial serpent cast filth into Eve. And his words are words of dreams, like one prophesying a vain vision; for "who set a drunkard among the Nazirites?"—as we shall explain, that the husk has no entry into holiness at all, as will be explained in the Gate of the Substitutions. And what it might have been possible to say [is] that by means of this channel judgment is poured from Hod to Malkhut; but all this is without foundation [yesod], as we shall explain in the coming chapter.

And what is fitting to know [is] that what the commentators said concerning the two channels—one from Netzach to Malkhut and the second from Hod to Malkhut—is not tenable at all. For it is clear that Malkhut receives effluence only by means of Yesod, as is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Noach (fol. 59b), and these are its words: "Rabbi Elazar said: 'These' [eleh] in every place invalidates the former ones. We have learned, etc. What is written above, in the portion of Bereshit? 'And a river issues from Eden to water the garden, and from there it divides,' etc. That river that flows and issues [nagid ve-nafik] and enters the garden and waters it with the watering from above, and gives it rest [naycha], and it yields fruit and makes seeds grow—and it is then rest for all. And this is rest for the garden, and this one makes rest in it, as it is said, 'for in it He rested,' and it is written, 'and He rested on the seventh day.' And this is the secret of the matter: this one makes generations, and no other. Come and see: [in like manner] Noah below was the holy covenant, a pattern of that above, and therefore he is called 'a man of the ground.' And we have learned a secret: for Noah needed the ark [tevah], to be joined with it and to sustain the seed of all, as it is written, 'to keep seed alive.' Who is the ark? This is the Ark of the Covenant. And Noah and the ark below were thus, after the pattern of above. Of Noah, 'covenant' is written, as it is written, 'and I will establish My covenant with you,' etc. And until the covenant was established in him he did not enter the ark, as it is written, 'and I will establish My covenant with you, and you shall come into the ark.' And then the ark was the Ark of the Covenant. Ark and Noah—all after the manner of above. And because this covenant above makes generations, in like manner Noah below makes generations. On account of this it is written, 'These are the generations of Noah: Noah was a righteous man.' So it is, certainly, after the manner of above. And therefore it is written, 'and the righteous one is the foundation of the world,' and the earth is sustained upon this; for he is the pillar upon which the world stands. And who is he? This is the Righteous One [Tzaddik]. And Noah is called 'righteous' below. And the secret of all: 'Noah walked with God'—precisely; that he never separated from Him, and [so as] to be on earth after the manner of above: 'a righteous man'—the foundation of the world; 'covenant of peace'—the peace of the world; 'a man of the ground'—certainly. And therefore, 'and Noah found favor in the eyes of YHVH.'" Thus far [its] words.

What there is to be precise about in this passage is: First, his saying "that river that flows and issues"—what need is there for the word "flows" [nagid]? For his saying "issues" [nafik]—which is the language of the verse, which says "and a river issues from Eden"—suffices.

And further: he ought to have [said] "issues, and afterward flows"; for such is the way—that first it issues, and afterward it is drawn onward. And we can resolve [this by saying] that he adopted the language of the verse, "a river of fire flowed and issued from before Him" (Daniel 7:10). And nonetheless, according to our way it will be made more precise.

And further, on the verse too there is a difficulty: why did it not say "a river … issued from before Him"? Or let it say "issued and flowed"; what is "flowed and issued," not in order? Second: what he said, "and waters it with the watering from above"—certainly it is the watering from above! For such is the way of a river: it is drawn from above downward and waters the lower ones from the effluence of the upper ones. And why did he go on at length about what teaches us nothing, since it is obvious? Third: his saying "and gives it rest," etc., and afterward he said "and it is then rest for the garden," etc., according to one reading—or, according to another reading, "and it is then rest for all," etc. One must see why he did not state, in the first clause, two aspects, as he stated in the latter clause—as appears from the sense of the language, where he says "and it is then rest for the garden, and the garden is rest in it," or, according to the other reading, "and this is rest for the garden, and this one makes rest in it." But in the first clause he said only "and gives it rest," alone. Fourth: his saying "and it yields fruit and makes seeds grow" appears a needless doubling. Fifth: his saying "Who is the ark? This is the Ark of the Covenant"—why did he adopt the language "the Ark of the Covenant," and not say "Who is the ark? This is Malkhut," which would be preferable? Sixth: here it is implied that the ark by itself is the Ark of the Covenant, whereas further on he concludes that when Noah is within the ark, the two of them in union are called the Ark of the Covenant. Seventh: his saying "'a righteous man'—so it is, certainly," etc., up to "for he is the pillar upon which the world stands," etc.—it all appears a lengthening upon what was already expounded at the beginning. Eighth: his saying "And who is he? This is the Righteous One." Now with what was he occupied until now, that he asks "who is he"? Are we not dealing with the Righteous One? And to resolve all this, it seems [right] to explain that for Rabbi Elazar there was a difficulty in the verse, in its saying "These are the generations." And his difficulty was: always, "And these" adds to the former ones; "These" invalidates the former ones—and this "These," what does it invalidate? For one cannot say that it invalidates the whole work of creation, for it would not be pleasing to their Master that one say so. And he said, "We have learned, etc. What is written above, in the portion of Bereshit?"—because it was difficult for him [that] we should say that it invalidates the generations of formlessness [tohu] and void [bohu] and darkness, which are the husks. Therefore he said, "What is written above, in the portion of Bereshit?"—as one who is precise and says that it is not fitting to explain that it refers back to formlessness and void and does not refer back to the whole portion of Bereshit that adjoins it.
